words.ex: He abbreviates the word 'example' as 'ex.'.
words.ex_cn: 他把单词 'example' 缩写为 'ex.'。
words.en: To abbreviate something means to make it shorter, especially by using a particular word or phrase to represent it.

words.ex: Rabbits proliferate quickly in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在野外繁殖得很快。
words.en: If something proliferates, it increases in number or spreads quickly.

words.tr: v. 驱散；消散；浪费；挥霍
words.ex: The fog will dissipate by noon.
words.ex_cn: 雾将在中午前消散。
words.en: If something dissipates or is dissipated, it becomes less or becomes less strong until it disappears or goes away completely.

words.tr: adj. 不利的；麻烦的；异常的；意外的；棘手的
words.ex: He faced untoward remarks from his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他遭到了同学的不友好的评论。
words.en: If you say that something is untoward, you mean that it is unexpected and causes difficulties.

words.ex: The blight destroyed the potato crops.
words.ex_cn: 这种枯萎病摧毁了马铃薯作物。
words.en: A blight is something that spoils or damages something, or a disease that affects plants.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；热心的；敏锐的；
words.ex: He is keen to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望学习英语。
words.en: If you are keen on doing something, you very much want to do it. If you are keen that something should happen, you very much want it to happen.

words.ex: His keenness to learn made him study every day.
words.ex_cn: 他学习的热忱让他每天都在学习。
words.en: The quality of being eager or enthusiastic, or the ability to perceive or understand things quickly and clearly.

words.ex: He showed xenophobia toward people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人表现出恐外心理。
words.en: Xenophobia is a strong feeling of dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.ex: He is xenophobic and dislikes foreigners.
words.ex_cn: 他有排外心理，不喜欢外国人。
words.en: If you describe someone as xenophobic, you disapprove of them because they show strong dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.tr: n. 渎职；不法行为；不正当
words.ex: The mayor was fired for malfeasance.
words.ex_cn: 市长因渎职被解雇了。
words.en: Malfeasance is the act of committing an illegal or wrongful act, especially by a public official.

words.tr: adj. 好战凶猛的；寻衅的；言词刻毒的
words.ex: He gave a truculent reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了好斗的答复。
words.en: If you say that someone is truculent, you mean that they are bad-tempered and aggressive.

words.ex: The children laughed with mirth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们带着欢乐大笑。
words.en: Mirth is amusement which you express by laughing.

words.ex: She had a mirthful laugh that could light up the room.
words.ex_cn: 她那愉快的笑声能让整个房间充满欢乐。
words.en: full of mirth; merry or amusing

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.ex: The child was compliant and followed all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子很顺从，遵守了所有规则。
words.en: If someone or something is compliant, they act in accordance with rules, standards, or laws.

words.ex: The judge will uphold the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官将维护法律。
words.en: If you uphold something such as a law, a principle, or a decision, you support and maintain it.

words.ex: The farm has a surplus of apples this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年农场苹果过剩。
words.en: A surplus is an amount of something that is extra or more than what is needed.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.tr: adj. 无可争辩的；攻不破的；不容置疑的
words.ex: His alibi is unassailable.
words.ex_cn: 他的不在场证明是无可置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something such as a person's reputation or an argument as unassailable, you mean that it cannot be criticized or attacked because it is completely right or true.

words.ex: The movie had a banal plot that everyone had seen before.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的剧情平庸得让人看过了无数次。
words.en: If you describe something as banal, you do not like it because you think that it is so ordinary that it is not at all effective or interesting.

words.ex: The movie was full of banality and had no original ideas.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影充满了陈词滥调，没有任何新意。
words.en: The quality of being banal; unoriginality.

words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.ex: It is customary to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是习惯做法。
words.en: Something that is customary is normal because it is the way something is usually done.

words.ex: The judge enjoin him from selling the house.
words.ex_cn: 法官禁止他出售这所房子。
words.en: If a judge enjoins someone from doing something, they order them not to do it. If a judge enjoins an action, they order people not to do it.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.ex: The stridency of the alarm clock was unbearable.
words.ex_cn: 闹钟的尖锐声音让人难以忍受。
words.en: The quality of being loud, harsh, and unpleasantly sharp in sound or manner.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

words.ex: His voraciousness for money led him to cheat others.
words.ex_cn: 他对金钱的贪婪使他欺骗了他人。

words.ex: The artist's work showed no preciosity, only simple beauty.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家的作品没有前性，只有简单的美。

words.tr: v. 使负罪；指控…有罪；牵连
words.ex: He did not want to incriminate his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让他的朋友涉罪。
words.en: If something incriminates someone, it suggests that they are guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.

words.ex: He denied the incrimination of his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了对朋友的指控。
words.en: The act of making someone appear guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.

words.ex: They shouted recrimination at each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此大声指责。
words.en: Recrimination is the act of accusing someone who has accused you of something.

words.tr: adj. 倾向性的；有偏见的；有争议的
words.ex: The media's tendentious reporting often misrepresents the truth.
words.ex_cn: 媒体的带有倾向性的报道常常歪曲事实。
words.en: If something is tendentious, it expresses a particular opinion or point of view very strongly, especially one that many people disagree with.

words.tr: n. 有偏见的倾向；带有特定意图的倾向
words.ex: His tendentiousness made the report unfair.
words.ex_cn: 他的有偏见的倾向使这份报告变得不公平。

words.ex: The rain offset the heat yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的雨抵消了炎热。
words.en: If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；令人不愉快的
words.ex: The noisome smell made everyone leave the room.
words.ex_cn: 那股难闻的气味让所有人都离开了房间。
words.en: If you describe something as noisome, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, especially because it has a very strong or bad smell.

words.ex: The herald announced the king's arrival.
words.ex_cn: 传令官宣布了国王的到来。
words.en: A herald is someone who carries or proclaims important news; a forerunner or harbinger.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；无能的；笨拙的
words.ex: His inept reply made the situation worse.
words.ex_cn: 他不适当的回答让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you say that someone is inept, you are criticizing them because they do something with a complete lack of skill.

words.ex: His ineptness in handling the situation made things worse.
words.ex_cn: 他处理这种情况的笨拙使事情变得更糟。
words.en: The quality or state of being inept; lack of skill or competence.

words.tr: n. 不合适；不擅长；笨拙；无能
words.ex: His ineptitude made him unsuitable for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他的不合适让他不适合这份工作。
words.en: Lack of skill or ability; incompetence.

words.tr: adj. 推测的；推理的；思索的；投机的
words.ex: He made a speculative guess about the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他对天气做了一个推测性的猜测。
words.en: Based on conjecture rather than knowledge; involving a high risk of loss.

words.ex: Babies have an innate ability to cry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿生来就有哭泣的能力。
words.en: An innate quality or ability is one that you were born with, not one you have learned.

words.ex: She is innately talented in music.
words.ex_cn: 她天生具有音乐才华。
words.en: In a way that exists from birth; naturally.

words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

words.tr: n. 迂腐之人；书呆子；学究
words.ex: He is a pedant who corrects every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑剔的书呆子，会纠正每一个小错误。
words.en: A pedant is a person who is excessively concerned with minor details and rules or with displaying academic learning.

words.ex: He gave a pedantic answer about grammar rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对语法规则给出了一个迂腐的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as pedantic, you mean that they are too concerned with unimportant details or traditional rules, especially in connection with academic subjects.

words.tr: n. 迂腐；拘泥于形式；卖弄学问
words.ex: He corrects every small mistake, showing too much pedantry.
words.ex_cn: 他纠正每一个小错误，表现出太多的死抠细节。
words.en: Pedantry is behavior that is too concerned with formal rules and small details, especially in teaching or learning.

words.ex: The country seeks hegemony over its neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家试图对邻国实现霸权。
words.en: Hegemony refers to the dominance or leadership of one group or state over others, especially in a political or cultural context.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.ex: The ubiquity of smartphones makes life easier.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的普遍存在让生活更轻松。
words.en: The state or capacity of being everywhere, especially at the same time; omnipresence.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺；抢劫；掠夺物
v. 抢劫；掠夺
words.ex: The soldiers committed pillage after winning the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在赢得战斗后进行了掠夺。
words.en: If a group of people pillage a place, they steal a lot of things from it and often cause a lot of damage, especially in a war.

words.ex: The electorate voted for a new leader.
words.ex_cn: 选民投票选出了新领导人。
words.en: The electorate refers to all the people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election.

words.ex: He is diffident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很腼腆。
words.en: If you are diffident, you are rather shy and do not enjoy talking about yourself or being noticed by other people.

words.tr: n. 意识形态；思想体系；
words.ex: His ideology is based on equality and justice.
words.ex_cn: 他的意识形态基于平等与正义。
words.en: An ideology is a set of beliefs, especially one held by a particular group, that influences the way people think and behave.

words.tr: n. 理论家；空想家；意识形态的拥护者
words.ex: He was an influential ideologue in the field of political science.
words.ex_cn: 他是政治科学领域有影响力的理论家。
words.en: An ideologue is someone who believes very strongly in particular principles and tries to follow them in their political or social activities.

words.tr: adj. 即席的；临时的；无准备的；不用讲稿的
words.ex: He gave an extemporaneous speech at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上做了一次即兴演讲。
words.en: spoken or done without preparation

words.tr: adj. 即兴的；临时的；无准备的
words.ex: He gave an extempore speech at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上发表了即兴演讲。
words.en: spoken or done without preparation; impromptu.

words.tr: v. 即兴而作；即席演说；当场表演
words.ex: She extemporized a speech on the spot.
words.ex_cn: 她当场即兴演讲。
words.en: To extemporize means to compose, perform, or produce something such as a speech or a piece of music on the spur of the moment, without preparation.

words.ex: The dark clouds foreshadow a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something foreshadows an event or situation, it suggests that it will happen.

words.ex: He faced vituperation after lying to the team.
words.ex_cn: 他向团队撒谎后遭到了严厉责骂。
words.en: Vituperation is the act of using harsh, abusive language to criticize or blame someone.

words.ex: He vituperates his boss for unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不公平的待遇而痛骂他的老板。
words.en: To criticize or blame someone harshly and angrily.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；笨重的；沉闷的
words.ex: He carried a ponderous box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他搬着一个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: Something that is ponderous is very heavy or is very slow and clumsy because of its weight or size.

words.ex: The ponderousness of the old chest made it hard to move.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧箱子的沉重让它难以搬动。

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.ex: The extraneous noise made it hard to concentrate.
words.ex_cn: 那些无关的噪音让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: Something that is extraneous is not relevant or essential to the subject you are dealing with.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.ex: He avoided partisanship in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中避免了党派偏见。
words.en: The state or quality of being partisan, especially in the sense of strong, sometimes blind, allegiance to a particular party, faction, cause, or person.

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.tr: adj. 上下文的；前后关系的；
words.ex: The meaning of the word depends on its contextual use.
words.ex_cn: 这个词的含义取决于它的上下文用法。
words.en: relating to or depending on the context of something

words.tr: v. 把…置于背景中考虑
words.ex: It is important to contextualize historical events to understand their true significance.
words.ex_cn: 将历史事件置于上下文中理解，以了解其真正的意义，这一点非常重要。
words.en: To contextualize something means to consider it in relation to the situation in which it happens or exists.

words.tr: adj. 令人不快的；令人反感的；讨厌的
words.ex: The movie contains objectionable content.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含令人反感的内容。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as objectionable, you consider them to be extremely offensive and unacceptable.

words.ex: He raised an objection to the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了反对。
words.en: An objection is an expression or feeling of disapproval or opposition; a reason for disagreeing.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.ex: The movie ended with suspense, and no one knew what happened next.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以悬念结束，没人知道接下来发生了什么。
words.en: Suspense is a state of excitement or anxiety about something that is going to happen very soon, especially something that could be either good or bad.

words.ex: He is phlegmatic even when things go wrong.
words.ex_cn: 即使事情出错，他依然冷静。
words.en: A phlegmatic person does not usually get emotional or excited about things.

words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.tr: adj. 教育性的；有启发的；有益的
words.ex: The movie is instructive for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对孩子们很有教育意义。
words.en: Providing useful or interesting information or knowledge.

words.tr: v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃
words.ex: The fresh air invigorates me every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早晨的新鲜空气让我精神焕发。
words.en: If something invigorates you, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.tr: n. 振奋；恢复活力；增强
words.ex: The fresh air gave him invigoration.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜空气给了他活力。
words.en: The process of making something or someone feel more energetic or lively.

words.ex: The drawer was a hodgepodge of old keys, buttons, and papers.
words.ex_cn: 抽屉里堆满了旧钥匙、纽扣和纸张的混杂物。
words.en: A hodgepodge is a confused mixture of different things.

words.ex: The new law impinges on people's privacy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律侵犯了人们的隐私。
words.en: To impinge means to have an effect or influence, especially a negative one, on someone or something.

words.ex: The diminution of water in the lake is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 湖中水量的减少是显而易见的。
words.en: A diminution of something is its reduction in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: There were no reperscussion after he spoke up.
words.ex_cn: 他发言后没有任何后果。

words.ex: He faced opprobrium for lying to the public.
words.ex_cn: 他因对公众撒谎而遭到谴责。
words.en: Opprobrium is harsh criticism or censure; public disgrace arising from shameful conduct.

words.tr: adj. 侮辱的；辱骂的；鄙俗的
words.ex: He shouted opprobrious words at the driver.
words.ex_cn: 他向司机喊出辱骂的话。
words.en: Expressing scorn or criticism; conveying disgrace or shame.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.tr: adj. 不吉利的；不顺遂的
words.ex: The weather was unpropitious for the outdoor event.
words.ex_cn: 天气对户外活动不利。
words.en: If you describe something as unpropitious, you mean that it is likely to lead to failure or be unfavorable.

words.ex: He spoke with animus against his rival.
words.ex_cn: 他带着敌意谈论他的对手。
words.en: A feeling of strong dislike or hatred.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: The baby eats navete with bread.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃萝卜配面包。
words.en: The quality or state of being naive; lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment.

words.ex: He acted as an intermediary between the two sides.
words.ex_cn: 他充当了双方之间的中间人。
words.en: An intermediary is a person who acts as a link between people or groups in order to try to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.tr: adj. 沉思的；愁眉苦脸的
words.ex: He sat pensive by the window.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边，若有所思。
words.en: Deeply or seriously thoughtful; reflective.

words.ex: He sat in pensiveness, staring at the window.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在那里沉思，凝视着窗户。
words.en: The state of being deep in thought, often with some sadness.

words.tr: adj. 猥亵的；淫秽的；诲淫的；好色的
words.ex: The novel was criticized for its salacious content.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说因其淫秽内容而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something such as a book or joke as salacious, you think that it deals with sexual matters in an unnecessarily detailed way.

words.ex: The movie was criticized for its salaciousness.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因其淫秽内容而受到批评。

words.ex: He gave a paltry amount of money to charity.
words.ex_cn: 他捐给慈善机构的钱微不足道。
words.en: If you describe an amount of money as paltry, you mean that it is very small.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.ex: He digresses when he talks about his vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他谈论假期时会跑题。
words.en: If you digress, you move away from the subject you are talking or writing about and talk or write about something different for a while.

words.ex: He made a digression to tell a funny story.
words.ex_cn: 他岔开话题讲了个有趣的故事。
words.en: A digression is a temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.

words.tr: adj. 离题的；不着边际的
words.ex: His speech was digressive and hard to follow.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲离题了，很难理解。
words.en: If you describe something such as a speech or piece of writing as digressive, you mean that it departs from the main subject or topic at hand.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.ex: The factory galvanize iron sheets to prevent rust.
words.ex_cn: 工厂对铁片进行镀锌以防止生锈。
words.en: To galvanize someone means to cause them to take action, for example by making them feel very excited, afraid, or angry.

words.ex: It seems counterintuitive, but less sleep can make you tired.
words.ex_cn: 这看起来违反直觉，但睡得少会让你更累。
words.en: Counterintuitive means contrary to what one would intuitively expect.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；苛性的；尖酸刻薄的
n. 腐蚀剂
words.ex: The caustic liquid burned through the metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种腐蚀性的液体腐蚀了金属。
words.en: A caustic substance is able to burn or destroy organic tissue by chemical action. Caustic remarks are extremely critical, sarcastic, or bitter.

words.ex: She commented caustically on his lack of manners.
words.ex_cn: 她刻薄地评论了他缺乏礼貌。
words.en: In a manner that is sarcastic or severely critical.

words.ex: The evidence helps to exculpate him.
words.ex_cn: 这些证据有助于为他开脱。
words.en: To remove blame from someone; to declare or prove someone not guilty of wrongdoing.

words.ex: The letter was an exculpation for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 这封信是对他的错误的开脱。
words.en: The act of clearing someone from blame or guilt.

words.tr: adj. 辩解的；开脱罪责的
words.ex: The lawyer presented exculpatory evidence that proved his client's innocence.
words.ex_cn: 律师提出了证明他的当事人无罪的辩解证据。
words.en: Adj. Providing evidence which serves to exonerate someone from blame or fault.

words.ex: He is culpable for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他对这起事故负有责任。
words.en: If someone is culpable, they are responsible for something wrong or bad that has happened.

words.ex: The court found him not guilty, but acknowledged his culpability in the incident.
words.ex_cn: 法庭判他无罪，但承认他在事件中的过失。
words.en: The state of being responsible for a fault or wrong; blame.

words.ex: The police caught the culprit who stole the bike.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了偷自行车的罪犯。
words.en: A culprit is someone who has done something wrong or illegal.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.ex: The precociousness of the child was evident in her ability to read at an early age.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子早熟的迹象在她很小就能阅读中显而易见。
words.en: Precociousness is the quality of a child showing mature characteristics at an unusually early age.

words.ex: The child's precocity in mathematics was remarkable.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在数学方面的早熟令人瞩目。
words.en: If you refer to someone's precocity, you mean that they show ability or intelligence at an earlier age than is usual.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
words.ex: The outcome was ineluctable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不可避免的。
words.en: Something that is ineluctable cannot be avoided or escaped from.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.ex: The problem has good tractability for solving.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题具有良好的可解性。
words.en: The quality of being easily managed, controlled, or persuaded.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.ex: The intractability of the problem surprised the scientists.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的难以解决让科学家们感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being difficult to control or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 依照环境的；间接的；详细的
words.ex: He gave a circumstantial explanation based on the situation.
words.ex_cn: 他根据情况给出了一个依照环境的解释。
words.en: Circumstantial evidence is evidence that suggests something by implication rather than direct proof.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.ex: His callousness toward the suffering of others was appalling.
words.ex_cn: 他对他人痛苦的无情态度令人震惊。
words.en: Callousness is the state of being insensitive and indifferent to the suffering of others.

words.ex: It was fortuitous that he found his keys just before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他在出发前刚好找到钥匙，真是幸运。
words.en: If you describe something as fortuitous, you mean that it happens by chance rather than by anyone's planning or intention.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.tr: adj. 不能渗透的；不透水的
words.ex: The raincoat is impermeable and keeps you dry.
words.ex_cn: 这件雨衣不透水，能让你保持干燥。
words.en: An impermeable material does not allow liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.tr: n. 不能透过的性质；不渗透性
words.ex: The impermeability of the fabric ensures that water cannot pass through.
words.ex_cn: 这种织物的不渗透性确保了水不能通过。
words.en: The quality or state of being impermeable; the inability of a substance to allow fluids or gases to pass through it.

words.ex: His ulterior motive was to get money.
words.ex_cn: 他别有用心，目的是弄到钱。
words.en: If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.

words.tr:
n. 怨恨；积怨；嫌隙
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜
words.ex: He holds a grudge against his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他对他哥哥心怀怨恨。
words.en: A grudge is a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury.

words.ex: He grudgingly agreed to help.
words.ex_cn: 他勉强同意帮忙。
words.en: If you do something grudgingly, you do it unwillingly, often because you feel that you have to do it.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.ex: The obsolescence of fax machines is due to email.
words.ex_cn: 传真机的过时是因为电子邮件。
words.en: Obsolescence is the state of being which occurs when an object, service, or practice is no longer wanted even though it may still be in good working order.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.tr: adj. 有益健康的；环境宜人的
words.ex: The air in the mountains is salubrious.
words.ex_cn: 山里的空气有益健康。
words.en: A salubrious place is pleasant, healthy, and good for you.

words.tr: n. 健康的；有益健康的性质
words.ex: The salubriousness of the mountain air helped him recover.
words.ex_cn: 山里健康的空气帮助他康复了。

words.tr: adj. 有害的；不利健康的
words.ex: The insalubrious conditions of the factory were causing many workers to fall ill.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的不卫生条件导致许多工人患病。
words.en: If you describe something as insalubrious, you mean that it is unhealthy, unwholesome, or harmful to one's health, often because of poor conditions or a bad environment.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: It is a hypothetical situation.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个假设的情况。
words.en: A hypothetical situation, idea, or explanation is based on possible ideas or situations rather than actual ones.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.ex: The precariousness of the bridge made everyone nervous.
words.ex_cn: 桥梁的不稳定性让每个人都感到紧张。
words.en: The state of being uncertain or unstable; dependent on chance.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: The deterioration of the road made driving dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 道路的恶化使驾驶变得危险。
words.en: The process of becoming progressively worse.

words.ex: They lionize the famous singer everywhere she goes.
words.ex_cn: 无论她去哪里，人们都把她当作名人追捧。
words.en: To treat someone as a celebrity or hero.

words.tr: n. 将某人奉为英雄；偶像化
words.ex: The media gave him lionization after he saved the children.
words.ex_cn: 媒体在他救了孩子们后将他奉为英雄。

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: He read an elegy for his dead dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为他去世的狗朗读了一首挽歌。
words.en: An elegy is a sad poem, often about someone who has died.

words.tr: adj. 挽歌体的；哀悼的；悲伤的
words.ex: The poem has an elegiac tone, reflecting on loss and sorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有一种挽歌的基调，反映了失落和悲伤。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of an elegy or something that expresses sorrow for something now past.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.tr: n. 隐居者；遁世者；隐士
words.ex: He lives as a recluse in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他住在树林里，过着隐居的生活。
words.en: A recluse is a person who lives alone and avoids other people.

words.ex: He wavers when choosing between two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在两个工作之间摇摆不定。
words.en: If you waver, you cannot decide about something or you are uncertain about what you should do.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: The movie has verisimilitude because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有逼真性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: the quality of seeming to be true or real

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.tr: adj. 沉闷乏味的；忧郁的；凄凉的
words.ex: The weather was dreary and rainy all day.
words.ex_cn: 天气一整天都阴沉沉的，还下着雨。
words.en: If you describe something as dreary, you mean that it is dull, lifeless, or depressing.

words.tr: adj. 无知的；缺乏知识的
words.ex: He was ignorant of the basic rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对基本规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as ignorant, you mean that they do not know things they should know. If someone is ignorant of a fact, they do not know it.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.ex: He contravenes the school rules by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: To contravene a law or rule means to do something that is forbidden by it.

words.tr: adj. 不妥协的；不让步的
words.ex: He is intransigent about his opinions.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的观点毫不让步。
words.en: If you describe someone as intransigent, you mean that they refuse to behave differently or to change their attitude to something.

words.ex: This is a commonplace event in big cities.
words.ex_cn: 这在大城市里是件普通的事。
words.en: Something that is commonplace is ordinary and not very interesting.

words.tr: n. 号角齐鸣（欢迎仪式等上奏的响亮短曲）
words.ex: The parade started with a lot of fanfare.
words.ex_cn: 游行以盛大的场面开始。
words.en: A fanfare is a short, showy piece of music played on trumpets or other brass instruments, often to announce something important.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.ex: He garnered food for the winter.
words.ex_cn: 他贮藏了过冬的食物。
words.en: To gather or collect something, especially information or support.

words.tr:
n. 平方；广场；正方形；四方形；
adj. 正方形的；四方形的；平方的；成直角的；
v. 与...一致；
adv. 成直角地；
words.ex: The area of the room is 16 square.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的面积是16平方米。
words.en: A square is a shape with four sides of equal length and four angles of 90 degrees. It can also refer to an open area in a town, often used for public events, or to the result of multiplying a number by itself.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.ex: He wore gold chains as a show of ostentation.
words.ex_cn: 他戴金链子是为了炫耀。
words.en: Ostentation is the act of showing off your wealth, possessions, or abilities in a way that is meant to impress others.

words.ex: He tried to disabuse her of the idea that money solves everything.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让她明白，钱并不能解决所有问题。
words.en: If you disabuse someone of something, you tell them or persuade them that what they believe is in fact not true.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.ex: The king decided to abdicate in favor of his son.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定退位，让位给他的儿子。
words.en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

words.ex: He ignored the frivolous complaint and focused on the real issue.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个无关紧要的投诉，专注于真正的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as frivolous, you mean they behave in a silly or light-hearted way, rather than being serious and sensible.

words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.ex: His hubris made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, often leading to downfall or failure.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.ex: The speech was a panegyric to the retiring chairman.
words.ex_cn: 这场演讲是对即将退休的主席的赞颂。
words.en: A panegyric is a formal public speech, or written verse, delivered in high praise of a person or thing, a eulogy.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.tr:
v. 使波动；使起伏
adj. 波动的；起伏的
words.ex: The hills undulate gently in the distance.
words.ex_cn: 远处的山丘轻轻起伏。
words.en: To move or cause to move in a smooth, wavelike motion.

words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.tr: n. 免于惩罚；不受惩处
words.ex: He stole the money and got away with it in impunity.
words.ex_cn: 他偷了钱，却逍遥法外。
words.en: If someone does something with impunity, they do it without fear of being punished for it.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.tr: v. 使巴尔干化；使分裂成小而敌对的单位
words.ex: The country began to balkanize after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争结束后，这个国家开始分裂。
words.en: To divide a region or group into smaller, often hostile, factions.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

words.tr: n. 意外之财；意外的收获；风吹落的果子
words.ex: He got a windfall from his uncle's inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他从叔叔的遗产中获得了一笔意外之财。
words.en: A windfall is an unexpected gain, piece of good fortune, or financial benefit.

words.ex: The city plan will revitalize the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市计划将使老城区复兴。
words.en: To revitalize something means to give it new life or energy.

words.ex: The church has a byzantine dome with gold mosaics.
words.ex_cn: 这座教堂有一个拜占庭风格的穹顶，饰有金色马赛克。
words.en: If you describe a system or process as byzantine, you are criticizing it because it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 拒不服从的；藐视法庭的
words.ex: He was contumacious and refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他桀骜不驯，拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If someone is contumacious, they are stubbornly or willfully disobedient to authority.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.tr:
v. 同意；赞成
n. 同意；赞成
words.ex: He gave his assent to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了这个计划。
words.en: If you assent to something, you agree to it or agree with it.

words.tr: adj. 不祥的; 不幸的; 凶兆的; 倒霉的
words.ex: It was an inauspicious day for the picnic because it started to rain.
words.ex_cn: 因为开始下雨，那天野餐并不顺利。
words.en: If you describe something as inauspicious, you mean it suggests that what is going to happen will not be successful or favorable.

words.tr:
n. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
v. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
words.ex: He felt an affront when they laughed at his idea.
words.ex_cn: 当他们嘲笑他的想法时，他感到受到了冒犯。
words.en: If something is an affront to you, it is an action or remark that insults or offends you.

words.tr:
n. 小河；溪
v. （不）忍受；（不）容忍
words.ex: The child jumps over the brook.
words.ex_cn: 孩子跳过小溪。
words.en: A small stream; to tolerate or allow something.

words.ex: He gave a justification for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他为迟到提供了一个正当的理由。
words.en: A justification for something is an acceptable reason or explanation for it.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支架；牙箍
v. 支撑；绷紧；紧靠；准备好
words.ex: The old bookshelf needs a brace to stay steady.
words.ex_cn: 旧书架需要一个支撑物来保持稳定。
words.en: To brace oneself means to prepare oneself for something difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr:
n. 斯多葛派人；坚忍克己之人；
adj. 斯多葛派的；坚忍克己的；
words.ex: He is a stoic who never shows his emotions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个从不流露情感的斯多葛派人。
words.en: Someone who is stoic does not show their feelings or complain when bad things happen to them.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adj. 暗示的；影射的；性暗示的
words.ex: His look was suggestive of sadness.
words.ex_cn: 他的眼神暗示着悲伤。
words.en: Something that is suggestive of something else is likely to make you think about or remember it.

words.ex: The issue polarized the community into two opposing groups.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题使社区分裂成了两个对立的群体。
words.en: To polarize means to cause something, especially a group or an issue, to divide into two sharply contrasting groups or sets of opinions or beliefs.

words.tr: adj. 教诲的；说教的；好教训人的
words.ex: The teacher gave a didactic speech to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 老师发表了一篇富有教育意义的演讲来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Something that is didactic is intended to teach people something, especially a moral lesson.

words.ex: There was a resurgence of interest in classical music last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年古典音乐的兴趣再次兴起。
words.en: A resurgence is a process in which something becomes active or popular again after a period of inactivity or unpopularity.

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.ex: He showed great temerity by challenging the expert without any preparation.
words.ex_cn: 他没有做任何准备就挑战专家，显得非常鲁莽。
words.en: If you say that someone has the temerity to do something, you are annoyed about something they have done which you think took a lot of nerve.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.tr: v. 使变质；损害；使失效
words.ex: The poison vitiated the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒物使水源变质。
words.en: To vitiate something means to impair or reduce the quality, value, or effectiveness of it.

words.tr: n. 反复无常；任性；怪想
words.ex: Her decision to quit the job was a sudden caprice.
words.ex_cn: 她决定辞职是突如其来的任性之举。
words.en: A sudden and unaccountable change of mood or behavior.

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.ex: Finding my lost keys while walking in the park was pure serendipity.
words.ex_cn: 在公园散步时偶然找到了丢失的钥匙，这真是易遇奇缘的运气。
words.en: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.

words.tr:
n. 大惊小怪者；危言耸听者
adj. 轻事重报的；危言耸听的
words.ex: He is an alarmist who always says the sky will fall.
words.ex_cn: 他是个悲观者，总是说天要塌了。
words.en: An alarmist is someone who exaggerates a danger and so causes needless worry or panic.

words.ex: The treaty will demarcate the new borders between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 条约将划定两国之间的新边界。
words.en: To set the boundaries or limits of something.

words.ex: The attrition between the two rocks caused sparks.
words.ex_cn: 两块岩石之间的摩擦产生了火花。
words.en: Attrition refers to the process of reducing something's strength or effectiveness through sustained attack or pressure, or the gradual reduction in the number of employees in an organization by retirement, resignation, or death.

words.tr:
v. 包括；遮盖；报道；
n. 遮盖物；庇护所；封面；
words.ex: The book covers basic math and science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包括基础数学和科学。
words.en: If something covers something else, it has been placed over or upon it, usually in order to protect it or hide it.

words.ex: The floor is slippery after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后地板很滑。
words.en: Something that is slippery is smooth, wet, or oily and is therefore difficult to walk on or to hold.

words.ex: The provenance of this ancient vase is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个古花瓶的起源未知。
words.en: The place of origin or earliest known history of something.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: The demise of the old king shocked the nation.
words.ex_cn: 老国王的去世震惊了全国。
words.en: The demise of something or someone is their end or death.

words.tr:
n. 化合物；
adj. 复合的；混合的；
words.ex: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水是由氢和氧组成的化合物。
words.en: A compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.ex: They have an intimate friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着亲密的友谊。
words.en: having a close, friendly, or personal relationship with someone; private and personal

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.tr: adj. 未受（或不容）侵犯的；未受（或不容）亵渎的
words.ex: The sacred site remains inviolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个神圣的遗址仍然不受侵犯。
words.en: If something is inviolate, it has not been or cannot be disturbed, harmed, or profaned.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的；可靠的
words.ex: His unimpeachable honesty earned everyone's trust.
words.ex_cn: 他无可挑剔的诚实赢得了每个人的信任。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimpeachable, you mean that they are completely honest and reliable.

words.ex: The court decided to expunge his record.
words.ex_cn: 法院决定删除他的记录。
words.en: If you expunge something, you get rid of it completely, because it causes problems or bad feelings.

words.tr: adj. 谦恭有礼的；和蔼可亲的
words.ex: He is an affable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is affable is pleasant and friendly.

words.ex: The pendulum oscillate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆缓慢地摆动。
words.en: If an object oscillates, it moves repeatedly from one position to another and back again, or if a figure or value oscillates, it keeps moving up and down.

words.tr: v. 使根深蒂固；使处于牢固地位；用壕沟围住
words.ex: The habit entrenches itself over time.
words.ex_cn: 这个习惯随着时间的推移变得根深蒂固。
words.en: To establish something very firmly so that it is very difficult to change.

words.ex: The roof has a sharp slant.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶有一个陡峭的倾斜。
words.en: If something slants or if you slant it, it is at an angle rather than being straight up and down or straight from side to side.

words.ex: The old system is cumbersome and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧系统复杂而低效。
words.en: Something that is cumbersome is large and heavy and therefore difficult to carry, wear, or handle.

words.ex: He did not agree with the policy, but he did not want to vilify those who supported it.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这项政策，但不想诋毁那些支持它的人。
words.en: To vilify someone means to say or write very unpleasant things about them in order to hurt their reputation.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: He feared retribution for his actions.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕因自己的行为而受到报复。
words.en: Retribution is punishment for a crime, especially punishment that is carried out by someone other than the official authorities.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.tr: adj. 难以置信的；不像真实的；
words.ex: It seems implausible that he won the lottery twice.
words.ex_cn: 他中了两次彩票，这似乎难以置信。
words.en: If you describe something as implausible, you believe that it is unlikely to be true.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: The dentist used an amalgam to fill the cavity.
words.ex_cn: 牙医用汞合金填补了蛀牙。
words.en: An amalgam is a mixture of mercury and another metal, especially one used by dentists to fill holes in teeth. It can also refer to a mixture of different things.

words.tr: adj. 有骑士风度的；彬彬有礼的；侠义的
words.ex: The knight was chivalrous and helped the lady.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士有骑士精神，帮助了那位女士。
words.en: A chivalrous man is polite, kind, and unselfish, especially towards women.

words.ex: The villainous man stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 那个邪恶的人偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as villainous, you mean that they are very wicked and evil.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.tr: adj. 无所不在的；遍及各处的
words.ex: The smell of bread is omnipresent in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨面包的香味无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something as omnipresent, you mean that it seems to be everywhere at the same time.

words.ex: The horse-drawn carriage was a forerunner of the car.
words.ex_cn: 马车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A forerunner is someone or something that comes before another and is often considered as a sign of what is to follow.

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；老谋深算的
words.ex: He is a canny trader who always makes smart choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精明的交易员，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: A canny person is clever and able to think quickly, especially in business or politics.

words.tr: adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；平淡无奇的
words.ex: His prosaic speech bored everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他平淡无奇的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as prosaic, you mean that it is ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.ex: The ancient text contained arcane symbols that no one could understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本古籍中包含着无人能理解的晦涩难解的符号。
words.en: Arcane refers to something that is mysterious or difficult to understand, often because it is known or understood by only a few people.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.tr:
n. 漠视；忽视；
v. 漠视；不理会；不顾；
words.ex: His advice was met with disregard.
words.ex_cn: 他的建议遭到了漠视。
words.en: If you disregard something, you ignore it or do not take account of it.

words.ex: He contrived to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他设法按时完成了项目。
words.en: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.tr: n. 误称…之名；不当之名
words.ex: Calling a tomato a vegetable is a misnomer.
words.ex_cn: 把番茄称为蔬菜是一种错误的称呼。
words.en: A misnomer is a name that is wrongly or unsuitably applied to someone or something.

words.ex: He showed restraint when he stayed calm during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持冷静，表现出了克制。
words.en: Restraint is a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control or within limits.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.ex: The exactitude of his measurements was crucial for the success of the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他测量的精确度对实验的成功至关重要。
words.en: The quality of being very accurate and careful about details.

words.tr:
v. 安慰；慰问
n. 控制台；操纵台
words.ex: She whispered kind words to console her crying friend.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声说些安慰的话来安抚哭泣的朋友。
words.en: If you console someone who is unhappy about something, you try to make them feel more cheerful.

words.ex: He felt uncomfortable with the adulation from his fans.
words.ex_cn: 他对于粉丝们的盲目崇拜感到不舒服。
words.en: Excessive admiration or praise.

words.tr:
n. 预示；前兆；预感
v. 预示；预兆
words.ex: The dark clouds presage a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something presages a situation or event, it is considered to be a warning or sign of what is about to happen.

words.tr: adj. 公式的；俗套的；刻板的
words.ex: His answer was too formulaic.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答太公式化了。
words.en: If you describe a way of saying or doing something as formulaic, you are criticizing it because it is not original and has been used many times before in similar situations.

words.tr: n. 新信徒；新手；初学者
words.ex: The neophyte learned the prayers from the elder.
words.ex_cn: 新信徒向长者学习祷告。
words.en: A neophyte is someone who is new to a particular activity, subject, or religion and is therefore inexperienced.

words.tr: adj. 断然的；不容置辩的；专横的
words.ex: He gave a peremptory order to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他下达了一个不容置疑的离开命令。
words.en: If someone's manner or behavior is peremptory, they are so confident and sure of their authority that they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.tr: adj. 可补救的；可补偿的
words.ex: The broken bike is reparable.
words.ex_cn: 这辆坏了的自行车可以修好。
words.en: If something is reparable, it is possible to fix or mend it.

words.ex: The rain was unremitting all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都没有停过。
words.en: If you describe someone's effort or activity as unremitting, you mean that it is continued without stopping or becoming less intense.

words.ex: He bemoans the loss of his old car.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨失去了他的旧车。
words.en: If you bemoan something, you express sorrow or dissatisfaction about it.

words.tr: adj. 欢腾的；欢欣鼓舞的
words.ex: The children were jubilant after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们赢了比赛后非常高兴。
words.en: If you are jubilant, you feel extremely happy because of a success.

words.ex: He gave a verbose answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对简单的问题给出了冗长的回答。
words.en: Using or containing more words than are necessary; long-winded.

words.tr: adj. 贪婪的；贪得无厌的；劫掠的
words.ex: The rapacious wolf ate all the food.
words.ex_cn: 贪婪的狼吃掉了所有食物。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as rapacious, you disapprove of their greedy or selfish behaviour.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.ex: The earthquake was a terrible calamity.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场巨大的灾难。
words.en: A calamity is an event that causes great harm or damage, such as a flood or a fire.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.tr:
v. 补充；
n. 补充物；附加费；
words.ex: He supplements his income by teaching part-time.
words.ex_cn: 他通过兼职教学来补充收入。
words.en: A supplement is something that is added to something else in order to make it complete or better.

words.ex: The company must retrench to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司必须裁员以节省资金。
words.en: If a person or organization retrenches, they spend less money.

words.tr: v. 使无效；抵消；废除；取消
words.ex: The judge will nullify the contract.
words.ex_cn: 法官将宣布该合同无效。
words.en: To nullify something means to make it have no effect or value.

words.tr: adj. 有说服力的；令人信服的
words.ex: His argument was cogent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点有说服力且容易理解。
words.en: A cogent argument, reason, etc. is clearly expressed and persuades people to believe it.

words.ex: The ball rebounded off the wall.
words.ex_cn: 球从墙上弹了回来。
words.en: To bounce back after hitting something; to recover in value, amount, or strength after a decrease or decline.

words.tr:
n. 扶墙；拱壁
v. 支持
words.ex: The old wall needs a buttress to stay standing.
words.ex_cn: 这面旧墙需要一个支撑物来保持不倒。
words.en: A buttress is a structure built against or projecting from a wall which serves to support or reinforce the wall. As a verb, to buttress means to support or strengthen something.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.ex: He gave a dismissive shrug when she explained her idea.
words.ex_cn: 当她解释自己的想法时，他轻蔑地耸了耸肩。
words.en: If you are dismissive of someone or something, you show that you do not consider them to be important or worth considering.

words.tr: v. 使全神贯注；独占；垄断
words.ex: He is engrossed in reading a novel.
words.ex_cn: 他正全神贯注地读一本小说。
words.en: If something engrosses you, it interests you so much that you do not notice anything else.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.ex: The coronation ceremony was a grand event.
words.ex_cn: 加冕典礼是一个盛大的活动。
words.en: A coronation is a ceremony in which a king or queen is officially crowned.

words.ex: He reads his horoscope every morning because he believes in astrology.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看星座运势，因为他相信占星术。
words.en: Astrology is the study of the movements and relative positions of celestial bodies interpreted as having an influence on human affairs and the natural world.

words.ex: He upended the bucket to drain the water.
words.ex_cn: 他把桶倒过来把水倒出。
words.en: To upend something means to turn it upside down or to change it completely.

words.tr: adj. 夸张的； v. “overblow”的过去分词；
words.ex: The news report was overblown and not true.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻报道太过夸张，不真实。
words.en: If you describe something as overblown, you mean that it is given more importance or is more elaborate than necessary.

words.ex: He gave a loud diatribe against the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他对新法律发表了一通激烈的抨击。
words.en: A diatribe is an angry speech or piece of writing that strongly criticizes something or someone.

words.tr: n. 时尚；一时流行的狂热
words.ex: Wearing those shoes is just a fad.
words.ex_cn: 穿那双鞋只是个短暂的潮流。
words.en: A fad is an activity or topic of interest that is very popular for a short time.

words.ex: His sudden win in the race was a real coup.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中突然获胜，真是了不起的成就。
words.en: A coup is a sudden, violent, and illegal seizure of power from a government.

words.ex: The king abrogated the old law.
words.ex_cn: 国王废除了旧法律。
words.en: If someone in a position of authority abrogates something such as a law, agreement, or practice, they put an end to it.

words.ex: His rectitude in business dealings was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的正直是众所周知的。
words.en: Moral integrity; honesty and correctness of judgement or behaviour.

words.tr: adj. 濒临死亡的；垂死的；
words.ex: The moribund patient stopped breathing.
words.ex_cn: 这位濒临死亡的病人停止了呼吸。
words.en: If you describe something as moribund, you mean that it is in a very bad condition and is not active or successful.

words.ex: The medicine helps inhibit pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制疼痛。
words.en: If something inhibits an event or process, it prevents it or slows it down.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.tr: adj. 邪恶的；险恶的；不祥的
words.ex: The old house looked sinister in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 那座老房子在月光下显得阴森可怖。
words.en: Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.

words.ex: The dark clouds prefigure a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If one thing prefigures another, it is a sign that the other thing will happen or exist in the future.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.ex: He used artifice to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计赢得了比赛。
words.en: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially as used to trick or deceive others.

words.tr: adj. 非物质的；无形的；不重要的
words.ex: The color is immaterial to the function.
words.ex_cn: 颜色对功能无关紧要。
words.en: If you say that something is immaterial, you mean that it is not important or not relevant.

words.ex: The expansive desert stretches for miles.
words.ex_cn: 广阔的沙漠延伸数英里。
words.en: If you describe something such as a period of time or a piece of writing as expansive, you mean that it is very long or detailed.

words.ex: He made an imprudent decision and lost all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个鲁莽的决定，失去了所有钱。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as imprudent, you think it is not sensible or carefully thought out.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.tr:
n. 忧愁
adj.  忧郁的
words.ex: He felt melancholy after the rain stopped.
words.ex_cn: 雨停后，他感到忧郁。
words.en: A feeling of deep sadness, typically with no obvious cause.

words.tr:
n. 询问；疑问；问号
v. 询问；怀疑
words.ex: He made a query about the bus schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了公交车的时刻表。
words.en: A query is a question, especially one that you ask in order to check that something is true or correct.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.ex: The composer's rhapsody captured the essence of the wild, untamed landscapes.
words.ex_cn: 作曲家的狂想曲捕捉到了狂野、未驯服的风景的精髓。
words.en: A rhapsody is a piece of music that is full of feeling and is not regular in its form. It can also refer to an expression of great enthusiasm or happiness.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.ex: The annexation of the small country by its neighbor caused international protest.
words.ex_cn: 邻国对这个小国的吞并引发了国际抗议。
words.en: The act of annexing, especially territory.

words.ex: He received an accolade for his excellent work.
words.ex_cn: 他因出色的工作而获得了一项荣誉。
words.en: An accolade is something done or given to someone as a special honor or as a sign of approval.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: The boy is a piano prodigy at age six.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩六岁时就是一位钢琴奇才。
words.en: A prodigy is someone who is unusually young and has a great natural ability in a particular area.

words.tr:
n. 茎；词干；
v. 起源于(~ from)；
words.ex: The flower grows on a long green stem.
words.ex_cn: 花长在一根长长的绿色茎上。
words.en: The main body or stalk of a plant or shrub, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean; to stop or restrict (the flow of something).

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.tr: adj. 很快消失的；渐消散的；短暂的
words.ex: The evanescent mist disappeared at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 那消散的薄雾在日出时消失了。
words.en: Something that is evanescent quickly disappears or fades away.

words.ex: The loon is a large aquatic bird known for its distinctive call.
words.ex_cn: 潜鸟是一种以其独特叫声而闻名的大型水鸟。
words.en: A loon is a large diving bird with a distinctive call, found in North America and northern Eurasia. It is also used informally to refer to a crazy or silly person.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；自命不凡的；浮华的
words.ex: He gave a pompous speech with big words.
words.ex_cn: 他用华丽的词藻做了一番自大的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as pompous, you mean that they behave or speak in a very serious way because they think they are more important than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 非典型的；不规则的
words.ex: He has an atypical way of solving problems.
words.ex_cn: 他解决问题的方式很不寻常。
words.en: Not representative of a type, group, or class; unusual or irregular.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 后勤人员；附加项目
words.ex: The ancillary staff help the doctors in the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 辅助人员在医院里帮助医生。
words.en: Ancillary means providing necessary support to the primary activities or operation of an organization, system, etc.

words.ex: The rain gave us a short respite from the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨为我们带来了短暂的凉爽缓解。
words.en: A respite is a short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 没有钱的；身无分文的；贫穷的
words.ex: The impecunious student had to rely on scholarships to continue his education.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的学生不得不依靠奖学金来继续他的学业。
words.en: If you describe someone as impecunious, you mean that they have very little money.

words.ex: The weather was agreeable for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气令人愉悦，适合散步。
words.en: Pleasant and easy to like; willing to agree to something

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

words.ex: The table has a wooden veneer on top.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子的表面有一层木制饰板。
words.en: A veneer is a thin layer of wood or other material that is used to cover a surface, especially in furniture making, to make it look more attractive.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.ex: He disavow any connection to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 他否认与这起犯罪有任何关联。
words.en: If you disavow something, you say that you are not responsible for it or you do not agree with it.

words.tr: v. 充分满足，使饱享； 使厌腻
words.ex: The rich food sated her hunger.
words.ex_cn: 丰盛的食物满足了她的饥饿感。
words.en: To satisfy a desire or an appetite to the full.

words.ex: His sentiment about the new policy is positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对新政策的看法是积极的。
words.en: A sentiment is a thought, opinion, or idea based on a feeling about a situation, or a way of thinking about something.

words.ex: She drank water to assuage her thirst.
words.ex_cn: 她喝水来缓解口渴。
words.en: If you assuage an unpleasant feeling that someone has, you make them feel it less strongly. To assuage a problem or situation means to make it less intense or severe.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.ex: He changed his stance on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了对气候变化的立场。
words.en: A stance is a particular way of standing, especially in sports such as golf or baseball, or a person's attitude or opinion about something, especially when it is stated publicly.

words.ex: His speech was hortatory, urging everyone to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲是劝勉性的，鼓励大家更加努力工作。
words.en: If someone makes a hortatory speech or statement, they are encouraging or urging people to do something.

words.tr:
n. 前情；先行词；祖先（常复）
adj. 在 ... 之前的
words.ex: The word 'dog' is the antecedent of 'it' in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 在这句话中，'dog' 是 'it' 的先行词。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.tr: v. 混淆；曲解；断章取义
words.ex: He garbled the message so no one understood it.
words.ex_cn: 他把消息说得乱七八糟，没人能听懂。
words.en: If you garble something, you distort or confuse it so that it is difficult to understand.

words.ex: He showed prescience by predicting the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他通过预测风暴展现了先见之明。
words.en: The ability to know or predict what will happen in the future.

words.ex: The hero in the story is an archetype of courage.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的英雄是勇气的原型。
words.en: An archetype is a very typical example of a certain person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 非自愿的；不由自主的；
words.ex: His hand moved in an involuntary way.
words.ex_cn: 他的手不自觉地动了一下。
words.en: If you make an involuntary movement or exclamation, you make it suddenly and without intending to because you are unable to control yourself.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.ex: He deluded himself into thinking he would win.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗自己，以为自己会赢。
words.en: If you delude yourself, you let yourself believe that something is true, even though it is not true.

words.tr:
adj. 无可名状的；难以区别的；无特征的；极普通的
n. 无以名状；不属任何类型的人
words.ex: The building was nondescript, with no special features.
words.ex_cn: 这栋建筑无可名状，没有任何特别的特征。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as nondescript, you mean that their appearance is rather dull, and not at all interesting or attractive.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.tr: adj. 无定形的；无组织的；
words.ex: The glass is amorphous because it lacks a regular shape.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃是无定形的，因为它没有规则的形状。
words.en: Lacking a clear shape or form; not clearly defined or structured.

words.ex: The alcohol is volatile and evaporates quickly.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是易挥发的，会迅速蒸发。
words.en: A volatile situation or person is one that is likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially by getting worse.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.tr:
adj. 狡猾的；奸诈的；巧妙的
n. 奸诈；狡猾
words.ex: The cunning fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is cunning is clever and good at deceiving others in order to get what they want.

words.tr: n. 追求轰动效应；哗众取宠
words.ex: The newspaper uses sensationalism to attract readers.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸使用煽情主义来吸引读者。
words.en: Sensationalism is the use of sensational subject matter, style, or methods, or the condition of being sensational.

words.tr: v. 解释；把…逐字译出；作句法分析
words.ex: He construes her silence as a yes.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
words.en: If you construe something in a particular way, you interpret it in that way.

words.tr: adj. 容量大的；广阔的；宽敞的
words.ex: The capacious room can hold many people.
words.ex_cn: 这个宽敞的房间可以容纳很多人。
words.en: Capacious means having a lot of space inside; roomy.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；充满…的
words.ex: Rumors are rife in the town.
