words.en: If you say that someone is supercilious, you disapprove of them because they behave in a way that shows they think they are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 想复仇的；报复性的；怀恨的
words.ex: He was vindictive and refused to forgive her.
words.ex_cn: 他心怀报复，拒绝原谅她。
words.en: If you say that someone is vindictive, you are critical of them because they deliberately try to upset or cause trouble for someone who they think has done them harm.

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.ex: He gave a furtive look around before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前偷偷看了一眼四周。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as furtive, you disapprove of them behaving as if they want to keep something secret or hidden.

words.tr: n. 阿谀奉承的人；谄媚者；马屁精
words.ex: He is a sycophant who always agrees with his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是附和老板的马屁精。
words.en: A sycophant is someone who praises powerful or rich people in an insincere way in order to get an advantage.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；起破坏作用的
n. 腐蚀性物品
words.ex: The acid is corrosive and can damage metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸具有腐蚀性，会损坏金属。
words.en: A corrosive substance is able to destroy solid materials by a chemical reaction.

words.ex: The cat is agile and jumps high.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳得很高。
words.en: Someone who is agile can move quickly and easily.

words.ex: The provincial government opened a new school.
words.ex_cn: 省政府开设了一所新学校。
words.en: Relating to a province or provinces; having the manners, viewpoints, etc., considered characteristic of unsophisticated inhabitants of a province; narrow-minded.

words.ex: His speech was full of trite phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了陈腐的表达。
words.en: If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite, you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.

words.ex: His fear is unfounded.
words.ex_cn: 他的恐惧是没有根据的。
words.en: If you describe a rumour, belief, or feeling as unfounded, you mean that it is wrong because it is not based on facts or evidence.

words.ex: The weather was congenial for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: A congenial person, place, or environment is pleasant because it suits your character or nature.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.ex: He tries to denigrate his rival's ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低对手的想法。
words.en: If you denigrate someone or something, you criticize them unfairly or insult them.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.ex: The experience was a salutary lesson in the importance of preparation.
words.ex_cn: 这次经历是一个关于准备重要性的有益教训。
words.en: A salutary experience or warning is one that has a good effect or influence, especially by showing you the bad results of a particular action or behaviour.

words.ex: The spectral lines show the elements in the star.
words.ex_cn: 光谱线显示了恒星中的元素。
words.en: Relating to or suggesting a spectrum; especially relating to or suggesting a ghost.

words.ex: His smile evinces joy.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑流露出快乐。
words.en: To show clearly that you have a particular quality, feeling, or ability.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.ex: The army stopped the incursion at the border.
words.ex_cn: 军队在边境阻止了入侵。
words.en: An incursion is a sudden attack on or invasion of a place.

words.ex: He gave a vicious smile before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前露出一个恶毒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vicious, you mean that they are violent and cruel, or that they are intended to cause someone great harm or suffering.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.ex: The enormity of the crime shocked the whole city.
words.ex_cn: 这桩罪行的极恶震惊了整个城市。
words.en: If you refer to the enormity of something that you consider to be a problem or difficulty, you are referring to its very great size, extent, or seriousness.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: The two roads converge at the town center.
words.ex_cn: 这两条路在镇中心交汇。
words.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a preeminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: Standing out in importance or reputation; superior to all others.

words.tr: adj. 不动感情的；冷静的；平心静气的
words.ex: She remained dispassionate throughout the heated debate.
words.ex_cn: 她在激烈的辩论中始终保持冷静。
words.en: If you are dispassionate, you are able to act calmly and reasonably and not be influenced by your feelings or by personal opinions.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicine for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了治疗感冒的药。
words.en: If a doctor prescribes medicine or treatment for you, he or she tells you what medicine or treatment to have.

words.ex: Good teachers edify their students with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 好老师用智慧启发学生。
words.en: To edify someone means to improve their mind or character by teaching them something.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr: adj. 空洞的；枯燥乏味的；不成熟的；缺乏营养的
words.ex: His jejune remarks made no sense to the audience.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的言论让听众无法理解。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as jejune, you are criticizing them for being very simple and unsophisticated.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.ex: He noticed the nuance in her voice.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她声音中的细微差别。
words.en: A very slight difference in meaning, sound, color, or someone's feelings that is not usually very obvious.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.ex: There is a dearth of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄缺乏干净的水。
words.en: A dearth of something is a lack or scarcity of it.

words.tr: n. 前景；最显著的位置；
words.ex: The trees in the foreground are very tall.
words.ex_cn: 前景中的树很高。
words.en: The part of a view that is nearest to the observer, especially in a picture or photograph; the most important or prominent position.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.tr: adj. 贪赃枉法的；腐败的
words.ex: The official was venal and took bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员贪腐，接受了贿赂。
words.en: If you describe someone as venal, you disapprove of them because they are prepared to do almost anything in return for money, even things which are dishonest or immoral.

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.tr: adj. 不能减缩的；无法减轻的
words.ex: This fraction is irreducible.
words.ex_cn: 这个分数是最简形式。
words.en: If you describe something as irreducible, you mean that it cannot be made smaller or simpler.

words.ex: She abhors violence.
words.ex_cn: 她憎恶暴力。
words.en: If you abhor something, you hate it very much, especially because you think it is immoral or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 溢于言表的；感情奔放的
words.ex: She was effusive in her praise for the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她对老师的赞美非常热情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as effusive, you mean that they express pleasure, gratitude, or approval in a very enthusiastic way.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: He showed disdain for the lazy students.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些懒惰的学生表现出蔑视。
words.en: If you feel disdain for someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 不知情的；不经意的
words.ex: He was the unwitting victim of a prank.
words.ex_cn: 他是不知情的恶作剧受害者。
words.en: If someone is unwitting, they do not know or realize something.

words.ex: The teacher lauded the student for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 老师称赞了这名学生努力学习。
words.en: If people laud someone, they praise and admire them.

words.ex: The old song is reminiscent of my childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌让人想起我的童年。
words.en: If you say that one thing is reminiscent of another, you mean that it reminds you of it.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.tr: adj. 不可改变的；永恒不变的
words.ex: The password is immutable and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 密码是不可更改的。
words.en: If you say that something is immutable, you mean that it cannot be changed at all.

words.tr:
adj. 反动的；保守的
n. 反动派；保守人士
words.ex: The reactionary government banned free speech.
words.ex_cn: 这个反动政府禁止了言论自由。
words.en: A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 不屈的；不屈服的；坚硬的
words.ex: He is unyielding in his decision.
words.ex_cn: 他在决定上毫不退让。
words.en: If you describe someone as unyielding, you mean that they are very determined and not likely to change their mind.

words.tr:
v. 喜欢；享受；从…获得乐趣
n. 享受；乐趣；调味品
words.ex: He relishes every bite of his favorite food.
words.ex_cn: 他享受着每一口他最喜欢的食物。
words.en: If you relish something, you enjoy it very much.

words.tr: adj. 自命不凡的；自负的；矫饰的
words.ex: He wore a fancy hat to seem pretentious.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶华丽的帽子，显得自命不凡。
words.en: If you describe something as pretentious, you mean that it is intended to seem important or significant, but you think it is not.

words.ex: She lamented the death of her dog.
words.ex_cn: 她哀悼她狗的去世。
words.en: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.

words.ex: His derogatory remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他毁谤的言辞伤害了她的感情。
words.en: If you make a derogatory remark or comment about someone or something, you say something that shows you have a low opinion of them.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.ex: He made an expeditious decision to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速做出了离开的决定。
words.en: If you describe something as expeditious, you mean that it is done quickly and efficiently.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: The old house had a labyrinthine hallway.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子有一条像迷宫一样的走廊。
words.en: If you describe a place as labyrinthine, you mean that it is like a labyrinth because it has a lot of narrow streets or paths that cross each other, making it difficult to find your way around.

words.ex: The enzyme acts as a catalyst in the reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶在反应中充当催化剂。
words.en: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a person or thing that precipitates a change.

words.ex: The virus can propagate quickly among people.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以在人群中迅速传播。
words.en: To propagate something means to spread it and encourage more people to believe in it or support it.

words.tr: adj. 腼腆的；怕羞的；忸怩的
words.ex: She gave a coy smile when asked about her new boyfriend.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及她的新男友时，她露出了腼腆的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as coy, you mean they are pretending to be shy about something in order to attract attention or to deceive people.

words.ex: They tried to extirpate the weeds from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图把花园里的杂草彻底清除。
words.en: To destroy or remove something completely, especially a problem or an organization.

words.tr: v. 对…表示极不赞成；强烈反对；轻视
words.ex: They deprecate old software.
words.ex_cn: 他们不推荐使用旧软件。
words.en: If you deprecate something, you criticize it or express your disapproval of it.

words.tr: adj. 易反应的；应答的；回答的；
words.ex: The child is responsive to his mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子对母亲的声音反应灵敏。
words.en: If someone or something is responsive, they react quickly and favorably.

words.ex: There was clear hostility between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间明显存在敌意。
words.en: Hostility is unfriendly or aggressive behaviour towards people or ideas.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；简明扼要的；凝练的
words.ex: He gave a laconic reply: 'Yes.'
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答：‘是的。’
words.en: If you describe someone as laconic, you mean that they use very few words to say something, so that they seem casual or unfriendly.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medication to palliate the patient's pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了药来减轻病人的疼痛。
words.en: To palliate means to make something less severe or intense without actually solving the cause of it. It can refer to the easing of physical pain or the attempt to make a fault or crime seem less serious.

words.tr: n. 赏赐；赠品；贺礼；慷慨赠与的钱或物
words.ex: The king showed largesse to the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王向穷人施舍恩惠。
words.en: Generosity in bestowing money or gifts upon others.

words.ex: He estranged his brother with harsh words.
words.ex_cn: 他用刻薄的话与兄弟疏远了。
words.en: If you estrange someone, especially a member of your family, you cause them to stop being friendly or close to you.

words.ex: He faced public denunciation for his lies.
words.ex_cn: 他因撒谎而遭到公众的谴责。
words.en: Denunciation is the act of criticizing something or someone strongly and publicly.

words.ex: He forbears from yelling when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他生气时忍住不喊叫。
words.en: If you forbear from doing something, you do not do it although you have the opportunity or the right to do it.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.ex: The child's petulant behavior was a result of his frustration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子暴躁的行为是因他的沮丧所致。
words.en: If you describe someone as petulant, you mean that they get angry or annoyed in a childish or unreasonable way.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；难以理解的；神秘莫测的
words.ex: His expression was inscrutable.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情难以捉摸。
words.en: If someone or something is inscrutable, it is impossible to understand or know what they are thinking or feeling.

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr: v. （故意地）混淆；使混乱；使困惑
words.ex: He tries to obfuscate the truth with complicated words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用复杂的词语混淆真相。
words.en: To obfuscate something means to deliberately make it unclear or difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 不乐意的；不情愿的；
words.ex: He is loath to apologize for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他不乐意为自己的错误道歉。
words.en: If you are loath to do something, you do not want to do it.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.ex: The angry father lambasted the bully with his belt.
words.ex_cn: 愤怒的父亲用皮带痛打了那个欺凌者。
words.en: If you lambaste someone, you criticize them severely, usually in public.

words.ex: The storm caused an upheaval in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A very large change in something that often causes confusion or problems.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.ex: He handed in his resignation last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周递交了辞职信。
words.en: The act of giving up a job or position in a formal or official way; also refers to the acceptance of something undesirable but inevitable.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；造成伤害的
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is deleterious has a harmful effect on something, especially on a person's health.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；肤浅的；易做到的
words.ex: He gave a facile answer to the hard question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个简单的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's arguments or suggestions as facile, you are criticizing them because their ideas are too simple and indicate a lack of careful, intelligent thinking.

words.tr: v. 砍；劈；削成…形状；开辟；坚持；遵守
words.ex: He hews wood every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上砍柴。
words.en: To cut or shape something with a tool such as an axe, or to make something by cutting.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.ex: He felt lethargy after eating too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完太多垃圾食品后感到无精打采。
words.en: Lethargy is the condition or state of being lethargic; sluggishness, drowsiness, or apathy.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.tr:
v. 煨；用文火炖；充满；即将爆发
n. 炖；即将发作
words.ex: The soup is simmering on the stove.
words.ex_cn: 汤正在炉子上慢炖。
words.en: To cook something slowly at a temperature slightly below boiling point.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.ex: This painting has a distinctive style.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有独特的风格。
words.en: Something that is distinctive has a special quality or feature which makes it easily recognizable and different from other things of the same type.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: The lamp illuminate the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.

words.ex: He believes in an egalitarian society where everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一个人人平等的平等主义社会。
words.en: Egalitarian is used to describe something that is based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.tr: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；不切实际的
words.ex: He made a quixotic effort to fix the broken bridge with sticks and glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用树枝和胶水试图修复那座破桥，这真是异想天开。
words.en: If you describe someone's ideas or plans as quixotic, you mean that they are imaginative or hopeful but unrealistic.

words.ex: The recondite math problem confused most students.
words.ex_cn: 这道深奥的数学题让大多数学生感到困惑。
words.en: Recondite knowledge or information is known and understood by very few people.

words.ex: He feels ennui while doing the same job every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天做同样的工作时感到厌倦。
words.en: A feeling of listlessness and dissatisfaction arising from a lack of occupation or excitement.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；失误
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；失误；跌跌撞撞地走
words.ex: He made a big blunder in the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中犯了一个大错误。
words.en: A blunder is a stupid or careless mistake.

words.ex: The bread is stale because it was left out too long.
words.ex_cn: 面包不新鲜了，因为它放得太久。
words.en: If food or air is stale, it is no longer fresh and therefore unpleasant.

words.ex: He took a provisional job until he found a better one.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到更好的工作之前做了一份临时工作。
words.en: Something that is provisional is temporary and likely to be changed or replaced in the future.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.tr: adj. 符合的；一致的；全等的
words.ex: The two shapes are congruent in size.
words.ex_cn: 这两个形状大小相符。
words.en: If one thing is congruent with another, they are similar or fit together well.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: He spoke with candor about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地谈到了自己的错误。
words.en: the quality of being open and honest in expression; frankness.

words.ex: The smoke began to stifle her breathing.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾开始让她窒息。
words.en: To stifle something means to prevent it from happening, continuing, or developing.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.ex: The knight's shield was emblazoned with his family crest.
words.ex_cn: 骑士的盾牌上装饰着他的家族徽章。
words.en: To decorate or adorn with heraldic or other symbols; to celebrate or proclaim something publicly.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.ex: Her smile heartened the tired students.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑鼓舞了疲惫的学生。
words.en: If someone is heartened by something, it encourages them and makes them cheerful.

words.ex: He underrates his own talent.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了自己的才华。
words.en: To underrate something or someone means to fail to recognize their true value or importance.

words.ex: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨来临前，乌云显得不祥。
words.en: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.

words.tr: v. 使失去勇气；使身心交疲；使气馁
words.ex: The loud noise unnerves her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让她心神不宁。
words.en: If something unnerves you, it makes you feel worried or uncomfortable.

words.tr: v. 即兴创作；即兴表演；临时准备；
words.ex: He improvise a song on the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他即兴创作了一首钢琴曲。
words.en: If you improvise, you make or do something using whatever you have or without having planned it in advance.

words.tr: adj. 和平主义的；和平的
words.ex: His irenic tone helped calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他平和的语气帮助平息了争论。
words.en: Promoting peace; conciliatory.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.ex: The caterpillar metamorphose into a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫变成了蝴蝶。
words.en: To change completely in form or nature.

words.ex: He made an unwonted silence during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上出乎意料地保持了沉默。
words.en: Not usual or common; unusual.

words.tr: adj. 风度好的；个性或外表宜人的；英俊的；貌美的；有魅力的
words.ex: He was a personable young man, always ready to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品貌兼优的年轻人，总是乐于助人。
words.en: If you describe someone as personable, you mean that they are pleasant and attractive in appearance and character.

words.tr: adj. 宽宏大量的；有雅量的
words.ex: He was magnanimous and forgave his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽宏大量，原谅了他的敌人。
words.en: If you are magnanimous, you behave kindly and generously toward someone, especially after defeating them or being treated badly by them.

words.ex: He fixates on small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他专注于小错误。
words.en: If you fixate on something, you think about it so much that you are unable to consider or think about anything else.

words.ex: The scarcity of water caused problems in the village.
words.ex_cn: 水的缺乏给村庄带来了问题。
words.en: A scarcity of something is a situation in which there is not enough of it.

words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.tr: adj. 谨小慎微的；一丝不苟的
words.ex: He is punctilious about following every rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对遵守每一条规则都谨小慎微。
words.en: If someone is punctilious, they are very careful to behave correctly and to follow the details of rules or customs.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.tr: v.  合理化； 使合理
words.ex: He tries to rationalize his bad choices.
words.ex_cn: 他试图为自己的错误选择找借口。
words.en: To rationalize something means to try to find reasons to explain or justify it, often when these reasons are not really good ones.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的；
words.ex: He made a shrewd decision to buy the house low.
words.ex_cn: 他精明地决定低价买下这栋房子。
words.en: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage.

words.tr: adj. 人道的；仁慈的；人文的
words.ex: The shelter treats animals in a humane way.
words.ex_cn: 这个收容所以人道的方式对待动物。
words.en: If you describe something as humane, you mean that it is good and kind, especially because it decreases suffering.

words.tr: adj. 每日的；平凡的；平常的
words.ex: He drinks coffee every quotidian morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is quotidian occurs every day or is very common and ordinary.

words.ex: Steve Jobs is the founder of Apple.
words.ex_cn: 史蒂夫·乔布斯是苹果公司的创办者。
words.en: A founder is someone who establishes an organization, company, or institution. As a verb, it means to fail or collapse, especially in terms of a plan or a ship sinking.

words.tr: adj. 有先见之明的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He is a provident man who saves money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有远见的人，会为未来存钱。
words.en: Making provision for the future; exercising foresight or forethought.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；暗中行事的
words.ex: He made a clandestine meeting with his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他与朋友进行了一次秘密会面。
words.en: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit.

words.tr: n. 诅咒；受诅咒的事；逐出教门；十分讨厌的人（或事物）
words.ex: Lying is anathema to her.
words.ex_cn: 说谎是她所诅咒的。
words.en: Something or someone that one vehemently dislikes.

words.tr: adj. 可导致诉讼的；爱打官司的；好争论的
words.ex: He is a litigious man who always sues his neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个爱打官司的人，总是起诉他的邻居。
words.en: If you describe someone as litigious, you mean that they are very willing to bring a dispute to a court of law in order to resolve it.

words.tr: adj. 机智的；圆滑的；得体的
words.ex: He was tactful when he said no to her request.
words.ex_cn: 当他拒绝她的请求时，他很得体。
words.en: If you describe someone as tactful, you approve of them because they are careful not to say or do anything that would offend or upset other people.

words.tr: adj. 说得过去的；站得住脚的；可防守的
words.ex: His excuse was a little weak, but still tenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口有点牵强，但还是说得过去的。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or plan is tenable, it is reasonable and could be successfully defended against criticism.

words.ex: He tried to dispel the fear with calm words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用平静的话语消除恐惧。
words.en: To dispel something such as a fear, belief, or idea means to make it disappear or to make people stop believing it.

words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.ex: The fusion of music and technology creates new sounds.
words.ex_cn: 音乐与技术的融合创造了新的声音。
words.en: The process or result of joining two or more things together to form a single entity.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的；
words.ex: He is a notorious thief who stole from many stores.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个声名狼藉的小偷，偷过许多商店。
words.en: Someone or something that is notorious is well known for something bad.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.tr:
adj. 不知所措的；陷于窘境的
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措；“nonplus”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was nonplussed by the unexpected question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个意外的问题感到不知所措。
words.en: If you are nonplussed, you are so surprised and confused that you do not know what to say or do.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.tr: v. 擦去；忘却；不抛头露面；使（自己）不受人注意
words.ex: He tried to efface the mark with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用橡皮擦掉那个痕迹。
words.en: To efface something means to remove it completely so that it no longer exists or is no longer noticeable.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.tr:
n. 雄鹿；公羊；雄兔；美元
v. （马等）猛然弓背跃起；抵制
words.ex: The buck ran through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 雄鹿在森林中奔跑。
words.en: A buck is a male deer, antelope, rabbit, or hare. It can also refer to a dollar in American slang. As a verb, it means to jump or to resist something.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.tr: n. 吝啬；小气；过度节俭
words.ex: His parsimony led to a reputation for stinginess.
words.ex_cn: 他的吝啬导致了他被认为是个小气鬼。
words.en: Parsimony is the quality of being very unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；欠缺的；微小的；
words.ex: There is scant evidence to support the claim.
words.ex_cn: 支持这一说法的证据不足。
words.en: If you describe something as scant, you mean that there is not enough of it or that it is not as much as it should be.

words.ex: This medicine is efficacious for colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: An efficacious method or treatment is one that has the ability to produce a desired effect or result.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr: adj. 痛切的；酸楚的；强烈的；尖刻的
words.ex: The letter was poignant and made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 这封信很感人，让她哭了。
words.en: A poignant piece of writing or music makes you feel sad or full of pity.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.tr: n. 拼贴画；拼贴艺术；杂烩
words.ex: He made a collage from old magazine pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧杂志的图片做了一幅拼贴画。
words.en: A collage is a picture that has been made by sticking pieces of colored paper, cloth, or photographs onto a surface.

words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这道数学题做了一个易懂的解释。
words.en: If someone is lucid, they are able to understand things clearly and think clearly, especially when they have been very ill or confused.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.ex: The scientist debunked the myth that sugar makes children hyper.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家揭穿了糖会使孩子多动的谬论。
words.en: If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false. If you debunk something that is widely admired, you show that it is not as good as people think it is.

words.ex: He tried to decipher the secret code.
words.ex_cn: 他试图破译那个秘密代码。
words.en: To decipher something means to convert it from a code into normal language or to understand something that is difficult to understand or that is not obvious.

words.ex: Children are susceptible to colds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子容易感冒。
words.en: If you are susceptible to something or someone, you are very likely to be influenced by them.

words.ex: The moon reached its apogee last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚月亮到达了远地点。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; a climax or culmination.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He is chary of spending money on useless things.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意把钱花在无用的东西上。
words.en: If you are chary of doing something, you are cautious or hesitant about doing it because you are worried that it might have bad consequences.

words.tr: v. 小偷小摸；偷窃（小东西）
words.ex: He was caught pilfering from the store.
words.ex_cn: 他因在商店里小偷小摸被抓。
words.en: To pilfer means to steal things of little value or in small quantities, often in a stealthy way.

words.ex: He spent the evening in introspection.
words.ex_cn: 他整个晚上都在反省。
words.en: The examination of one's own thoughts, feelings, and sensations; self-examination.

words.ex: He has a sartorial style that impresses everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种令人印象深刻的服装风格。
words.en: Sartorial relates to tailoring, clothes, or style of dress.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.ex: The dog has a long pedigree from champion lines.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗有着来自冠军血统的悠久血统。
words.en: A pedigree is the recorded ancestry or lineage of a person or animal, often used to indicate purity of breed or high social status.

words.tr: adj. 精疲力竭的；腻烦的；无兴致的
words.ex: She felt jaded after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 工作了一整天后，她感到精疲力竭。
words.en: If you are jaded, you feel bored, tired, and not enthusiastic, especially because you have had too much of something.

words.tr:
n. 骗局
v. 诈骗
words.ex: He fell victim to an online scam.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了一个网络骗局的受害者。
words.en: A scam is a dishonest scheme or fraud.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a placebo to see if his pain would go away.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一个安慰剂，看看他的疼痛是否会消失。
words.en: A substance that has no therapeutic effect, used as a control in testing new drugs, or given for its psychological effect to a patient who believes it to be a medicine.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: The erudite professor knows many ancient languages.
words.ex_cn: 这位博学的教授懂得许多古代语言。
words.en: Having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.ex: His rude words inflamed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了人群。
words.en: To inflame a situation or feeling means to make it much more intense or serious.

words.ex: He is a hypocrite because he says he loves peace but fights often.
words.ex_cn: 他是个伪君子，因为他声称热爱和平，却经常打架。
words.en: A hypocrite is someone who pretends to have certain beliefs or opinions that they do not really have, especially in order to deceive people.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.ex: He is taciturn and rarely speaks.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默寡言，很少说话。
words.en: A taciturn person does not say very much and can seem unfriendly.

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.tr: v. 重述要点；简要回顾
words.ex: Can you recapitulate the main points of the lecture?
words.ex_cn: 你能重述一下讲座的主要要点吗？
words.en: If you recapitulate something, you say it again briefly, or you give a summary of it.

words.tr: adj. 极神圣的；神圣不可侵犯的
words.ex: The church's rules were considered sacrosanct and unchangeable.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的规定被认为是神圣不可侵犯的，不可改变的。
words.en: If you describe something as sacrosanct, you mean that it is considered to be special and should not be changed or interfered with.

words.ex: He gave a constructive comment on my essay.
words.ex_cn: 他对我的论文给出了建设性的评论。
words.en: If something is constructive, it is useful and intended to help or improve something.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.ex: He has business acumen and makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他有商业洞察力，能做出明智的决定。
words.en: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

words.tr: adj. 不注意的；疏忽的；非故意的
words.ex: He made an inadvertent mistake while typing.
words.ex_cn: 他在打字时不小心犯了个错误。
words.en: If something bad is inadvertent, it is done without realizing that it is wrong or that it could have bad consequences.

words.tr: adj. 作为象征的；作为标志的；
words.ex: The dove is emblematic of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
words.en: If something is emblematic of a particular quality or situation, it is considered to be typical or representative of it.

words.tr: n. 弹幕射击；掩护炮火；拦河坝
words.ex: The soldiers faced a barrage of bullets.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们面对着一阵弹雨。
words.en: A barrage is a heavy and continuous bombardment of gunfire or a dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

words.tr: n. 地狱；炼狱；无法控制的大火
words.ex: The city was an inferno of fire and destruction.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市成了火与毁灭的地狱。
words.en: An inferno is a place or situation that is extremely hot and fiery, resembling hell.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；老式的； v. “outmode”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This phone is outmoded and needs to be replaced.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，需要更换。
words.en: If you describe something as outmoded, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.tr:
v. 断然拒绝
n. 粗暴回绝；生硬的拒绝
words.ex: He rebuffed her offer with a shake of his head.
words.ex_cn: 他摇了摇头，拒绝了她的提议。
words.en: If you rebuff someone or rebuff a suggestion that they make, you refuse to do what they suggest.

words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.ex: The family endured years of privation during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭在战争期间经历了多年的贫困。
words.en: Privation is a situation in which you do not have the things that are essential for a comfortable life, such as enough food, clothing, or shelter.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.tr: adj. 迟缓的；呆钝的；不活泼的；蛰伏的
words.ex: The cat was torpid in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 猫在阳光下懒洋洋的。
words.en: If you are torpid, you are mentally or physically inactive, especially because you are feeling lazy or sleepy.

words.tr:
adj. 巡回的；流动的
n. 四处奔波的人；流浪者
words.ex: The itinerant worker moves from town to town for jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这位流动工人为了工作从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: Someone who is itinerant travels from place to place, usually because they have no permanent home or job, or because they are involved in a particular activity that requires this.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.tr: adj. 乐天的；自信的；红润的
words.ex: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the future.
words.ex_cn: 尽管遭遇挫折，他对未来仍然充满希望。
words.en: If you are sanguine about something, you are cheerful and confident that things will happen in the way that you want them to.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.tr: v. 监禁；禁闭；把...嵌在墙上
words.ex: He was immured in the old tower for years.
words.ex_cn: 他被囚禁在那座旧塔里多年。
words.en: To confine someone within or as if within walls; imprison.

words.tr:
n. 贮藏物；隐藏物
v. 贮藏；囤积
words.ex: The treasure hunter found a hoard of gold coins.
words.ex_cn: 寻宝者发现了一堆金币。
words.en: If you hoard things such as food or money, you save or store them, often in secret, because they are valuable or important to you.

words.tr: adj. 预谋的；事先策划的； v. “premeditate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The theft was premeditated, not random.
words.ex_cn: 这次盗窃是预谋的，不是随机的。
words.en: If you describe an action as premeditated, you mean that it has been planned or thought about before it is done.

words.tr: n. 奸诈；欺骗；口是心非
words.ex: He showed duplicity by lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他通过对朋友撒谎表现出虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of duplicity, you mean that they are deceitful.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: He retains his old photos in a box.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧照片保存在一个盒子里。
words.en: If you retain something, you keep it or continue to have it.

words.ex: His conjecture was that the missing key was in the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 他猜测丢失的钥匙在抽屉里。
words.en: A conjecture is a conclusion that is based on information that is not certain or complete.

words.ex: The docile dog followed its owner quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这只温顺的狗安静地跟着主人。
words.en: A docile person or animal is quiet, not aggressive, and easily controlled.

words.ex: We use a repellent to keep mosquitoes away.
words.ex_cn: 我们使用驱虫剂来驱赶蚊子。
words.en: A repellent is a substance that is used to keep insects or animals away from something. It can also refer to something that is extremely unpleasant or disgusting.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.ex: After running for an hour, he felt fatigue.
words.ex_cn: 跑了一个小时后，他感到疲乏。
words.en: A feeling of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.ex: The sponge is porous and absorbs water easily.
words.ex_cn: 海绵是多孔的，容易吸水。
words.en: If something is porous, it has a lot of tiny holes in it that allow water or air to pass through slowly.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: She accentuates the first syllable when she says the word.
words.ex_cn: 她说这个词时重读第一个音节。
words.en: To accentuate something means to emphasize it or make it more noticeable.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.ex: The company's policies were inimical to the interests of its employees.
words.ex_cn: 公司的政策对员工的利益是有害的。
words.en: If one thing is inimical to another, it prevents the second thing from happening or being successful, or it is harmful to it.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr: adj. 不安宁的； 焦躁不安的；难驾驭的；倔强的
words.ex: The audience grew restive as the speaker droned on.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者喋喋不休，听众开始焦躁不安。
words.en: If you are restive, you are impatient or bored with a situation and you want it to change.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.tr: adj. 拖拉的；拖沓的；磨蹭的
words.ex: He gave a dilatory answer to the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师的问题回答得很拖拉。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as dilatory, you mean that they are slow and cause delay.

words.tr: adj. 不可靠的；不稳固的；无根据的；不佳的
words.ex: The building's structure was found to be unsound.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的结构被发现是不牢靠的。
words.en: If something or someone is unsound, they are not in a good condition or are not based on good reasons.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.ex: I presume he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假设他明天会到。
words.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

words.tr:
adj. 离奇可笑的；滑稽古怪的
n. 小丑；滑稽演员
words.ex: His droll sense of humor always lightens the mood.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的幽默感总是能缓和气氛。
words.en: If you describe something as droll, you mean that it is amusing, especially in an odd or unusual way.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.tr: n. 愤世嫉俗者；悲观者；怀疑者
words.ex: He is a cynic who never believes in good intentions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不相信任何善意的愤世嫉俗者。
words.en: A cynic is someone who believes that people are motivated purely by self-interest rather than acting for honorable or unselfish reasons.

words.ex: He faced ridicule for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿旧衣服而遭到嘲笑。
words.en: To ridicule someone or something means to make fun of them in an unkind way.

words.tr: adj. 匆忙的；草率的；急躁的
words.ex: He made a hasty decision and regretted it.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个仓促的决定，后来后悔了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as hasty, you mean that they are acting too quickly, without thinking carefully, often with unwanted results.

words.ex: He dissimulated his anger to keep the peace.
words.ex_cn: 他掩饰了自己的愤怒以维持和平。
words.en: To dissimulate means to hide your real feelings, character, or intentions.

words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.ex: He tries not to antagonize his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他尽量不惹恼他的弟弟。
words.en: To antagonize someone means to cause them to feel hostile or unfriendly towards you.

words.tr: adj. 巡游的；到处走的；兼职的
words.ex: He is a peripatetic teacher who moves from town to town.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位四处奔波的老师，从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: If you have a peripatetic job or way of life, you travel around a lot, living or working in different places for short periods of time.

words.tr: adj. 变化多端的；千变万化的
words.ex: He is protean in his interests, changing often.
words.ex_cn: 他对兴趣变化多端，经常改变。
words.en: Able to change frequently or easily; versatile.

words.tr:
adj. 麻木的；失去知觉的
v. 使麻木；使迟钝
words.ex: His fingers felt numb after being in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他的手指在寒冷中变得麻木。
words.en: If a part of your body is numb, you cannot feel it, usually for a short time.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.tr: adj. 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
words.ex: He drank the tepid water slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地喝着温吞的水。
words.en: Slightly warm; lukewarm. Also, showing little enthusiasm.

words.ex: He lives a sybaritic life with luxury cars and five-star meals.
words.ex_cn: 他过着奢侈的生活，有豪华汽车和五星级酒店的餐食。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sybaritic, you mean that they are fond of luxury and pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 无拘束的；无牵挂的
words.ex: She felt an overwhelming sense of unfettered freedom.
words.ex_cn: 她感到一种无拘无束的自由感。
words.en: If you describe something as unfettered, you mean that it is not controlled or limited by anyone or anything.

words.tr: n. 支柱；中坚；中流砥柱
words.ex: His support has been the mainstay of the project.
words.ex_cn: 他的支持一直是这个项目的支柱。
words.en: If you describe something as the mainstay of a particular thing, you mean that it is the most basic part of it.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.tr: adj. 充满（不愉快事物）的；
words.ex: The journey was fraught with delays.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅程充满了延误。
words.en: If a situation or activity is fraught with problems or risks, it is full of them.

words.ex: He extols the beauty of nature every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天赞美大自然的美。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.ex: The steps must be followed in sequential order.
words.ex_cn: 这些步骤必须按顺序进行。
words.en: Sequential means relating to or following in a sequence.

words.tr: adj. 多种的；各式各样的
words.ex: She has multifarious hobbies, like painting, singing, and gardening.
words.ex_cn: 她有很多不同的爱好，比如绘画、唱歌和园艺。
words.en: If you describe things as multifarious, you mean that they are many and of various types.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.tr: adj. 假情假义的；油腔滑调的
words.ex: His unctuous manner made me uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他油腔滑调的态度让我感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as unctuous, you are critical of them because they seem to be full of praise, kindness, or interest, but in a way that is not sincere.

words.ex: The teacher will enlighten the students about the truth.
words.ex_cn: 老师将向学生们阐明真相。
words.en: To enlighten someone means to give them more knowledge and greater understanding about something.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.ex: The village sent a tribute of grain to the king.
words.ex_cn: 村庄向国王进贡了谷物。
words.en: A tribute is something that you say, do, or make to show your admiration and respect for someone.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；高傲自大的
words.ex: He gave a haughty smile when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品时露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as haughty, you mean that they behave in a proud, unfriendly way, because they think that they are better than other people.

words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: The teacher castigated the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师因学生作弊而严厉批评了他。
words.en: To castigate someone means to criticize or punish them severely.

words.ex: The trip is contingent on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行取决于天气情况。
words.en: A contingent event or situation depends on something else in order to happen or exist.

words.ex: The soldiers were bombarded with cannon fire.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们遭到炮火轰击。
words.en: To bombard someone or something means to attack them continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles. It can also mean to subject someone to a lot of something, such as questions or information.

words.ex: She showed empathy when her friend cried.
words.ex_cn: 当她的朋友哭泣时，她表现出了同感。
words.en: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

words.tr: adj. 明白易懂的；表达清楚的
words.ex: The instructions were written in a perspicuous manner.
words.ex_cn: 说明书写得清晰易懂。
words.en: If you describe something such as an argument or explanation as perspicuous, you mean that it is clear and easy to understand.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；逢迎的；谄媚的
words.ex: He was obsequious to his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他为了得到晋升，对老板阿谀奉承。
words.en: If you describe someone as obsequious, you are criticizing them because they are too eager to help or agree with someone more important than them.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.tr: adj. 沉默寡言的；讳莫如深的
words.ex: He is reticent about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的感受很沉默。
words.en: If you are reticent about something, you are unwilling to talk about it or make your feelings known.

words.tr:
v. 挣扎；深陷困境
n. 比目鱼
words.ex: The fish floundered in the shallow water.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在浅水中挣扎。
words.en: If you flounder, you experience great difficulties and are likely to fail completely.

words.ex: His painting shows great originality.
words.ex_cn: 他的画作展现了极大的独创性。
words.en: The quality of being new and original in a way that is not derived from something else.

words.ex: His virtuosity on the piano amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在钢琴上的精湛技艺让所有人惊叹。
words.en: Great skill in music or another artistic pursuit.

words.tr:
n. 浮标；浮筒
v. 使浮起；支撑；鼓励
words.ex: The buoy floats on the water.
words.ex_cn: 浮标漂浮在水面上。
words.en: A buoy is a floating object that is anchored in water to mark a location, warn of danger, or indicate a navigational channel.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr: adj. 摇摇欲坠的；破烂不堪的
words.ex: The old house was ramshackle and needed repair.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子摇摇欲坠，需要修理。
words.en: A ramshackle building or vehicle is in very bad condition and in danger of falling down.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.ex: The snake constricts its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇缠住它的猎物。
words.en: If something constricts you, it limits your actions so that you cannot do what you want to do.

words.tr: n. 全部；全范围；全音阶；音域
words.ex: The gamut of human emotions was on display during the performance.
words.ex_cn: 表演中展现了人类情感的全部范围。
words.en: The gamut of something is the complete range of things of that kind, or a scale that includes all the notes in a musical octave.

words.ex: He conform to the rules of the school.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守学校的规章制度。
words.en: To conform means to behave in a way that is accepted by most people or to obey a rule, law, or custom.

words.tr: adj. 务实的；实事求是的；
words.ex: He took a pragmatic approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他采取了务实的方法来解决问题。
words.en: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.

words.tr: adj. 应受谴责的；应受指责的；
words.ex: His lying to the teacher was reprehensible.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师撒谎是应受谴责的。
words.en: If you think that someone's behavior is reprehensible, you think that it is very bad or unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.ex: He used subterfuge to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用遁词来避免回答问题。
words.en: Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal.

words.tr: adj. 俗气的；华而不实的；虚有其表的
words.ex: The decoration was meretricious and lacked any real artistic merit.
words.ex_cn: 装饰俗气，缺乏真正的艺术价值。
words.en: Something that is meretricious is attractive in a showy or cheap way, often without having any real value or quality.

words.tr: adj. 若无其事的；不在乎的；冷淡的
words.ex: He was nonchalant about the test result.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试结果表现得漫不经心。
words.en: If you describe someone as nonchalant, you mean that they appear not to worry or care about things and that they seem very calm.

words.ex: The dark clouds are a harbinger of storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预兆。
words.en: A harbinger is something that shows that something is going to happen soon, especially something bad.

words.tr: adj. 坏心眼的；脾脏的；容易发怒的; n. 脾气坏的人
words.ex: His splenetic outbursts were becoming increasingly frequent.
words.ex_cn: 他易怒的爆发变得越来越频繁。
words.en: If you describe someone as splenetic, you mean that they easily become very angry about things and express their anger in an uncontrolled way.

words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.ex: He plays on a collegiate basketball team.
words.ex_cn: 他参加大学篮球队。
words.en: Collegiate means relating to a college or its students.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.ex: He abandoned his car in the snow.
words.ex_cn: 他把车抛弃在雪地里。
words.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.ex: He wore an outlandish hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as outlandish, you mean that it is very unusual, strange, or exaggerated.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: n. 攻击传统观念的人；
words.ex: He is an iconoclast who challenges old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑战传统观念的人。
words.en: An iconoclast is someone who criticizes or attacks cherished beliefs or institutions.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.ex: Rain can affect the crop growth.
words.ex_cn: 雨水会影响作物生长。
words.en: To have an influence on or cause a change in someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 不关心政治的；不重视政治的；与政党无关的
words.ex: He is apolitical and never talks about elections.
words.ex_cn: 他不关心政治，从不谈论选举。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as apolitical, you mean that they are not interested in or involved with politics.

words.ex: The city hosted an exposition last summer.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市去年夏天举办了一场博览会。
words.en: An exposition is a detailed explanation or description of an idea or theory. It can also refer to a large public exhibition of art or trade goods.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；热情洋溢的；
words.ex: The exuberant children ran around the park.
words.ex_cn: 那些精力充沛的孩子们在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: If you are exuberant, you are full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness.

words.ex: The synthesis of ideas helped solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这些想法的综合帮助解决了问题。
words.en: The act of combining different ideas, influences, or objects into a new and coherent whole.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.ex: They tried to subvert the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图颠覆政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: His knowledge is encyclopedic.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识非常渊博。
words.en: Comprehensive in terms of information or knowledge, resembling or suggesting an encyclopedia.

words.ex: The letter 'b' is a consonant.
words.ex_cn: 字母 'b' 是一个辅音。
words.en: A consonant is a speech sound that is articulated with complete or partial closure of the vocal tract.

words.ex: The dissonant notes made the music sound unpleasant.
words.ex_cn: 这些不和谐的音符让音乐听起来很难听。
words.en: If something is dissonant, it is not harmonious or consistent; it may refer to sounds that are harsh and unpleasant or to ideas, opinions, or elements that are in disagreement.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.tr: n. 仓库；贮藏室；存放处；智囊
words.ex: He saves his code in a GitHub repository.
words.ex_cn: 他把代码保存在 GitHub 仓库中。
words.en: A repository is a place where something is stored or can be found.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.tr: adj. 纯粹的；[材] 非合金的
words.ex: He has unalloyed joy when he sees his daughter smile.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到女儿微笑时，他感到纯粹的快乐。
words.en: Not mixed or diluted with any different or extra elements; complete and absolute.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.ex: Please verify your email address.
words.ex_cn: 请核实你的电子邮件地址。
words.en: To verify something means to check or prove that it is true, accurate, or justified.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.tr: adj. 阴暗的；枯燥的；无趣的；
words.ex: The room was dull because the windows were covered.
words.ex_cn: 房间很阴暗，因为窗户被遮住了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as dull, you mean they are not interesting or exciting.

words.ex: The dullard never understood the math lesson.
words.ex_cn: 这个愚笨的人从未理解过数学课。
words.en: A dullard is someone who is considered to be rather slow and not very intelligent.

words.tr: v. 使慌张；使窘迫；使不安
words.ex: The sudden noise disconcerted her.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让她感到不安。
words.en: If something disconcerts you, it makes you feel anxious, confused, or embarrassed.

words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.tr: adj. 错误的；不正确的；不当的；
words.ex: The answer is wrong.
words.ex_cn: 这个答案是错误的。
words.en: If you say there is something wrong, you mean there is something unsatisfactory about the situation, person, or thing you are talking about.

words.tr: adj. 爱开玩笑的；乱引人发笑的
words.ex: He gave a facetious answer when asked about his age.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到年龄时，他给出了一个开玩笑的回答。
words.en: If you say that someone is being facetious, you are criticizing them because they are making humorous remarks or saying things that they do not mean in a situation where they ought to be serious.

words.tr: n. 幽默；开玩笑的倾向；不严肃的态度
words.ex: His facetiousness made the meeting awkward.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻浮态度让会议变得尴尬。
words.en: The quality of being humorous in a way that is not serious or appropriate.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.ex: He judiciously saved his money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他明智地为将来存钱。
words.en: In a way that shows good judgment or sense.

words.tr: adj. 不明智的；不慎重的；浅薄的；不聪明的
words.ex: He made an injudicious decision and lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个不明智的决定，失去了工作。
words.en: If you describe a person or something that they have done as injudicious, you are critical of them because they have shown very poor judgment.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.ex: He showed wariness when talking to strangers.
words.ex_cn: 他和陌生人交谈时表现出谨慎。
words.en: Wariness is the feeling or state of being cautious about possible dangers or problems.

words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.ex: His moralistic tone made the lecture boring.
words.ex_cn: 他那说教的语调让讲座变得无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone as moralistic, you are critical of them for making harsh judgments of other people's behavior based on their own beliefs about what is right and wrong.

words.tr: adj. 无道德观念的；不辨是非的
words.ex: He made an amoral decision to lie for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱做出了一个不道德的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as amoral, you mean that they do not consider whether their behavior is morally right or wrong.

words.tr: v. 使士气低落；使失去斗志
words.ex: The bad news demoralized the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队士气低落。
words.en: If something demoralizes someone, it makes them lose so much confidence in what they are doing that they want to give up.

words.ex: The blood will coagulate if it is left outside the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液如果留在体外，就会凝结。
words.en: If a liquid coagulates, it becomes thick and almost solid.

words.ex: The wound showed coagulation after a few minutes.
words.ex_cn: 几分钟后，伤口出现了凝固。
words.en: Coagulation is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel, forming a clot.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.ex: The crowd was exultant after their team won.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了之后，人群欣喜若狂。
words.en: If you are exultant, you feel very happy and proud because of something that has happened.

words.ex: She wore a chic dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条别致的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as chic, you mean that they are stylish and fashionable.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；华丽的；过分装饰的
words.ex: Her cheeks were florid after running in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 她在寒冷中跑步后，脸颊变得红润。
words.en: If you describe something as florid, you mean that it is complicated and elaborate rather than plain and simple.

words.tr: n. 华丽的风格；繁复的修饰；过分华丽
words.ex: The floridness of his speech impressed the audience.
words.ex_cn: 他言语的华丽风格给观众留下了深刻印象。

words.tr:
adj. 给人良好印象的；令人喜爱的；吸引人的
v. 使预先具有（某种思想）；使…先怀偏见；使产生偏爱；“prepossess”的现在分词
words.ex: She had a prepossessing smile that could light up a room.
words.ex_cn: 她有一个迷人的微笑，能照亮整个房间。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as prepossessing, you mean that they have a quality that makes you like or approve of them immediately.

words.ex: The coach changed his tactic to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 教练改变了战术以赢得比赛。
words.en: A tactic is a method or plan chosen to bring about a desired future, such as achieving a goal or solving a problem.

words.tr: n. 有策略的人；手段高明的人
words.ex: He was known as a brilliant tactician in the field of military strategy.
words.ex_cn: 他是军事战略领域中著名的战术家。
words.en: A tactician is someone who is skilled in planning the best way to achieve something, especially in war or politics.

words.tr: adj. 不机智的；不机敏的；不老练的；不圆滑的；不乖巧的
