words.ex: He was tactless when he criticized her in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前批评她，显得很不妥当。
words.en: If you describe someone as tactless, you think what they say or do is likely to offend other people.

words.ex: The sloth moves very slowly in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 树懒在树上移动得非常慢。
words.en: Sloth is a disinclination to work or exert oneself; laziness, or a slow-moving tropical American mammal that lives in trees.

words.tr: n. 分水岭；集水区；转折点
words.ex: The river forms a watershed between two valleys.
words.ex_cn: 这条河构成了两个山谷之间的分水岭。
words.en: A watershed is an event or period that is important because it represents a big change in how people do or think about something.

words.ex: They will dismantle the old bridge next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将拆除这座旧桥。
words.en: To dismantle something means to take it to pieces.

words.ex: The teacher will delimit the scope of the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师将限定考试的范围。
words.en: If you delimit something, you fix or establish its limits.

words.ex: He told an aphorism about patience.
words.ex_cn: 他说了一句关于耐心的格言。
words.en: An aphorism is a short, clever saying that expresses a general truth or observation.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不着边际的
words.ex: He gave a discursive speech about many topics.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇关于许多主题的散漫演讲。
words.en: If a style of writing or speech is discursive, it includes a lot of information that is not relevant to the main subject.

words.ex: He tried to extenuate his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由减轻自己的错误。
words.en: To lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of (guilt or an offense) by providing partial excuses.

words.tr: v. 大声呵斥；强烈谴责
words.ex: He fulminates against unfair laws.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈谴责不公正的法律。
words.en: To fulminate means to express vehement protest. It can also mean to explode or detonate.

words.ex: His fulmination against the new policy was heard throughout the office.
words.ex_cn: 他对新政策的强烈抗议在整个办公室都能听到。
words.en: A fulmination is a vehement protest or denunciation.

words.ex: The baker used a metal mold to shape the cake.
words.ex_cn: 面包师用一个金属模具来塑造蛋糕。
words.en: A mold is a hollow container used to give shape to molten or hot liquid material when it cools and hardens. It can also refer to a fungus that grows on food or damp surfaces.

words.tr:
n. 跛子；（身体部分或全部肢体）有缺陷的人
v. 使成瘸子；严重损坏（削弱）
words.ex: The cripple walked slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 那个跛子拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: If someone is crippled by an injury, it is so serious that they can never move their body properly again. A cripple is a person who is severely disabled or unable to walk because of damage to their body.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: The plan went awry when the rain started.
words.ex_cn: 当雨下起来时，计划就出差错了。
words.en: If something goes awry, it does not happen in the way that was planned.

words.tr: adj. 糟糕透顶的；恶劣的；卑鄙的
words.ex: He said a vile thing to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友说了句卑鄙的话。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is vile, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant.

words.ex: She wears modish clothes every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天穿时髦的衣服。
words.en: If something is modish, it is fashionable and modern.

words.ex: The country supports pluralism in religion and culture.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家支持宗教和文化的多元主义。
words.en: Pluralism is a situation in which people of different social classes, religions, races, etc., are together in a society but continue to have their different traditions and interests.

words.ex: This city is pluralistic, with many cultures living together.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市是多元化的，许多文化共同生活在一起。
words.en: Relating to or advocating a system in which two or more states, groups, principles, sources of authority, etc., coexist.

words.ex: The children's laughter brought gaiety to the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们的笑声为派对带来了欢乐。
words.en: Gaiety is a feeling, attitude, or atmosphere of liveliness and fun.

words.tr:
n. 协约；契约
v. 订立契约
words.ex: They made a covenant to always help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们立下契约，永远互相帮助。
words.en: A covenant is a formal agreement or promise between two or more people, often involving legal obligations.

words.tr:
n. 箔；陪衬物
v. 阻止；挫败
words.ex: He used foil to wrap the sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他用锡纸包住了三明治。
words.en: To prevent someone from succeeding in their plans or intentions, especially by doing something clever or unexpected.

words.ex: The law is outside the purview of the local police.
words.ex_cn: 这法律不在当地警察的职权范围内。
words.en: The purview of something is the range of its authority, influence, or knowledge.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.tr: n. 闯入者；干涉他人事务者
words.ex: The interloper walked into the meeting without permission.
words.ex_cn: 那个闯入者未经允许走进了会议。
words.en: An interloper is someone who becomes involved in a situation or place where they are not wanted or are considered not to belong.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.ex: She tried to compartmentalize her work and personal life.
words.ex_cn: 她试图将工作和私人生活分开。
words.en: To compartmentalize something means to divide it into separate sections or categories.

words.tr: adj. 确定性的；命运注定论的
words.ex: The machine works in a deterministic way.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器以确定的方式运行。
words.en: Relating to the philosophical doctrine that all events, including human action, are ultimately determined by causes external to the will.

words.tr: v. 过度确定；使...具有过多的决定因素
words.ex: The system is overdetermined because there are more equations than unknowns.
words.ex_cn: 这个方程组被过度确定，因为方程的数量比未知数多。

words.tr: adj. 未成熟的；无处世经验的；乳臭未干的
words.ex: The new recruits were callow and inexperienced.
words.ex_cn: 新兵们年轻而无经验。
words.en: If you describe someone as callow, you mean that they are inexperienced and immature.

words.ex: His callowness was evident in his naive decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他缺乏经验在他天真的决定中显而易见。
words.en: The state of being immature or inexperienced.

words.tr: adj. 休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的
words.ex: The volcano is dormant now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Something that is dormant is not active or growing but has the ability to be active at a later time.

words.ex: He made an animadversion on his friend's poor choice.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的糟糕选择提出了批评。
words.en: A critical or censorious remark or comment.

words.tr:
adj. 乱花钱的；挥霍的
n. 浪费金钱的人；挥金如土的人
words.ex: He is a spendthrift who buys things he doesn't need.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乱花钱的人，买很多不需要的东西。
words.en: A spendthrift is someone who spends money in an extravagant, irresponsible way.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.tr:
n. 有志者；立志…的人
adj. 有野心的；有抱负的
words.ex: He is an aspirant for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他是这份工作的求职者。
words.en: An aspirant is someone who is ambitious and eager to achieve a particular goal or position.

words.ex: His aspiration is to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他的渴望是成为一名医生。
words.en: A strong desire to achieve something high or great.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.ex: The forest looked primeval and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林看起来远古而未被破坏。
words.en: relating to the earliest ages of the world or the universe; ancient or prehistoric.

words.tr: n. 底层；下层土壤地基
words.ex: The rock layer is the substratum of the soil.
words.ex_cn: 岩石层是土壤的基底。
words.en: A substratum is an underlying layer or substance, especially one that forms a foundation or basis.

words.ex: The priest was known as an oracle who spoke for the gods.
words.ex_cn: 这位祭司被称为传达神谕的传神谕者。
words.en: An oracle is a person or thing considered to provide wise and insightful guidance or prophetic predictions, often through divine inspiration.

words.ex: His oracular words confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他那神秘莫测的话语让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as oracular, you mean that it is like an oracle, especially because it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain without oxygen was a great feat.
words.ex_cn: 在不吸氧的情况下爬山是一项伟大的壮举。
words.en: A feat is an act or achievement that shows great courage, skill, or strength.

words.tr: v. 删去（书籍中不合适之处）
words.ex: The teacher expurgated the old book to remove bad words.
words.ex_cn: 老师删改了这本旧书，去掉了不好的词语。
words.en: To remove material that is considered improper or offensive from (a book, movie, etc.).

words.ex: The old man is frail and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人瘦弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: Someone who is frail is not very strong or healthy.

words.tr: adj. 天生的；先天的；天赋的
words.ex: He has an inborn talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 他天生就有音乐才能。
words.en: An inborn quality or ability is one that you have had naturally since birth.

words.tr: adj. 基督教大联合的；普世的；普遍的
words.ex: The ecumenical movement seeks to promote unity among all Christian churches.
words.ex_cn: 普世运动旨在促进所有基督教会之间的团结。
words.en: Ecumenical is used to describe something that is concerned with promoting unity among the world's different Christian churches.

words.tr: adj. 平民的；卑贱的；卑鄙的；不光彩的
words.ex: He came from an ignoble family, but worked hard to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他出身于平民家庭，但努力工作以取得成功。
words.en: If you describe something as ignoble, you mean that it is bad and something to be ashamed of.

words.ex: The number of stars in the sky is incalculable.
words.ex_cn: 天空中的星星数量是无数的。
words.en: If something is incalculable, it cannot be calculated or measured because it is so great.

words.ex: He tries to attune his ears to the quiet sound.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让自己的耳朵适应那细微的声音。
words.en: If you attune your ear or your senses to something, you become used to it and can recognize it or understand it.

words.tr: v. 使惊呆；使惊愕；使神志不清
words.ex: The sudden noise stupefied everyone.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: To stupefy someone means to make them unable to think clearly or to be surprised or shocked.

words.ex: He stared in stupefaction at the sudden crash.
words.ex_cn: 他震惊地盯着突如其来的撞击声。
words.en: The state of being stupefied; astonishment.

words.ex: The linguist analyzed the English corpus to find common phrases.
words.ex_cn: 语言学家分析了英语语料库以寻找常用短语。
words.en: A corpus is a large collection of written or spoken texts that is used for language research.

words.ex: Alzheimer's is a degenerative disease.
words.ex_cn: 阿尔茨海默病是一种衰退性疾病。
words.en: A degenerative disease or condition is one that gradually gets worse.

words.ex: The degeneracy of society is often reflected in its art.
words.ex_cn: 社会的堕落常常在艺术中得到反映。
words.en: Degeneracy refers to the state of being degenerate, especially in a moral sense, or the process of becoming degenerate.

words.ex: The nefarious thief stole money from the poor.
words.ex_cn: 那个极坏的贼从穷人那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as nefarious, you mean that it is wicked and immoral.

words.ex: The nefariousness of his actions shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他行为的邪恶让所有人都感到震惊。

words.ex: The meeting felt interminable.
words.ex_cn: 这场会议感觉没完没了。
words.en: If you describe something as interminable, you are emphasizing that it continues for a very long time and indicating that you find it boring or annoying.

words.tr:
int. 呸；嘘
n. 嘘声
v. 发出嘘声
words.ex: The crowd gave a loud boo when the player missed the goal.
words.ex_cn: 当球员错失进球时，观众发出了大声的嘘声。
words.en: If you boo a speaker or performer, you shout 'boo' or make other loud sounds to indicate that you do not like them, their opinions, or their performance.

words.tr: adj. 密封的；不透气的；与外界隔绝的
words.ex: The container was hermetic to ensure the contents stayed fresh.
words.ex_cn: 这个容器是密封的，以确保内容物保持新鲜。
words.en: If something is hermetic, it is so tightly sealed that no air can get in or out.

words.ex: He bought some miscellaneous items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店里买了一些各种各样的东西。
words.en: Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.

words.ex: The track is elliptical in shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个跑道是椭圆形的。
words.en: Something that is elliptical has the shape of an ellipse or is characterized by the omission of words that are understood to be obvious.

words.ex: He will enumerate the steps clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地列出这些步骤。
words.en: To enumerate means to mention things one by one.

words.ex: He gave an enumeration of all the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他列出了书架上所有的书。
words.en: The act of naming things one by one or a list of items.

words.ex: His lapse in judgment caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: A lapse is a temporary failure or a slight error, or the process by which something gradually passes into a different state, especially a worse one.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.tr: adj. 推定的；假定的；一般认为的
words.ex: The putative father was asked to take a DNA test.
words.ex_cn: 被推定的父亲被要求做DNA测试。
words.en: Generally believed to be or to exist, but not proved to be so.

words.tr:
n. 猛跌；衰退；萧条期
v. 急剧下降；暴跌；重重地坐下（或倒下）
words.ex: The company's sales went into a slump last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月，这家公司的销售额下滑了。
words.en: If something such as the value of something slumps, it falls suddenly and by a large amount.

words.tr:
n. 猫叫春声
v. 发出猫叫春一般的声音
words.ex: The cats were caterwauling all night long.
words.ex_cn: 这些猫整晚都在号叫。
words.en: to make a shrill, discordant sound like that of a cat in heat; to complain loudly

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.ex: His speech was full of invective against his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了对对手的辱骂。
words.en: Invective is rude and unpleasant things that people shout at someone they hate or are angry with.

words.tr: adj. 先入为主的； v. “preconceive”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He had a preconceived idea that all dogs are dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个先入为主的观念，认为所有狗都危险。
words.en: If you have preconceived ideas about something, you have already formed an opinion about it before you have enough information or experience.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.tr: adj. 插曲般的；由松散片段组成的；不定期发生的；
words.ex: The movie has an episodic structure, with each scene telling a small story.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有插曲般的结构，每个场景讲述一个小故事。
words.en: An episodic piece of writing or film consists of a series of separate events or episodes that are linked together.

words.ex: He is conversant with basic math.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉基础数学。
words.en: If you are conversant with something, you are familiar with it and able to deal with it.

words.tr: n. 祸根；致命伤；烦扰之源；
words.ex: Smoking is the bane of his health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是他健康的祸根。
words.en: Something that causes misery or death.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；有毒的；使人苦恼的
words.ex: The baneful effect of pollution harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 污染的有害影响损害了环境。
words.en: Something that is baneful is extremely harmful or destructive.

words.tr: n. 赞扬；称赞；荣誉；奖状
words.ex: He received a commendation for his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他因努力工作而获得了表扬。
words.en: A commendation is a formal statement or speech that praises someone for something they have done.

words.ex: The teacher commends her for working hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师表扬她学习努力。
words.en: If you commend someone or something, you praise them formally.

words.ex: He tried to gild the old box with gold paint.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用金漆把旧盒子镀金。
words.en: To cover something with a thin layer of gold or to make something seem more attractive or valuable than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 柔软的；灵活的；思维敏捷的
words.ex: The yoga teacher has supple legs.
words.ex_cn: 瑜伽老师腿很柔软。
words.en: A supple object or material bends or changes shape easily without breaking or cracking.

words.ex: Yoga improves suppleness in the body.
words.ex_cn: 瑜伽能增强身体的柔韧性。
words.en: The quality of being able to bend and move easily and gracefully.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.ex: The dark clouds betoken a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着暴风雨的来临。
words.en: If something betokens something else, it is a sign of it.

words.tr: adj. 说教的；过分认真的；简洁的；富于警句的
words.ex: His speech was full of sententious remarks.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了简洁精炼的格言。
words.en: If you describe someone as sententious, you mean that they try to appear wise, intelligent, and moral, but in a way that is often perceived as pompous or insincere.

words.ex: Some people follow that cult blindly.
words.ex_cn: 有些人盲目追随那个狂热崇拜。
words.en: A cult is a group of people who have extreme admiration for a particular person, idea, or thing, often following unusual or extreme practices or beliefs.

words.tr:
n. 定量；配给量
v. 配给；定量供应
words.ex: He gets a small ration of food each day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天得到少量的食物配给。
words.en: A ration is a fixed amount of something such as food or fuel that is officially allowed to each person, especially when there is not enough of it available.

words.ex: I reckon it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我认为明天会下雨。
words.en: If you reckon that something is true, you think that it is true.

words.tr: n. 势利小人；谄上欺下的人；恃才傲物的人
words.ex: He acts like a snob because he only likes expensive things.
words.ex_cn: 他只喜欢昂贵的东西，所以表现得像个势利小人。
words.en: A snob is someone who thinks they are better than other people because they are more intelligent, more cultured, or of a higher social class.

words.tr: adj. 势利的；谄上欺下的
words.ex: He is snobbish and ignores people who are not rich.
words.ex_cn: 他很势利，不理睬不富有的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as snobbish, you disapprove of them because they are too proud of their social status, intelligence, or taste.

words.ex: He adulterates milk with water to make more money.
words.ex_cn: 他往牛奶里加水以赚更多钱。
words.en: To make something poorer in quality by adding another substance to it.

words.tr: n. 迷信；迷信观念（或思想）；
words.ex: He avoids walking under ladders because of superstition.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迷信而不愿从梯子下走过。
words.en: A superstition is a belief or practice resulting from ignorance, fear of the unknown, trust in magic or chance, or a false conception of causation.

words.tr: adj. 迷信的；有迷信观念的
words.ex: He is superstitious about walking under ladders.
words.ex_cn: 他迷信地认为走过梯子下面会带来厄运。
words.en: Having or showing a belief in superstitions.

words.ex: He refuses to accept the dogma of the church.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝接受教会的教条。
words.en: A principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true.

words.tr: adj. 教条的；武断的；固执己见的
words.ex: He is dogmatical about his beliefs and never listens to others.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的信念非常固执，从不听别人的意见。

words.ex: The company will compensate you for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 公司会因延误而补偿你。
words.en: If you compensate for a lack of something or for something you have done wrong, you do something to show that you are sorry or that you are trying to make things better.

words.ex: He got compensatory pay for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了补偿性工资。
words.en: Compensatory is used to describe something that is intended to compensate for something else, especially loss or damage.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；丑恶可耻的；公然的
words.ex: He made a flagrant mistake during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中犯了一个明显的错误。
words.en: If you describe an action as flagrant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way and is intended to shock or offend people.

words.tr: adj. 再三要求的；纠缠不休的
words.ex: He was importunate in asking for money.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地要求给钱。
words.en: persistent to the point of annoyance

words.tr:
v. 避开；躲避
n. 躲避；诡计
words.ex: He dodged the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速躲开了球。
words.en: If you dodge, you move quickly, often to avoid being hit, caught, or seen.

words.ex: He gave a sardonic smile when she told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当她说出真相时，他露出了讽刺的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as sardonic, you mean they are mocking or scornful in a humorous way.

words.tr: v. 装入胶囊；压缩；简述；概括
words.ex: The pharmacist encapsulate the medicine into small capsules.
words.ex_cn: 药剂师把药物装入小胶囊中。
words.en: To encapsulate something means to express or show the most important facts about it in a very short and clear form.

words.ex: The company uses plastic encapsulation for the electronic parts.
words.ex_cn: 公司用塑料包装电子元件。
words.en: The process of enclosing something in or as if in a capsule; a summary or condensation.

words.tr: v. 使麻痹；使瘫痪；使无效；使停止活动
words.ex: The accident paralyzed his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿瘫痪了。
words.en: If someone is paralyzed by an accident or an illness, they have no feeling in their body, or in part of their body, and are unable to move.

words.tr:
v. 沉思
n. （作家、画家等的）灵感；缪斯
words.ex: He often muses about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他常常沉思生命的意义。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the Muses are the goddesses of the inspiration of literature, science and the arts. As a verb, to muse means to think about something carefully and for a long time.

words.tr:
adj. 沉思的；冥想的
n. 沉思；冥想
v. 沉思；默想；“muse”的现在分词
words.ex: He was musing about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他正在沉思生命的意义。
words.en: If you are musing about something, you are thinking about it in a deep and serious way.

words.tr: adj. 可控告的；可提起诉讼的
words.ex: The email contained actionable evidence of fraud.
words.ex_cn: 这封邮件包含了可被起诉的欺诈证据。
words.en: Capable of being acted upon or used as a basis for action.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；肿大；使扩张；使膨胀；
words.ex: The balloon distend when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充满空气时会膨胀。
words.en: If a part of your body distends or if you distend it, it becomes larger or swollen, often because of pressure from inside.

words.ex: He tried to inveigle her into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗她借钱给他。
words.en: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；易懂的
words.ex: The water in the mountain stream was so pellucid that we could see the fish swimming.
words.ex_cn: 山间溪流中的水如此清澈，我们可以看到鱼儿在游动。
words.en: If something is pellucid, it is very clear and easy to understand.

words.ex: The new car outstrips the old one in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车在速度上超过了旧车。
words.en: To outstrip means to go faster or to do better than someone or something else.

words.ex: They believed there was a conspiracy to hide the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他们相信有人密谋隐瞒真相。
words.en: A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group of people to do something harmful or illegal.

words.tr: n. 阴谋家；密谋者；谋反者
words.ex: The conspirator was arrested for plotting against the government.
words.ex_cn: 这名阴谋者因密谋反对政府而被捕。
words.en: A conspirator is a person who is involved in a conspiracy.

words.ex: He gave a conspiratorial whisper.
words.ex_cn: 他低声说了句神秘的话。
words.en: Relating to or suggestive of a conspiracy.

words.ex: The teacher asked students to annotate the text with notes.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们在文本上做注释。
words.en: To add notes or comments to a text or diagram, providing explanation or criticism.

words.ex: The annotator added helpful notes to the manuscript.
words.ex_cn: 注释者在手稿上添加了有用的笔记。
words.en: An annotator is a person who writes explanatory or critical notes on a text.

words.tr:
n. 吹牛者；自夸者
adj. 吹牛的
words.ex: He is a braggart who always talks about his wins.
words.ex_cn: 他是个自吹自擂的人，总是谈论自己的胜利。
words.en: A braggart is someone who boasts about their achievements or possessions in a way that is annoying to others.

words.ex: He talks with braggadocio about his small wins.
words.ex_cn: 他夸夸其谈地谈论自己微小的胜利。
words.en: Braggadocio refers to boastful or arrogant behavior; bragging.

words.tr: adj. 脱节的；不连贯的； v. “disjoint”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His speech was disjointed and hard to follow.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲脱节，难以理解。
words.en: If you describe something such as a speech or piece of writing as disjointed, you mean that it is not well organized or easy to follow, often because it contains ideas that are not connected or arranged in a logical order.

words.tr:
n. 瘟疫；疫病；
v. 困扰；折磨；
words.ex: The plague killed many people in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 瘟疫在中世纪的欧洲杀死了许多人。
words.en: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills a lot of people. It can also refer to a large number of insects or animals that cause damage or are a nuisance.

words.tr: adj. 无情的；冷酷的；残忍的；
words.ex: The ruthless boss fired employees without warning.
words.ex_cn: 这位无情的老板未经警告就解雇了员工。
words.en: If you say that someone is ruthless, you mean that you disapprove of them because they are very harsh or cruel, and will do anything that is necessary to achieve what they want.

words.tr: adv. 残忍地；冷酷地；无情地
words.ex: He ruthlessly fired the employee.
words.ex_cn: 他无情地解雇了那位员工。
words.en: If someone is ruthless, they are determined to get what they want and do not care if they hurt other people.

words.tr:
v. 放逐到孤岛上
n. 孤立的人；褐红色；栗色
adj. 褐红色的；栗色的
words.ex: The ship was marooned on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船被困在了一个小岛上。
words.en: Maroon is used to describe a dark reddish-brown color. As a verb, it means to leave someone in a place from which they cannot escape, especially on a deserted island.

words.ex: The rain stymied our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨水阻碍了我们去远足的计划。
words.en: To stymie someone or something means to prevent them from achieving their aims.

words.tr: adj. 日间活动的；昼行性的
words.ex: The bird sings during diurnal hours.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟在白天活动时鸣叫。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in a 24-hour period; daily.

words.ex: He tweaked the volume to make it louder.
words.ex_cn: 他微调了音量，让它更大声。
words.en: To tweak something means to make a small change to it in order to improve it or make it work better.

words.ex: The fairy tale features a dwarf who lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个童话故事中有一个住在小房子里的侏儒。
words.en: A dwarf is a person, animal, or plant that is much smaller than the usual size of its species. As a verb, to dwarf means to make someone or something seem small or insignificant in comparison.

words.ex: He tries to rive the wood with an axe.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用斧头劈开木头。
words.en: To tear or split apart violently.

words.tr: adj. 悦耳的；动听的；和谐的
words.ex: The singer's voice is euphonious.
words.ex_cn: 这位歌手的声音悦耳动听。
words.en: Something that is euphonious has a pleasant sound.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.tr: adj. 爱咬人的；爱喝叱的；脾气暴躁的
words.ex: The dog was snappish when strangers came near.
words.ex_cn: 当陌生人靠近时，这只狗爱咬人。
words.en: If someone is snappish, they speak to people in a sharp, unfriendly way.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.tr: adj. 可继承的；可传让的
words.ex: The estate is heritable and can be passed down to future generations.
words.ex_cn: 这个庄园是可继承的，可以传给后代。
words.en: Capable of being inherited or passed down from one generation to the next.

words.tr: adj. 镇定自若的；临危不乱的
words.ex: She remained unflappable even under intense pressure.
words.ex_cn: 即使在巨大的压力下，她依然保持镇定。
words.en: If you describe someone as unflappable, you mean that they stay calm in difficult or worrying situations.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是必须的。
words.en: If something is compulsory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.ex: The lush grass looked green after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，葱翠的草地显得格外绿。
words.en: A lush area has a lot of green, healthy plants, grass, and trees.

words.tr: adj. 过分劳累的；过度兴奋的；过分紧张的
words.ex: He felt overwrought after working 16 hours straight.
words.ex_cn: 他连续工作了16个小时，感到精疲力尽。
words.en: If someone is overwrought, they are very upset and are not thinking or behaving calmly or sensibly.

words.ex: He averred that he was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他断言自己是无辜的。
words.en: To state or assert to be the case.

words.ex: He will not forsake his family.
words.ex_cn: 他不会抛弃他的家人。
words.en: If you forsake someone, you leave them when you should have stayed, or you stop helping them or looking after them.

words.tr: v. 诽谤；中伤；损毁名誉
words.ex: He tried to defame his rival with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用虚假的故事诋毁他的竞争对手。
words.en: To defame someone means to damage their reputation by saying or writing bad things about them that are not true.

words.ex: He sued him for defamation after the false story was published.
words.ex_cn: 虚假报道发布后，他因诽谤起诉了他。
words.en: Defamation is the act of damaging someone's good reputation by saying or writing bad things about them that are not true.

words.tr:
adj. 悲痛的；令人伤心的
v. 耙地；折磨；使愁苦；“harrow”的现在分词
words.ex: The harrowing story of the survivors left a deep impression on everyone.
words.ex_cn: 幸存者的悲惨故事给每个人留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: Causing feelings of deep distress or anguish.

words.ex: This food contains a harmless additive for flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物含有用于调味的无害添加物。
words.en: An additive is a substance which is added in small amounts to something else in order to improve it, preserve it, or make it more effective.

words.tr: n. 博学者；学识渊博的人；
words.ex: Leonardo da Vinci was a polymath who excelled in art, science, and engineering.
words.ex_cn: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇是一位博学者，在艺术、科学和工程方面都很出色。
words.en: A polymath is a person who knows a lot about many different subjects.

words.tr: adj. 博学的；通晓多门学科的；具备多方面知识的
words.ex: He is a polymathic genius who understands science, art, and music.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位博学的天才，懂科学、艺术和音乐。
words.en: Having knowledge across many different subjects.

words.ex: He gave a synopsis of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他简要介绍了这部电影。
words.en: A synopsis is a brief summary or general survey of something.

words.ex: The complexity of the instructions bemused the students.
words.ex_cn: 指令的复杂性让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: If something bemuses you, it puzzles or confuses you.

words.ex: The quiet music was a prelude to the loud concert.
words.ex_cn: 轻柔的音乐是盛大音乐会的前奏。
words.en: A prelude is an introductory piece of music, event, or action that comes before a more important one.

words.tr:
n. 叛徒；变节者；叛教者
adj. 背叛的；变节的
v. 背叛
words.ex: He is a renegade who left the team suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个突然离开团队的叛徒。
words.en: A renegade is a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles.

words.tr: adj. 灾难性的；大变动的
words.ex: The volcano erupted in a cataclysmic explosion.
words.ex_cn: 火山以一场灾难性的爆炸喷发了。
words.en: A cataclysmic event is one that causes great damage or suffering.

words.ex: The army will not capitulate to the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 军队不会向敌人投降。
words.en: If you capitulate, you stop resisting and do what someone else wants you to do.

words.tr: n. （有条件的）投降；投降条约
words.ex: The capitulation of the city marked the end of the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的投降标志着战争的结束。
words.en: The act of surrendering or yielding under specified conditions; a document containing the terms of surrender.

words.tr: adj. 头脑冷静的；清醒的
words.ex: She is always levelheaded in a crisis.
words.ex_cn: 她在危机中总是保持冷静。
words.en: If you describe a person as levelheaded, you mean that they are calm and sensible even in difficult situations.

words.tr: v. 神化；把…奉若神明；崇拜
words.ex: They deify their ancient heroes.
words.ex_cn: 他们崇拜自己的古代英雄。
words.en: To treat someone or something as a god or goddess, or to consider them as if they were divine.

words.ex: The ancient people worshipped a sun deity.
words.ex_cn: 古人崇拜太阳神。
words.en: A deity is a god or goddess, or anything revered as divine.

words.tr: adj. 闪烁的；才气横溢的; v. 闪耀（scintillate 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: The sky was filled with scintillating stars.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中满是闪烁的星星。
words.en: If you say that someone is scintillating, you mean that they are lively, intelligent, and amusing.

words.ex: The water in the swamp is brackish.
words.ex_cn: 沼泽里的水是微咸的。
words.en: Brackish water is slightly salty, as is the mixture of river water and seawater in estuaries.

words.ex: He loves studying jurisprudence to understand laws better.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢学习法学以更好地理解法律。
words.en: Jurisprudence is the study of law and the principles on which law is based.

words.ex: She has a slender figure.
words.ex_cn: 她身材苗条。
words.en: Someone or something that is slender is thin and graceful.

words.ex: The slenderness of the tree made it look delicate.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的纤细让它看起来很纤弱。
words.en: The quality of being slender; a thin and graceful physical form.

words.tr: adj. 肥沃的；有繁殖力的；多产的；富饶的；
words.ex: The fertile land grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地长满了各种作物。
words.en: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

words.ex: The doctor checked her fertility to help her get pregnant.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了她的生育力，以帮助她怀孕。
words.en: Fertility refers to the ability to produce offspring or to the quality of being fertile, especially in terms of soil or land.

words.ex: Bees help to fertilize flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂帮助花朵受精。
words.en: To fertilize means to make soil or land more fertile or productive by adding substances to it, or to cause an egg, female animal, or plant to develop a new individual by introducing male reproductive material.

words.ex: He gets a free lunch as a perquisite.
words.ex_cn: 他得到免费午餐作为福利。
words.en: A perquisite is a benefit which one enjoys or is entitled to on account of one's job or position.

words.tr: adj. 自由的；不受约束的
words.ex: She felt an untrammeled sense of freedom while hiking in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中徒步时感受到了一种无拘无束的自由感。
words.en: Not limited or restricted; free.

words.ex: The old house came with many appurtenances, including a large garden and a barn.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子附带了许多附属物，包括一个大花园和一个谷仓。
words.en: An appurtenance is a piece of property that is considered to be a part of a larger property and is transferred with it.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

words.ex: The rain rendered the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 雨水使道路变得滑溜。
words.en: To render something means to cause it to become or to provide it. It can also mean to express or translate something.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: The law has a loophole that lets companies avoid taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律有一个漏洞，让公司可以避税。
words.en: A loophole is a small mistake in a law or set of rules which allows people to do something that would otherwise be illegal or not allowed.

words.tr: adj. 统一的；单一的；中央集权制的
words.ex: The team worked in a unitary way to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队以统一的方式合作完成了项目。
words.en: A unitary system or organization is one in which all the parts are under the control of one central authority.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.ex: The king believed in absolutism and made all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 国王相信绝对主义，并制定所有规则。
words.en: Absolutism is a political theory and form of government where unlimited, complete power is held by a centralized sovereign individual, with no checks or balances from any other part of the nation or government.

words.ex: He is an absolutist who believes in total control.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个相信绝对控制的专制主义者。
words.en: An absolutist is someone who believes in absolute principles in political, philosophical, or theological matters.

words.tr: v. 改变（说法、决定等）；原路返回；倒回
words.ex: The algorithm backtracks when it encounters a dead end.
words.ex_cn: 该算法在遇到死胡同时会回溯。
words.en: To go back over the course by which one has come.

words.tr:
adj. 教条（主义）的；空谈理论的
n. 教条主义者；空论家
words.ex: He is a doctrinaire who always follows rules strictly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个教条主义者，总是严格遵守规则。
words.en: If you say that someone is doctrinaire, you are criticizing them for following fixed theories or principles rather than considering practical problems.

words.ex: They tried to indoctrinate the children with their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图用他们的信仰灌输孩子们。
words.en: To indoctrinate someone means to teach them a particular belief or set of beliefs, especially with the aim of making them accept it without questioning it.

words.tr: adj. 矫揉造作的；不自然的；守规矩的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: Her mannered speech was hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 她矫揉造作的言辞让人难以理解。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or a work of art as mannered, you dislike it because it is elaborate or formal, and therefore seems false or artificial.

words.tr: n. 警告；防止误解的说明；注意事项
words.ex: He gave me a warning, a caveat, before I signed the contract.
words.ex_cn: 我在签署合同之前，他给了我一个警告，一个注意事项。
words.en: A caveat is a warning of a specific limitation of something such as information or an agreement.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；优厚的； 大方的
words.ex: He gave a munificent donation to the school.
words.ex_cn: 他向学校捐赠了一笔慷慨的款项。
words.en: If you describe someone as munificent, you mean that they are very generous, often in the form of giving money or gifts.

words.tr: n. 宽宏大量；慷慨给与
words.ex: Her munificence in donating to charity is well known.
words.ex_cn: 她对慈善机构的慷慨捐赠是众所周知的。
words.en: Munificence is the quality of being extremely generous.

words.tr:
n. 泥潭；泥沼；困境
v. 使陷进泥坑里
words.ex: The car got stuck in the mire.
words.ex_cn: 汽车陷在泥沼里了。
words.en: Mire refers to an area of wet, soggy ground or a difficult situation from which it is hard to extricate oneself.

words.ex: He composes music in his spare time.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间创作音乐。
words.en: To compose something means to make it by combining parts or elements.

words.ex: He kept his composure during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中保持了冷静。
words.en: The state of being calm and in control of your emotions.

words.ex: He had no recourse but to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他别无依靠，只能求助。
words.en: If you have recourse to a particular course of action, you use it when you are in a difficult situation or when you need to achieve something.

words.ex: The acme of his career was winning the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的顶点是获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: The highest point of achievement or excellence.

words.tr: v. 预先假定；预料；以…为先决条件
words.ex: He presupposes that everyone likes coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他假设每个人都喜欢咖啡。
words.en: If one thing presupposes another, the first thing cannot be true or exist unless the second thing is true or exists.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.tr:
v. 艰难地行走；吃力地行进
n. 劳苦；沉重的脚步（声）
words.ex: He plodded through the snow with heavy boots.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着沉重的靴子艰难地在雪地中行走。
words.en: To plod means to walk slowly with heavy steps, especially because you are tired or working hard. It can also mean to work slowly and steadily at something, especially something that is boring or difficult.

words.tr: adj. 不畏缩的；不退缩的
words.ex: He gave an unflinching answer to the tough question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了毫不动摇的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as unflinching, you mean that they are not deterred from a course of action by difficulty or danger, and they remain determined and resolute.

words.ex: It was just a ploy to get attention.
words.ex_cn: 那只是为了引起注意的一个策略。
words.en: A ploy is a cunning plan or action designed to turn a situation to one's own advantage.

words.ex: He recoiled when he saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到蛇时，他退缩了。
words.en: If something makes you recoil, you move your body quickly away from it because it frightens, offends, or hurts you.

words.tr: adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑剔的
words.ex: He made a captious comment about the small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对一个小错误发表了挑剔的评论。
words.en: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.

words.tr:
v. 注意；留心
n. 注意；留心
words.ex: He did not heed the warning.
words.ex_cn: 他没有理会那个警告。
words.en: If you heed someone's advice or warning, you pay attention to it and do what they suggest.

words.tr: adj. 密切注意的；深切留心的
words.ex: He remained heedful of the teacher's instructions throughout the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 在整个实验过程中，他始终注意老师的指示。
words.en: If you are heedful of something, you pay careful attention to it.

words.tr: adv. 不注意地，掉以轻心地
words.ex: He drove heedlessly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他毫不在意地开车穿过街道。
words.en: If someone does something heedlessly, they do it without paying attention to the possible consequences.

words.ex: She wears a gold earring.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一只金耳环。
words.en: An earring is a piece of jewelry that you attach to your ear.

words.tr: adj. 轻飘的；缥缈的；虚空的；精致的；
words.ex: The ethereal scarf floated gently in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 那条轻飘的围巾在风中轻轻飘动。
words.en: Something that is ethereal is extremely delicate and light in a way that seems not to be of this world.

words.tr: adj. 乏味的；无味的；枯燥的
words.ex: The movie was vapid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影乏味又无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vapid, you are criticizing them because they are dull and uninteresting.

words.tr: n. 平淡无味；乏味；空洞
words.ex: The movie's plot was full of vapidity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节毫无趣味。

words.tr: v. 使（植物）因缺乏光照而变得苍白、细弱；使苍白；使虚弱
words.ex: The plant etiolates in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 植物在黑暗中变得黄而细长。
words.en: To weaken or reduce the strength or vitality of something, often through neglect.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.tr:
adj. 丧失近亲的；丧失密友的
v. 夺去；使丧失；“bereave”的过去式
words.ex: The bereaved mother cried quietly at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 这位失去孩子的母亲在葬礼上静静地哭泣。
words.en: If someone is bereaved, a relative or close friend has just died.

words.tr: v. 使混乱；使狼狈；迷惑
words.ex: The complex instructions flummoxed the new employee.
words.ex_cn: 复杂的指示让新员工感到困惑。
words.en: To flummox someone means to confuse them so much that they do not know what to do.

words.tr:
v. 声称；意指；意味着
n. 意义；要旨；主要意思
words.ex: The letter purports to be from the president.
words.ex_cn: 这封信声称是总统写的。
words.en: If something purports to be a particular thing or to do a particular thing, it claims or appears to be that thing or to do that thing, even though this may not be the case.

words.ex: He detests eating broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌吃西兰花。
words.en: If you detest something, you dislike it intensely.

words.tr: n. 憎恶，厌恶的人，嫌恶
words.ex: He feels detestation for dishonest people.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶不诚实的人。
words.en: A feeling of intense dislike or hatred.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: His belligerence made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他的好斗态度让所有人都感到不舒服。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.tr:
n. 树液；
v. 使逐渐耗竭；使削弱；
words.ex: The tree releases sap in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在春天流出树液。
words.en: Sap is the watery fluid that circulates in the vascular system of a plant, carrying nutrients and sugars. It can also refer to the vitality or energy of a person or thing.

words.ex: The speech embolden the protesters to speak up.
words.ex_cn: 这次演讲鼓舞了抗议者们发声。
words.en: To embolden someone means to make them feel more confident or courageous.

words.tr: adj. 注意的；专心的；留心的；关心的
words.ex: The child is attentive in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子上课很专心。
words.en: If you are attentive, you are paying close attention to what is being said or done.

words.tr: adj. 松散; 粗疏; 不注意的; 疏忽的，漫不经心的
words.ex: He was inattentive during the lesson and missed the key points.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时心不在焉，错过了重点。
words.en: If someone is inattentive, they are not paying attention to something and so they may not notice it or may not do it properly.

words.tr: adj. 人为的；人类起源的
words.ex: The increase in greenhouse gases is largely anthropogenic.
words.ex_cn: 温室气体增加主要是人为的。
words.en: Anthropogenic refers to environmental pollution and pollutants originating in human activity.

words.ex: Anthropocentrism often leads to the neglect of environmental conservation.
words.ex_cn: n. 人类中心主义常常导致对环境保护的忽视。
words.en: Anthropocentrism is the belief that human beings are the central or most significant entities in the world, often considering human needs and interests as more important than those of other species or the environment.

words.tr: adj. 拟人的；赋予人性的；神人同形同性论的
words.ex: The cartoon characters were anthropomorphic animals.
words.ex_cn: 卡通角色是拟人化的动物。
words.en: Anthropomorphic refers to the attribution of human traits, emotions, or intentions to non-human entities.

words.ex: The story gives human feelings to the dog, which is anthropomorphism.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事赋予狗人类的情感，这就是拟人化。
words.en: The attribution of human characteristics or behavior to a god, animal, or object.

words.tr:
adj. 贬损的；轻蔑的
n. 贬损语
words.ex: He used a pejorative word to describe his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个贬义词来描述他的邻居。
words.en: A pejorative word or expression is one that expresses criticism or disapproval.

words.tr: n. 变色龙；见风使舵的人
words.ex: The chameleon changes color to hide.
words.ex_cn: 变色龙改变颜色来隐藏自己。
words.en: A chameleon is a type of lizard that can change the color of its skin in order to blend in with its surroundings.

words.ex: The police scotched the plan to rob the bank.
words.ex_cn: 警察阻止了抢劫银行的计划。
words.en: To scotch something means to stop it from continuing or developing.

words.ex: He spent inordinate time on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他花了过多的时间玩电子游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as inordinate, you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively large in amount or degree.

words.ex: His coat is threadbare from many years of use.
words.ex_cn: 他的外套因为用了多年而变得破旧。
words.en: Worn out by overuse; shabby and old.

words.tr:
adj. 超自然的；神秘的；隐藏的
v. 掩蔽
n. 神秘的事物；神秘学
words.ex: He is interested in the occult.
words.ex_cn: 他对神秘学感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to mystical, supernatural, or magical powers, practices, or phenomena.

words.tr: v. 使（物质）成微粒，使（液体）雾化；使分裂成原子；使粉碎，使分裂
words.ex: The machine atomizes the liquid into a fine mist.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器将液体雾化成细小的水雾。
words.en: To atomize something means to break it down into very small parts or particles, often to the point where it becomes a fine spray or mist.

words.ex: He caught a crab at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在海滩上抓到一只蟹。
words.en: A crab is a sea creature with a flat round body covered by a shell, and five pairs of legs with large claws on the front pair. Crabs usually move sideways.

words.tr: n. 技巧；敏捷手法；策略；戏法
words.ex: The magician used sleight to make the coin disappear.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师用技巧让硬币消失了。
words.en: Skill in using the hands, especially in performing tricks.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；激昂地说
n. 喧闹的话；夸口话；叫喊
words.ex: He went on a rant about bad service.
words.ex_cn: 他大肆抱怨服务很差。
words.en: To speak or write in an angry or violent manner, often for a long time.

words.ex: The teacher admonished the student to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师劝告学生完成作业。
words.en: To admonish someone means to tell them in a serious way that they have done something wrong.

words.tr: n. 训戒；警告（等于 admonition）
words.ex: The teacher's admonishment was clear: no more late assignments.
words.ex_cn: 老师的训诫很明确：不能再有迟交的作业。
words.en: A verbal or written warning or reprimand.

words.ex: The ancient pottery was so friable that it crumbled in our hands.
words.ex_cn: 这件古老的陶器非常易碎，在我们手中就碎了。
words.en: Easily crumbled or reduced to powder.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；怠慢的；不留心的
words.ex: It would be remiss of me not to mention the importance of regular exercise.
words.ex_cn: 不提及定期锻炼的重要性，我会感到疏忽。
words.en: If someone is remiss, they are careless and do not do the things they are expected to do.

words.ex: There are only two extant copies of the ancient book.
words.ex_cn: 这本古书现存只有两份。
words.en: If something is extant, it is still in existence, in spite of being very old.

words.ex: The story is an allegory about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是一个关于善良的寓言。
words.en: An allegory is a story, poem, or picture which can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning, typically a moral or political one.

words.ex: The painting is rich in allegorical symbolism.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画充满了讽喻的象征意义。
words.en: An allegorical story, poem, or painting uses characters and events as symbols to express a moral, spiritual, or political idea.

words.ex: The chair has a wobble on one leg.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子有一条腿在晃动。
words.en: If something wobbles or if you wobble it, it moves unsteadily from side to side.

words.ex: He felt chagrin when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛时感到懊恼。
words.en: Chagrin is a feeling of disappointment, upset, or annoyance, perhaps because of your own failure.

words.tr: adj. 没有用的；不必要的；多余的
words.ex: The meeting was deemed otiose as it did not address any new issues.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议被认为是多余的，因为它没有解决任何新问题。
words.en: If you describe something as otiose, you mean that it serves no practical purpose or has no effect.

words.ex: The epilogue showed what happened to the characters after the story ended.
words.ex_cn: 尾声展示了故事结束后角色们的命运。
words.en: An epilogue is a section or speech at the end of a book or play that serves as a comment on or a conclusion to what has happened.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.tr:
n. 傻笑；假笑；痴笑
v. 傻笑；假笑；痴笑
words.ex: She simpered at him, trying to catch his attention.
words.ex_cn: 她对他假笑，试图引起他的注意。
words.en: To smile in a silly or affected way, often to appear more attractive or to hide one's true feelings.

words.ex: The omission of his name was an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的名字被漏掉是无意的。
words.en: An omission is something that has not been included or has not been done, either deliberately or accidentally.

words.tr: adj. 抛光的；磨光的；擦亮的； v. 擦亮；磨光；“polish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The polished table reflected the light.
words.ex_cn: 抛光的桌子反射着光线。
words.en: If something is polished, it has been made smooth and shiny by rubbing it with a cloth or a special substance.

words.tr: adj. 开胃的；促进食欲的
words.ex: The smell of the food was appetizing.
words.ex_cn: 食物的香味很诱人。
words.en: If you describe food as appetizing, you mean that it looks or smells good and makes you want to eat it.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.tr: v. （因抵押人未如期还贷）取消赎回权；排除；妨碍
words.ex: The bank foreclosed on the house after the owner defaulted on the mortgage.
words.ex_cn: 房主在抵押贷款违约后，银行取消了房屋的赎回权。
words.en: If the person or organization that lent someone money forecloses, they take possession of a property that was bought with the borrowed money, for example because regular repayments have not been made.

words.ex: He is proficient in playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹钢琴很熟练。
words.en: If you are proficient in something, you can do it well because you have learned how to do it.

words.ex: The teacher showed favoritism toward his favorite student.
words.ex_cn: 老师对他的最爱学生表现出偏袒。
words.en: The practice of giving unfair preferential treatment to one person or group at the expense of another.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: His generosity helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助了那个贫困的家庭。
words.en: Generosity is the quality of being kind and generous.

words.ex: He was ravenous after running five miles.
words.ex_cn: 跑了五英里后，他饿极了。
words.en: If you are ravenous, you are extremely hungry.

words.ex: His daily routine is humdrum.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活很单调。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as humdrum, you mean that they are ordinary, dull, or boring.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.ex: The cat hunched its back when it saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫看到狗时，背部拱了起来。
words.en: A hunch is a feeling or guess based on intuition rather than known facts.

words.tr: adj. 阴险的；潜伏的；暗中作祟的
words.ex: The insidious virus spread quietly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种隐蔽的病毒悄然在小镇蔓延。
words.en: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects.

words.tr: adv. 阴险地；隐伏地；暗中为害地
words.ex: The disease spreads insidiously, often without any noticeable symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病隐伏地传播，通常没有任何明显的症状。
words.en: In a way that is gradual and subtle but with very harmful effects.

words.ex: The village has a quaint old church.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄有一座古色古香的古老教堂。
words.en: Something that is quaint is attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned.

words.tr: n. 奇事；巧合；怪癖；奇行
words.ex: His habit of talking to his plants is a strange quirk.
words.ex_cn: 他跟植物说话的习惯是一个奇怪的奇事。
words.en: A quirk is a peculiar habit or aspect of a person's character, or an unexpected twist in a situation or story.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；离奇的；诡诈的
words.ex: He wears quirky hats every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都戴些古怪的帽子。
words.en: Something or someone that is quirky is unusual or unpredictable in an interesting or appealing way.

words.ex: The kinetic energy of the moving ball is high.
words.ex_cn: 运动的球的动能很高。
words.en: Relating to or resulting from motion.

words.ex: The pesky fly keeps buzzing around my head.
words.ex_cn: 那只烦人的苍蝇一直在我头上嗡嗡飞。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pesky, you are annoyed by them.

words.tr: adj. 不体面的；不相配的；不适宜的
words.ex: It is unseemly to shout in a library.
words.ex_cn: 在图书馆大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that someone's behaviour is unseemly, you disapprove of it because it is not appropriate in a particular situation.

words.tr:
adj. 鲁莽的；狂妄的；轻率的
n. 狂妄的人（尤指女子）
words.ex: The madcap boy ran through the park with no hat.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯疯癫癫的男孩没戴帽子跑过了公园。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as madcap, you mean that they are full of energy and enthusiasm, but slightly crazy or uncontrolled.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.ex: The study shows causality between smoking and lung cancer.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究表明吸烟与肺癌之间的因果关系。
words.en: Causality is the relationship between causes and effects.

words.ex: The insurrection failed because people did not support it.
words.ex_cn: 这次起义失败了，因为人们不支持它。
words.en: An insurrection is a violent uprising against an authority or government.

words.ex: The old woman gleaned wheat from the field after the harvest.
words.ex_cn: 这位老妇人在收割后从田里拾落穗。
words.en: To gather information or material bit by bit.

words.tr: adj. 自恋的；自我陶醉的
words.ex: She had a narcissistic personality and always thought she was the center of attention.
words.ex_cn: 她有自恋型人格，总是认为自己就是关注的中心。
words.en: If you describe someone as narcissistic, you are critical of them because they think about themselves a lot and admire themselves too much.

words.tr:
n. 马鞍；鞍座
v. 给（马）装鞍
words.ex: The boy rode on a saddle on the horse.
words.ex_cn: 男孩骑在马的马鞍上。
words.en: A saddle is a seat for a rider on the back of a horse or other animal, or a similar seat on a bicycle or motorcycle. It can also refer to the act of putting a saddle on a horse or to burden someone with a responsibility.

words.ex: He believes in naturalism and avoids supernatural explanations.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自然主义，避免使用超自然的解释。
words.en: Naturalism is a style and theory of representation based on the accurate depiction of detail.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.ex: The coach chastened the team for their poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 教练因球队表现不佳而惩罚了他们。
words.en: If you are chastened by something, it makes you regret that you have behaved badly or stupidly.

words.tr: adj. 虚弱的；衰弱的；无力的；
words.ex: The old man gave a feeble smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人露出虚弱的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

words.ex: He felt enmity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对他邻居怀有敌意。
words.en: Enmity is a feeling of hostility or ill will towards someone or something.

words.ex: A plume of smoke rose from the chimney.
words.ex_cn: 一股烟从烟囱里升起。
words.en: A plume is a large, soft, feather or a group of feathers, especially one that is used as a decoration.

words.tr: v. 将（某物）商品化；使变得商业化
words.ex: They commodify nature by selling clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过出售纯净水来将自然商品化。
words.en: To turn something into a commodity, often by assigning it a monetary value or treating it as a marketable good.

words.tr:
n. 退潮；衰退；减少
v. 退潮；衰退；减少
words.ex: The ebb of the tide left fish on the sand.
words.ex_cn: 退潮把鱼留在了沙滩上。
words.en: The movement of the tide out to sea.

words.tr: v. 打滚；躺卧；（船）颠簸；沉湎
words.ex: The pig wallow in the mud.
words.ex_cn: 猪在泥里打滚。
words.en: If you say that someone is wallowing in an unpleasant situation, you are criticizing them for being deliberately unhappy.

words.tr: adj. 欢乐的；轻松快活的；好交际的
words.ex: The party was convivial and everyone laughed a lot.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛友好愉快，大家都笑得很开心。
words.en: A convivial atmosphere or event is friendly and pleasant, and people enjoy being together.

words.ex: The conviviality at the party made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 派对上的友好气氛让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: Conviviality is the quality of being friendly and making people feel happy and welcome.

words.tr:
v. 预言；预测
n. （古罗马）占兆官；占卜师
words.ex: The early reviews augur well for the success of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 早期的评论预示着这部电影将取得成功。
words.en: to predict or foretell, especially from signs or omens

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

words.tr: adj.  快活的；愉快的；高兴的
words.ex: His jovial nature made him popular among his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他天性快活，这使他在同事中很受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone as jovial, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.tr:
n. 补锅匠
v. 小修；小补；摆弄
words.ex: He is a tinker who fixes old pots and pans.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名补锅匠，修理旧锅旧盆。
words.en: If you tinker with something, you make some small changes to it in an attempt to improve it or repair it.

words.tr:
n. 白鼬；雪貂
v. 用雪貂打猎；搜寻
words.ex: The ferret ran under the fence.
words.ex_cn: 白鼬从篱笆下跑过去了。
words.en: A ferret is a small, fierce animal which is used for hunting rabbits and rats. To ferret means to search for something persistently.

words.ex: His first book is a touchstone for modern writers.
words.ex_cn: 他的第一本书是现代作家的典范。
words.en: A touchstone is a criterion or standard by which something is judged or recognized.

words.ex: He used a euphemism to say he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个委婉语来表示他失业了。
words.en: A euphemism is a polite word or expression that is used to refer to things which people may find upsetting or embarrassing to talk about.

words.tr: adj. 传导的；能传导（热、电）的
words.ex: Copper is conductive and used in wires.
words.ex_cn: 铜具有导电性，用于电线。
words.en: Having the property of conducting something (especially heat or electricity).

words.tr: adj. 仓促马虎的；毛躁的；潦草的
words.ex: He gave a slapdash answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个草率的回答。
words.en: If you say that something is done in a slapdash way, you mean that it is done carelessly and quickly, without much attention to detail.

words.tr:
n. 元帅；高级军官；典礼官；消防局长
v. 整理；集结
words.ex: The marshal led the army into battle.
words.ex_cn: 元帅率领军队上战场。
words.en: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, especially in the army or air force, or a person who arranges or directs a public event.

words.tr:
n. 撤退；退却；静居处；
v. 撤退；退却；
words.ex: The army ordered a retreat after the battle.
words.ex_cn: 战斗后，军队下令撤退。
words.en: If you retreat, you move away from something or someone, often because you are frightened or because you want to be alone. A retreat is also a quiet, isolated place that you go to in order to rest or to do things in private.

words.tr: adj. 衰弱的；衰败的；软弱的
words.ex: The old king was effete and could not lead.
words.ex_cn: 这位老国王虚弱无能，无法领导。
words.en: No longer productive or effective; lacking the power or will to achieve or succeed.

words.ex: She sifts flour through a fine mesh.
words.ex_cn: 她用细网筛面粉。
words.en: To sift means to put a fine, loose, or powdery substance through a sieve so as to remove lumps or large particles. It can also mean to examine something thoroughly so as to isolate that which is most important or useful.

words.tr: n. 退休；退休金；废弃；陈旧
words.ex: He pays money into his superannuation every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都向他的养老金账户缴费。
words.en: Superannuation refers to a pension or retirement fund that an employee contributes to during their working life, which is then paid out to them upon retirement.

words.tr:
v. 挑毛病；吹毛求疵
n. 挑剔；挑毛病
words.ex: He cavils at every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他挑剔每一个小错误。
words.en: If you say that someone cavils at something, you mean that they make criticisms of it that you think are unimportant or unnecessary.

words.ex: His novels are often criticized for their prurience.
words.ex_cn: 他的小说经常因为其好色内容而受到批评。
words.en: Prurience refers to an excessive interest in sexual matters.

words.tr: v. 确定无罪；免除（罪责）
words.ex: The new evidence helped to exonerate him.
words.ex_cn: 新的证据帮助他洗清了罪名。
words.en: If someone is exonerated, they are proved to be not guilty of a crime or responsible for something bad that happened.

words.tr:
n. 尖塔；尖顶；尖峰；尖岩石；顶点；顶峰
v. 造小尖塔；把...放在极高处
words.ex: The pinnacle of the church reached high into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔高耸入云。
words.en: The pinnacle of something is the highest point or level that it can reach, especially when it is very good.

words.tr: adj. 无表情的（面孔）；表情冷淡的
words.ex: He delivered the punchline with a deadpan expression.
words.ex_cn: 他用面无表情的表情说出了笑点。
words.en: If you describe someone as deadpan, you mean that they appear serious and do not show emotion in their face or voice, even when they are joking or teasing.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.tr: adj. 享有声望的；声望很高的；
words.ex: He got into a prestigious university.
words.ex_cn: 他进入了一所享有声望的大学。
words.en: A prestigious institution, job, or activity is respected and admired because it is considered to be of very high quality.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: The somnolent boy nodded off during class.
words.ex_cn: 那个昏昏欲睡的男孩在课堂上睡着了。
words.en: If you are somnolent, you feel sleepy.

words.tr: n. 困倦；昏昏欲睡；嗜睡
words.ex: After taking the medication, she experienced a deep state of somnolence.
words.ex_cn: 服用药物后，她进入了深深的困倦状态。
words.en: Somnolence is a state of near-sleep, a strong desire for sleep, or sleeping for unusually long periods.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.ex: He gave the exact time of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了会议的确切时间。
words.en: If you describe something as exact, you mean that it is precise and accurate in all its details.

words.tr: n. 强求；勒索；苛捐杂税
words.ex: The king demanded exaction of heavy taxes.
words.ex_cn: 国王要求征收重税。
words.en: The act of demanding and obtaining something from someone, especially money, through force or threats.

words.ex: The wind strews leaves on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得满地都是。
words.en: To scatter or spread things untidily over a surface or area.

words.ex: The priest offered prayers for the expiation of sins.
words.ex_cn: 牧师为赎罪祈祷。
words.en: The act of making amends or reparation for guilt or wrongdoing; atonement.

words.tr: v. 置入神龛中；入庙祀奉；奉为神圣；珍藏
words.ex: They enshrined the ancient statue in a golden shrine.
words.ex_cn: 他们把这尊古代雕像置入了一个金色神龛中。
words.en: If something such as a tradition or a right is enshrined in something such as a constitution or law, it is protected by it.

words.tr: n. 讲演术；小礼拜堂；祈祷室
words.ex: His oratory captured the attention of everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲术吸引了房间里每个人的注意。
words.en: The art or practice of formal speaking in public, especially in a way that is intended to be persuasive or eloquent.

words.tr: n. 良心的责备；后悔；悔恨
words.ex: He felt no compunction about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他撒谎骗朋友时毫无愧疚。
words.en: A feeling of guilt or moral scruple that prevents or follows the doing of something bad.

words.tr: n. 顽固；执拗；坚持到底
words.ex: His pertinacity helped him finish the hard task.
words.ex_cn: 他的执着帮助他完成了这项困难的任务。
words.en: The quality of holding firmly to a purpose, belief, or action; stubbornness.

words.ex: He is pertinacious about finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is pertinacious continues trying to do something in a very determined way, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.tr: adj. 感情脆弱的；易落泪的；多愁善感的
words.ex: She was feeling maudlin after watching the sentimental movie.
words.ex_cn: 看完那部感人的电影后，她感到非常伤感。
words.en: If you describe someone as maudlin, you mean that they are being sad and sentimental in a foolish way, perhaps because of drinking alcohol.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.tr: n. 恶心；晕眩；疑虑；不安
words.ex: The smell of the food gave her a qualm.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A qualm is a feeling of uneasiness about whether what you are doing is right.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.tr: n. 背信弃义；奸诈；不忠
words.ex: His perfidiousness shocked everyone who knew him.
words.ex_cn: 他的背信弃义让所有认识他的人感到震惊。

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.ex: Her hug gave me solace after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 在失去亲人后，她的拥抱给了我安慰。
words.en: Solace is comfort that you feel when you are consoled in times of disappointment or sadness.

words.tr: adj. 可补救的；可挽救的；可矫正的
words.ex: The damage to the environment is remediable if we act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们迅速采取行动，对环境的破坏是可以补救的。
words.en: If something is remediable, it can be corrected or cured.

words.tr: adj. 无光泽的；暗淡的；无生气的；乏善可陈的
words.ex: The paint on the car looked lackluster after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴过后，车漆显得暗淡无光。
words.en: If you describe something as lackluster, you mean that it is not exciting or not very good quality.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: He spread calumny about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: A false statement made to damage someone's reputation.

words.ex: He made a gamble on the horse race.
words.ex_cn: 他在这场赛马上赌了一把。
words.en: If you gamble on something, you take a risky action or decision in the hope of gaining something.

words.tr:
n. 寿衣；裹尸布；覆盖物
v. 覆盖；遮蔽
words.ex: The body was wrapped in a white shroud.
words.ex_cn: 遗体被裹在一件白色的寿衣里。
words.en: A shroud is a cloth which is used for wrapping a dead body. It can also refer to something that covers, hides, or protects.

words.tr: adj. 浮肿的；肿胀的；浮夸的
words.ex: His legs looked turgid after the long walk.
words.ex_cn: 他长时间走路后，双腿看起来浮肿了。
words.en: If you describe something such as a piece of writing or a speech as turgid, you think it is boring and difficult to understand because it is too serious or complicated.

words.ex: The obstreperous crowd made it difficult to hear the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 吵闹的人群使得演讲者的话难以听清。
words.en: If you say that someone is obstreperous, you are annoyed because they are noisy and difficult to control.

words.tr: n. 巨大的数量（或收藏品）
words.ex: The festival showed a panoply of colorful costumes.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日展示了丰富多彩的服装。
words.en: A panoply is a complete or impressive collection of things or a splendid display.

words.ex: There was a spike in sales after the advertisement.
words.ex_cn: 广告发布后，销量出现了激增。
words.en: A spike is a thin, pointed piece of metal, wood, or another hard material, or a sudden increase in something.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

words.ex: He is tapping his pen incessantly.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地敲打钢笔。
words.en: Without interruption; constantly.

words.ex: He can deduce the answer from the clues.
words.ex_cn: 他能从线索中推断出答案。
words.en: If you deduce something or deduce that something is true, you reach that conclusion because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: He uses deductive reasoning to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他使用演绎推理来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Deductive reasoning is a logical process in which a conclusion is based on the concordance of multiple premises that are generally assumed to be true.

words.ex: The dog cowers when the thunder sounds.
words.ex_cn: 当雷声响起时，狗会蜷缩起来。
words.en: To crouch down in fear.

words.tr: n. 喜爱；类同；密切关系；亲和力
words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 彩虹色的；色彩斑斓的
words.ex: The soap bubble is iridescent in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 肥皂泡在阳光下呈现出彩虹色。
words.en: Showing luminous colors that seem to change when seen from different angles.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: The case will be heard in court next week.
words.ex_cn: 这个案件将于下周在法院审理。
words.en: A court is a place where legal matters are decided by a judge and jury or by a magistrate.

words.ex: It's preposterous to think cats can drive cars.
words.ex_cn: 认为猫会开车是极其荒谬的。
words.en: If you describe something as preposterous, you mean that it is extremely unreasonable and foolish.

words.ex: He is a revisionist historian who questions old stories.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位修正主义历史学家，质疑旧的故事。
words.en: A revisionist is someone who advocates or practices revision, especially of a political or historical nature, often challenging the accepted views or interpretations.

words.tr: adj. 疑惑的；嘲弄的；揶揄的
words.ex: He gave a quizzical look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出困惑的表情。
words.en: If you give someone a quizzical look or smile, you look at them or smile at them in a way that shows that you are surprised or amused by their behavior.

words.ex: The new phone outcompete the old model in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机在速度上超过了旧型号。
words.en: To outcompete means to surpass others in competition, especially in business or sports, by being more effective or successful.

words.tr: v. 跛行；蹒跚；捆绑（马等的）两腿
words.ex: The old man hobbled along the street.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人一瘸一拐地走在街上。
words.en: If you hobble, you walk in an awkward way, usually because your feet or legs hurt.

words.tr: v. 发誓放弃；断然丢弃
words.ex: He forswears lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓不再对朋友撒谎。
words.en: If you forswear something, you promise to stop doing it or having it, especially because you think it is bad or harmful.

words.tr: adj. 自由自在的；无拘无束的；随意的
words.ex: He is a freewheeling artist who paints without rules.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不受拘束的艺术家，画画时不按规则来。
words.en: Characterized by a lack of restraint or inhibition; free and easy.

words.tr: adj. 外界的；外在的；非固有的；
words.ex: The reward was extrinsic, not from within.
words.ex_cn: 这个奖励是外界的，不是来自内心的。
words.en: Extrinsic means not forming part of or belonging to a thing; external.

words.tr:
n. 绳肌腱；腿筋
v. 割断腿筋；使不能正常工作
words.ex: He injured his hamstring during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中拉伤了绳肌腱。
words.en: A hamstring is a tendon at the back of a person's knee. If someone is hamstrung by something, it means they are severely restricted in their ability to act or perform.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.tr: adj. 宗派的；教派的；派别的；
words.ex: The conflict was fueled by sectarian tensions.
words.ex_cn: 这场冲突由宗派紧张局势加剧。
words.en: If you describe someone as sectarian, you mean that they belong to a particular sect, especially a religious one, and that their beliefs and practices are influenced by this.

words.tr: n. 详尽解释；专题讨论；专题演讲；专题论文
words.ex: The professor delivered a lengthy disquisition on the history of philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 教授就哲学史发表了一篇冗长的专题论文。
words.en: A disquisition is a long and detailed explanation or discussion of a particular subject.

words.ex: The library keeps old newspapers in an archive.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆把旧报纸保存在档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.tr: adj. 档案的；关于档案的
words.ex: The archival documents provide valuable insights into the past.
words.ex_cn: 这些档案文件为过去提供了宝贵的见解。
words.en: Relating to or contained in archives.

words.tr:
adj. 杂色的；混杂的
n. 杂色；混杂
words.ex: The motley crowd cheered at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 这群杂乱的人群在游行中欢呼。
words.en: If you describe a group of things or people as motley, you mean that they are very different from each other and do not seem to belong together.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.tr: n. 接触传染病；传染；歪风；蔓延
words.ex: The contagion spread quickly among the children.
words.ex_cn: 这种传染病在孩子们中迅速传播。
words.en: A contagion is the spreading of a disease, especially one that is caused by bacteria or viruses, from one person or animal to another by direct or indirect contact.

words.ex: He will pare the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他将用刀削苹果。
words.en: To pare something means to cut off its outer layer or to reduce its size or amount by cutting or trimming.

words.tr: adj. 不调和的；不一致的；不和谐的
words.ex: The two voices sounded discordant.
words.ex_cn: 这两声音听起来不和谐。
words.en: Something that is discordant is strange or unpleasant because it does not fit in with other things.

words.ex: Their answers were concordant.
words.ex_cn: 他们的答案是一致的。
words.en: If two things are concordant, they are in agreement or harmony with each other.

words.ex: The people tried to overthrow the corrupt government.
words.ex_cn: 人民试图推翻腐败的政府。
words.en: To overthrow a government or a leader means to remove them from power, often by force.

words.ex: The court checked the constitutionality of the new law.
words.ex_cn: 法院审查了这项新法律的合宪性。
words.en: The quality or state of being in accordance with a constitution; the principle that a government's authority is determined by a body of laws or constitution.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.ex: The computer uses a buffer to store data temporarily.
words.ex_cn: 计算机使用缓冲区临时存储数据。
words.en: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that reduces the impact of something.

words.tr: adj. 不整洁的；凌乱的；不修边幅的
words.ex: Her hair was unkempt and her clothes were disheveled.
words.ex_cn: 她的头发蓬乱，衣服也凌乱不堪。
words.en: If you describe someone's hair or appearance as unkempt, you mean that it is untidy or messy.

words.ex: He lacked the wherewithal to start his own business.
words.ex_cn: 他缺乏创业所需的资金。
words.en: The necessary means, especially financial means, to accomplish something.

words.tr:
v. 颤抖；颤动；发抖
n. 颤抖
words.ex: The leaf quivers in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树叶在风中颤抖。
words.en: To shake or tremble with a slight rapid motion; a case for carrying arrows.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；清晰的
words.ex: The lake water is limpid and clear.
words.ex_cn: 湖水清澈透明。
words.en: Clear and transparent, especially in a way that makes it easy to understand.

words.tr: v. 幸灾乐祸；沾沾自喜；满足地看
words.ex: He gloats when his rival loses the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的对手输掉比赛时，他幸灾乐祸。
words.en: To gloat means to observe or think about something with triumphant and often malicious satisfaction, gratification, or delight.

words.ex: The judge will summon him tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 法官明天将传唤他。
words.en: If you summon someone, you order them to come to you.

words.ex: The doctor explained the disease to the layperson in simple words.
words.ex_cn: 医生用简单的语言向普通人解释了这种疾病。
words.en: A layperson is someone who is not trained, qualified, or experienced in a particular subject or activity.

words.ex: The firefighters brought salvation to the people trapped in the burning building.
words.ex_cn: 消防员拯救了被困在着火大楼里的人们。
words.en: Salvation is the act of saving or protecting from harm, risk, loss, destruction, etc., or the state of being saved from such conditions.

words.ex: The class was engaged in a lively disputation about the validity of the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 全班同学就新政策的有效性展开了热烈的辩论。
words.en: A disputation is a formal debate or argument, especially one that is conducted in a public setting.

words.tr: adj. 有争议的；可商榷的
words.ex: The result is disputable because the data is unclear.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果是有争议的，因为数据不清楚。
