words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是来自古代的遗迹。
words.en: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest.

words.ex: The disease is caused by exogenous bacteria.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病是由外源性细菌引起的。
words.en: Exogenous refers to something originating from outside an organism, system, or specific field of study, often used in biology, economics, and other sciences to describe external influences or factors.

words.ex: He is a conscientious student who always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个尽责的学生，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is conscientious is very careful to do their work properly.

words.ex: He saw a beautiful panorama from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 他从山顶看到了美丽的全景。
words.en: A panorama is a view of a wide area, or a description or study that presents all the different parts or aspects of a particular subject.

words.tr:
v. 沉重缓慢地行进；猛击；苦干
n. 苦工；长途跋涉
words.ex: They slog through the mud after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 他们在大雨后艰难地跋涉过泥地。
words.en: To work hard over a long period, especially doing work that is difficult or boring.

words.ex: She spoke with aplomb during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 她在面试中自信地发言。
words.en: If you do something with aplomb, you do it with confidence in a relaxed way.

words.tr:
adj. 患黄疸病的；有偏见的
v. 使产生黄疸；使怀偏见；“jaundice”的过去式
words.ex: His judgment was jaundiced by his personal dislike for the candidate.
words.ex_cn: 他对候选人的个人反感使他的判断带有偏见。
words.en: If someone has a jaundiced view of something, they see it in a negative way because they are jealous or bitter.

words.ex: The pauper lived in a small hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个穷人住在一间小屋里。
words.en: A pauper is someone who is extremely poor and has very little money or possessions.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.tr:
n. 救援；援助者
v. 救援
words.ex: The nurse gave succor to the injured man.
words.ex_cn: 护士向受伤的男人提供了援助。
words.en: Succor is assistance and support given to someone in times of hardship or distress.

words.tr: v. 使具体化；使抽象概念具体化
words.ex: The artist sought to reify his emotions through his paintings.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家试图通过他的画作使他的情感具体化。
words.en: To reify means to make something abstract more concrete or real.

words.tr: n. 反对者；否定者；爱唱反调的人
words.ex: Despite the naysayers, she managed to achieve her goals.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有那些摇头族，她还是设法实现了自己的目标。
words.en: A naysayer is someone who always says something will not work or is not possible.

words.ex: After the failed performance, he became the laughingstock of the school.
words.ex_cn: 那次失败的表演后，他成了学校的笑柄。
words.en: A person or thing that is regarded as ridiculous or absurd and thus becomes the object of laughter or mockery.

words.tr: n. 冒充内行者；庸医；骗子
words.ex: He is a charlatan who pretends to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: A charlatan is someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge that they do not really possess.

words.tr: v. 否认；放弃；拒绝承认
words.ex: He disclaims any responsibility for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他否认对这个错误负有任何责任。
words.en: If you disclaim knowledge of something or disclaim responsibility for something, you say that you did not know about it or are not responsible for it.

words.ex: The new app is an offshoot of the original website.
words.ex_cn: 这个新应用是原网站的衍生物。
words.en: An offshoot is something that has developed from something larger or more general.

words.ex: He smiled at the recollection of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回忆起童年时微笑了。
words.en: The act of remembering something or the ability to remember.

words.ex: The team showed great camaraderie during the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队在比赛中展现了深厚的友爱。
words.en: A feeling of good friendship among the people in a group.

words.tr:
adj. 即时的；未经准备的；唐突无礼的
adv. 即时地；未经思索地；随便地
words.ex: He gave an offhand answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个即时的回答。
words.en: If you say something offhand, you say it without checking the details or facts of it beforehand.

words.tr: n. 苦心而成的著作；学术作品；刻苦钻研
words.ex: The professor's latest lucubration is a comprehensive study on ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 教授最新的苦心之作是对古代文明的综合研究。
words.en: A lucubration is a piece of writing that is produced by someone who studies or works hard at night, often implying that it is the result of deep thought and effort.

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.ex: The punishment was condign for the crime committed.
words.ex_cn: 这个惩罚对于所犯的罪行来说是应得的。
words.en: Deserved; appropriate; fitting.

words.tr: v. 透支；过度往后拉；过分描述
words.ex: He overdraws his bank account every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都透支银行账户。
words.en: To overdraw means to withdraw more money from a bank account than the account holds, resulting in a negative balance. It can also mean to exaggerate or embellish in description or representation.

words.ex: He is a multifaceted person who can sing, paint, and code.
words.ex_cn: 他是个多方面的人，会唱歌、绘画和编程。
words.en: Having many facets or aspects.

words.tr: v. 取出内脏；重伤元气
words.ex: The cat eviscerated the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫掏出了老鼠的内脏。
words.en: To eviscerate means to remove the internal organs of a person or animal, or to remove the most important parts of something, leaving it weak or ineffective.

words.ex: He faltered when asked his name.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到名字时，他犹豫了。
words.en: If you falter, you lose your confidence and stop doing something or start making mistakes.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.tr:
v. 宠爱；娇养；纵容
n. 宠儿
words.ex: She cosseted her baby with soft blankets and gentle songs.
words.ex_cn: 她用柔软的毯子和轻柔的歌声呵护她的婴儿。
words.en: To cosset someone means to treat them with great care and attention, often in a way that is excessive or indulgent.

words.ex: The teacher made an emendation to the text.
words.ex_cn: 老师对文本做了一处修改。
words.en: the act of making corrections or improvements to a text

words.tr: adj. 爱讲道的；说教的；爱唠叨的
words.ex: His speech was preachy and full of moral lessons.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了道德说教。
words.en: If you describe someone as preachy, you mean that they try to give people moral advice in a way that is annoying or boring.

words.ex: The machine is designed to emulsify the mixture.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器设计用来乳化混合物。
words.en: To emulsify means to mix two liquids together to form an emulsion, which is a mixture in which small drops of one liquid are spread throughout another liquid.

words.ex: He rebut the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: If you rebut a charge or criticism that is made against you, you give reasons why it is untrue or unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 智慧的；表现智慧的；赋予智慧的
words.ex: He reads sapiential texts to find wise advice.
words.ex_cn: 他阅读智慧文献以寻找明智的建议。
words.en: Relating to wisdom or the wise, often used to describe literature or sayings that impart wisdom.

words.tr: adj. 极甜的；过分甜的；故作多情的；奉承的；过于亲近的
words.ex: The cake tasted too saccharine.
words.ex_cn: 这块蛋糕尝起来太甜了。
words.en: Excessively sweet or sentimental.

words.tr: adj. 史诗的；叙事诗的；宏丽的；
words.ex: The movie tells an epic story of heroes and dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影讲述了一个关于英雄和龙的史诗故事。
words.en: An epic is a long book, poem, or film, whose story extends over a long period of time or tells of great events.

words.tr: v. 解开；解脱；解决（纠纷等）
words.ex: He tried to disentangle the tangled wires.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把缠在一起的电线解开。
words.en: To free something or someone from being tangled or twisted, or to separate things that are twisted together.

words.tr:
n. 高谈阔论；长篇大论；大声斥责的讲话
v. 作长篇大论；高谈阔论；猛烈的批评或训斥
words.ex: The politician gave a long harangue about taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客就税收问题发表了一番长篇高谈阔论。
words.en: A harangue is a lengthy and aggressive speech, especially one delivered in public.

words.ex: He left his watch as a pawn at the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他把手表当成了典当品放在店里。
words.en: To pawn something means to leave it with a pawnbroker, who lends you money in exchange. The pawnbroker keeps the item until you pay back the money plus interest.

words.ex: The violent news appalls her.
words.ex_cn: 这起暴力新闻令她震惊。
words.en: to fill with horror or dismay; shock deeply

words.tr:
adj. 零碎的；
adv. 零碎地；
words.ex: He fixed the car piecemeal, one part at a time.
words.ex_cn: 他一点一点地修理汽车，一次修一个零件。
words.en: If you describe a change or process as piecemeal, you disapprove of it because it happens gradually, usually at irregular intervals, and is probably not satisfactory.

words.ex: I met him at a party, but he is only an acquaintance.
words.ex_cn: 我在聚会上认识了他，但他只是个熟人。
words.en: An acquaintance is someone you know a little, who is not a close friend.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；不松懈的；无情的
words.ex: He showed unrelenting effort to finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持不懈地努力完成比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as unrelenting, you mean that they are continuing to do something in a very determined way, often without caring whether they hurt or embarrass other people.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.ex: The storm denuded the trees of their leaves.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把树上的叶子都刮掉了。
words.en: To strip something of its covering, possessions, or assets; to make bare.

words.ex: The rain teemed down all night.
words.ex_cn: 雨整晚倾泻而下。
words.en: If a place teems with people, animals, or things, it is full of them and they are all moving around.

words.ex: He denied the aspersion on his character.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了对他人格的污蔑。
words.en: An aspersion is a remark or statement that criticizes someone or something and damages their reputation.

words.ex: The elephant was gargantuan compared to the dog.
words.ex_cn: 这只大象比起狗来说巨大无比。
words.en: If you say that something is gargantuan, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 失败的；夭折的；发育不完全的
words.ex: The abortive plan failed before it started.
words.ex_cn: 这个失败的计划在开始前就失败了。
words.en: Failing to produce the intended result; unsuccessful.

words.tr:
n. 灾难；祸患；鞭子
v. 鞭打；折磨；使受苦难
words.ex: Pollution is a scourge on the environment.
words.ex_cn: 污染是对环境的祸害。
words.en: A scourge is something that causes a lot of trouble or suffering, or a whip used as an instrument of punishment.

words.ex: The rapid changes in the economy have caused a state of disequilibrium.
words.ex_cn: 经济的快速变化导致了不平衡状态。
words.en: A state of imbalance or instability, especially in an economy or market, where supply and demand are not equal.

words.ex: The political situation in the country was like a maelstrom.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的政治局势就像一个大漩涡。
words.en: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool in the sea or a river, or a situation in which there is great confusion, violence, and destruction.

words.ex: She confides in her best friend.
words.ex_cn: 她向最好的朋友倾诉。
words.en: If you confide in someone, you tell them a secret.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: He is a zealot for environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心者。
words.en: A zealot is someone who is extremely enthusiastic about something, especially religion or politics.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；懒散的；马虎的
words.ex: He is lax about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很松懈。
words.en: If you say that a person's behaviour or a system is lax, you mean they are not careful or strict about maintaining high standards.

words.ex: He made a proposition to lower taxes.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了降低税收的建议。
words.en: A proposition is a statement or an idea that people can consider or discuss to decide whether it is true.

words.ex: The company agreed to defray the travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司同意支付差旅费。
words.en: If you defray someone's costs or expenses, you give them money which represents the amount that they have spent, for example while they have been doing something for you or acting on your behalf.

words.tr:
n. 说笑；玩笑
v. 开玩笑
words.ex: He likes to jest with his friends during lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在午餐时和朋友开玩笑。
words.en: A jest is a remark that is intended to be amusing or funny, especially one that is made in a light-hearted or teasing manner.

words.tr: n. 奇想；异想天开；怪异多变
words.ex: His plans change with every vagary of mood.
words.ex_cn: 他的计划随着情绪的每个变化而改变。
words.en: A vagary is an unexpected and inexplicable change in a situation or in someone's behavior.

words.ex: I envisage a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 我设想一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: If you envisage something, you imagine that it is true, real, or likely to happen.

words.tr:
n. 亲属；血缘关系
adj. 同源的；类似的
words.ex: He visited his kindred during the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 他在假期里探望了他的亲属。
words.en: If two people or things are kindred, they are similar in some way, often because they are related.

words.tr: adj. 过分虚伪而令人生厌的
words.ex: He gave her a fulsome compliment.
words.ex_cn: 他给了她一段过分的赞美。
words.en: If you describe expressions of praise, apology, or gratitude as fulsome, you disapprove of them because they are exaggerated and elaborate, so that they sound insincere.

words.tr:
v. 加酵母；使发酵；影响
n. 酵素；酵母；潜移默化的影响
words.ex: She uses yeast to leaven the bread.
words.ex_cn: 她用酵母使面包发酵。
words.en: Leaven is a substance, typically yeast, that is used in dough to make it rise. It can also refer to something that modifies or lightens a situation or atmosphere.

words.tr:
v. 覆盖；叠加；铺；镀
n. 覆盖物；涂层
v. 躺在…上面；把（婴儿）覆闷致死；“overlie”的过去式
words.ex: He put an overlay on the photo to add text.
words.ex_cn: 他在照片上叠加了一层以添加文字。
words.en: To cover something with a layer of another material, or to lie on top of something else.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.tr:
v. 献出；拿出；提供
n. 献出；拿出；提供
words.ex: He proffered a cup of tea to his guest.
words.ex_cn: 他递给客人一杯茶。
words.en: If you proffer something to someone, you offer it to them for acceptance.

words.ex: He shifted the gear to slow down the car.
words.ex_cn: 他换挡以减慢车速。
words.en: Gear refers to a toothed wheel that works with others to alter the relation between the speed of a driving mechanism (such as the engine of a vehicle) and the speed of the driven parts (the wheels). It can also mean equipment that is used for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adj. 造成创伤的；痛苦的；不愉快的
words.ex: The car accident was a traumatic experience.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次创伤性的经历。
words.en: If something is traumatic, it causes you severe emotional distress and anxiety.

words.tr: n. (尤指道德方面的)戒律；准则
words.ex: He follows the precept to be kind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循要善良的教诲。
words.en: A precept is a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought.

words.tr: n. 绝境；僵局；死路；死胡同
words.ex: The talks reached an impasse and no one could move forward.
words.ex_cn: 谈判陷入了僵局，没有人能继续前进。
words.en: An impasse is a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible, especially because of disagreement; a deadlock.

words.ex: The snooper watched his neighbor through the window.
words.ex_cn: 这个窥探者通过窗户盯着他的邻居。
words.en: A snooper is someone who secretly looks at things that are private or belong to someone else, especially by looking through windows or reading someone else's letters or messages.

words.tr:
n. （赶牲畜的）尖头棒；激励；刺激
v. 刺激；驱使
words.ex: The farmer used a goad to guide the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一根尖头棒赶牛。
words.en: If you goad someone, you deliberately make them feel angry or irritated, often causing them to react by doing something.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.tr: v. 抗议；表示异议；劝诫
words.ex: He remonstrated with his friend for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为朋友迟到而责备了他。
words.en: To remonstrate means to make a forcefully reproachful protest.

words.ex: He had a hallucination after taking the medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他服药后出现了幻觉。
words.en: A hallucination is a perception in the absence of external stimulus that has qualities of real perception. Hallucinations are vivid, substantial, and are perceived to be located in external objective space.

words.ex: The plasticity of the clay made it ideal for sculpting.
words.ex_cn: 黏土的可塑性使其非常适合雕塑。
words.en: The quality of being easily shaped or molded.

words.tr:
n. 松鸡；松鸡肉；怨言；牢骚
v. 抱怨；发牢骚
words.ex: The hunter saw a grouse in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎人在森林里看到一只松鸡。
words.en: A grouse is a bird with a plump body and feathered legs, belonging to the family Tetraonidae. As a verb, to grouse means to complain or grumble.

words.ex: He will proofread the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送这封信之前会校对。
words.en: To read and mark corrections on a text before it is published.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

words.tr: v. 痛饮狂欢；狂饮作乐
words.ex: They carouse every weekend at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周末都在海滩上狂欢。
words.en: To engage in a noisy, lively drinking party.

words.tr: n. 喧嚣；大混乱；大吵大闹
words.ex: The crowd created pandemonium when the winner was announced.
words.ex_cn: 当获胜者被宣布时，人群陷入了混乱。
words.en: Pandemonium is a situation in which there is a lot of noise and confusion because people are excited, angry, or frightened.

words.tr: adj. 可憎的；讨厌的；令人作呕的
words.ex: The smell of the garbage was odious.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的气味令人讨厌。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odious, you think that they are extremely unpleasant, horrible, or disgusting.

words.ex: He learned about his ancestry from his grandmother.
words.ex_cn: 他从祖母那里了解了自己的血统。
words.en: Your ancestry is the series of ancestors from whom you are descended.

words.tr: adj. 轻松活泼的；得意洋洋的；自信满满的
words.ex: He walked with a jaunty step, clearly pleased with himself.
words.ex_cn: 他步伐轻快，显然对自己感到很满意。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jaunty, you mean that they are full of confidence and energy.

words.tr:
adv. 迷路地；误入歧途地
adj. 迷路的；误入歧途的
words.ex: The little dog went astray in the park.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在公园里走丢了。
words.en: If you go astray, you lose your direction when you are trying to go somewhere.

words.ex: The king was accompanied by a large retinue.
words.ex_cn: 国王由一大群随行人员陪同。
words.en: A retinue is a group of people who travel with an important person to help or protect them.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.tr: adj. 非常自负的；自命不凡的
words.ex: He was so vainglorious that he believed his own press clippings.
words.ex_cn: 他非常自负，以至于相信了自己的新闻剪报。
words.en: If you describe someone as vainglorious, you are critical of them because they are very proud of their own status, abilities, or achievements.

words.tr: adj. 爱发牢骚的；脾气坏的；不悦的； 愠怒的
words.ex: He is grouchy when he wakes up early.
words.ex_cn: 他早起时脾气很暴躁。
words.en: If someone is grouchy, they are bad-tempered and complain a lot.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；暗淡的；无生气的
words.ex: Her face was pallid after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 久病之后，她的脸色变得苍白。
words.en: If you describe something such as a performance or a piece of writing as pallid, you mean that it is weak and not at all exciting or interesting.

words.ex: He juxtaposes old photos with new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他把老照片和新照片放在一起。
words.en: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.

words.ex: She coddles her little brother too much.
words.ex_cn: 她太宠着她的弟弟了。
words.en: To treat someone in an indulgent or overprotective way.

words.ex: The embryonic stage is the earliest phase of development.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎阶段是发育的最早时期。
words.en: In an early stage of development; rudimentary.

words.tr:
n. 窥探；杠杆；爱打探的人
v. 打听；窥探；用杠杆撬开
words.ex: His pry into my private messages made me angry.
words.ex_cn: 他窥探我的私信让我很生气。
words.en: To try to find out private information about someone or something in a way that is annoying or rude.

words.tr: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难；
words.ex: Don't ignore the pitfall of skipping homework.
words.ex_cn: 不要忽视不做作业这个陷阱。
words.en: A pitfall is a likely mistake or problem in a situation.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.tr: v. （使）复活；（使）恢复知觉；（使）复兴
words.ex: The paramedics tried to resuscitate the man after he collapsed.
words.ex_cn: 当这位男子晕倒后，急救人员试图救活他。
words.en: To resuscitate someone means to bring them back to consciousness or to make them start breathing again after they have stopped.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.tr: v. 厚厚地覆盖；使…窒息；闷死
words.ex: He tried to smother the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用毯子把火闷灭。
words.en: To smother someone or something means to kill them by covering their face so that they cannot breathe, or to put out a fire by covering it.

words.tr: adj. 兴高采烈的；狂喜的；热烈的
words.ex: The audience burst into rapturous applause.
words.ex_cn: 观众爆发出热烈的掌声。
words.en: If you describe someone as rapturous, you mean that they are extremely happy or enthusiastic about something.

words.tr: n. 预断病情；预后；预测
words.ex: The prognosis for patients with this disease is generally poor.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病的患者预后通常不佳。
words.en: A prognosis is an estimate of the future course and outcome of a disease, especially of the chances of recovery.

words.tr: n. 细节；细枝末节；琐事；“minutia”的复数
words.ex: The detective focused on the minutiae of the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 侦探专注于犯罪现场的微小细节。
words.en: The small, precise, or trivial details of something.

words.ex: The spy tried to infiltrate the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 间谍试图渗透敌方基地。
words.en: To enter or gain access to (an organization, place, etc.) surreptitiously and gradually, especially in order to acquire secret information.

words.ex: The clement teacher gave students extra time.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师给了学生更多时间。
words.en: Mild or merciful in disposition or character; lenient; compassionate.

words.ex: The teacher chastised the boy for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为男孩在课堂上说话而责备了他。
words.en: To chastise someone means to punish or criticize them severely.

words.tr: adj. 讳莫如深的；守口如瓶的；谨慎小心的；狡猾的
words.ex: He was cagey when asked about his plans.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到他的计划时，他很谨慎。
words.en: If you describe someone as cagey, you mean that they are careful not to give too much information or to show their feelings.

words.tr: adj. 未被预订的；无保留的；不隐瞒的
words.ex: He gave an unreserved apology.
words.ex_cn: 他毫无保留地道歉了。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or behaviour as unreserved, you mean that they have expressed their feelings or done something in a very open and full way.

words.tr:
n. （赎罪的）苦行；苦修；忏悔
v. 使...以苦行赎罪
words.ex: He performed penance for his sins.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的罪行忏悔。
words.en: Penance is the act of doing something to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done, especially in some religions.

words.tr:
adj. 蛮勇的；鲁莽大胆的
n. 鲁莽大胆的人
words.ex: He is a daredevil rider who jumps over cars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个蛮勇的骑手，会跳过汽车。
words.en: A daredevil is someone who enjoys doing dangerous things and taking risks.

words.ex: He imbibes coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol, or to absorb or take in something, such as knowledge or ideas.

words.ex: The sun is a bright luminary in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 太阳是天空中一个明亮的发光体。
words.en: A luminary is a person who is very famous and highly respected, especially in a particular field.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.ex: He gave a dolorous look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or appearance as dolorous, you mean that it is very sad and depressing.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: v. 豪饮；痛饮；开怀畅饮
words.ex: He quaffed the cold drink quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝下了那杯冷饮。
words.en: To drink (a beverage) heartily and with gusto.

words.ex: The team will oust the coach after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 球队在输球后将撤换教练。
words.en: If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

words.tr: adj. 骚乱的；喧闹的；热烈的
words.ex: The crowd was tumultuous during the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人群喧闹不安。
words.en: A tumultuous event or period of time involves many exciting and confusing events or feelings.

words.ex: He amended the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送信件之前修正了它。
words.en: To amend something means to make changes to it in order to improve it or make it more accurate.

words.ex: The king tried to subjugate the rebels.
words.ex_cn: 国王试图征服叛乱者。
words.en: To subjugate a country or group of people means to take complete control of them, especially by defeating them in a war.

words.ex: His mien showed calm and confidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的神情显得平静而自信。
words.en: A person's mien is their general appearance and manner, which might give you an idea of their character or mood.

words.ex: The dewy grass sparkled in the morning sun.
words.ex_cn: 带露水的草在晨光中闪闪发亮。
words.en: Something that is dewy is wet with dew or looks as if it is wet with dew.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；大方的； 豪爽的
words.ex: He is openhanded with his money, always helping friends.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨大方，总是帮助朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone as openhanded, you mean that they give generously or freely.

words.ex: The polestar guides sailors at night.
words.ex_cn: 北极星在夜晚为水手指路。
words.en: A polestar is a star that is used to guide someone, especially the North Star, which is used by sailors to navigate.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；勤苦工作的
words.ex: He is sedulous in practicing piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天勤奋地练习钢琴。
words.en: If you describe someone as sedulous, you mean that they work hard and pay great attention to detail.

words.ex: The cacophonous noise made her cover her ears.
words.ex_cn: 刺耳的噪音让她捂住了耳朵。
words.en: If you describe a mixture of sounds as cacophonous, you mean that they are loud and unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 感官的；肉欲的；愉悦感官的；耽于肉欲的
words.ex: The sensual smell of fresh bread made her hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的感官香味让她感到饥饿。
words.en: Relating to or involving gratification of the senses and physical, especially sexual, pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；安详的
words.ex: The lake is serene in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的湖面很宁静。
words.en: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled; tranquil.

words.tr: v. 故态复萌；退步；再犯
words.ex: He backslid into old habits after quitting smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他戒烟后又回到了旧习惯。
words.en: To revert to bad habits or undesirable activities after a period of improvement.

words.ex: The artist elongated the figure to create a sense of grace.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家拉长了人物形象，以创造出一种优雅的感觉。
words.en: To elongate something means to make it longer, especially by stretching it.

words.tr: adj. 使疲倦的；令人厌烦的；乏味的
words.ex: The wearisome task of filling out forms took hours.
words.ex_cn: 填写表格这项乏味的任务花了好几个小时。
words.en: If you describe something as wearisome, you mean that it is very tiring and boring or frustrating.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.ex: Some people believe in immortality after death.
words.ex_cn: 有些人相信死后会有永生。
words.en: The state of being able to live or last forever.

words.tr: n. 自命不凡的新上任者；狂妄自大的新手
words.ex: The upstart claimed he could run the company better than the founder.
words.ex_cn: 这个自命不凡的新上任者声称他比创始人更能管理公司。
words.en: An upstart is someone who has suddenly risen to a higher social or economic class and behaves in a way that is considered arrogant or presumptuous.

words.ex: The picture is fuzzy and hard to see.
words.ex_cn: 这张图片很模糊，看不清楚。
words.en: Something that is fuzzy is unclear or indistinct, often because it is out of focus or because it is covered with a soft, fluffy material.

words.tr: n. 权威人士；专家；评论员
words.ex: The pundit said the team will win tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这位专家说球队明天会赢。
words.en: A pundit is a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is often asked to give their opinions to the public.

words.tr: adj. 单一意思的；意义明确的
words.ex: The term 'univocal' is used to describe something that has a single, clear meaning.
words.ex_cn: 术语“univocal”用于描述具有单一、明确含义的事物。
words.en: Having only one possible meaning or interpretation.

words.tr:
v. 会谈；谈判
n. 会谈；谈判
words.ex: The two sides agreed to parley in order to resolve their differences.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意进行会谈以解决分歧。
words.en: A parley is a discussion between two opposing sides in a conflict, especially a discussion of terms for a truce.

words.ex: The team's loss was a total debacle.
words.ex_cn: 球队的失败是一场彻底的惨败。
words.en: A debacle is a sudden and complete failure or collapse, often in a way that is very embarrassing or causes a lot of damage.

words.tr: adj. 妄想狂的；有权力妄想的；自大狂的
words.ex: He made megalomaniacal plans to control the world.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了妄想狂般的计划来控制世界。

words.ex: He misinformed the crowd about the time.
words.ex_cn: 他告诉人群错误的时间。
words.en: To misinform someone means to give them false or inaccurate information.

words.ex: Washing hands can kill germs.
words.ex_cn: 洗手可以杀死病菌。
words.en: A germ is a very small organism that causes disease.

words.ex: The Pantheon is an ancient temple in Rome.
words.ex_cn: 万神庙是罗马的一座古代神庙。
words.en: A pantheon is a group of particularly respected, famous, or important people, or a temple dedicated to all the gods of a particular polytheistic religion.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；不骚动的；镇定的; v. 使平整；变得平静（unruffle 的过去分词）
words.ex: He remained unruffled during the loud argument.
words.ex_cn: 在激烈的争吵中，他依然镇定自若。
words.en: If someone is unruffled, they are calm and not upset or worried, even though they have had problems or have been treated badly.

words.tr: adj. 线性的；一维的；一度空间的
words.ex: The line is unidimensional.
words.ex_cn: 这条线是一维的。
words.en: Involving or having only one dimension.

words.ex: The cactus is prickly and hurts if you touch it.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌是多刺的，碰了会疼。
words.en: Something that is prickly feels as if it has a lot of small sharp points on it, or is covered with them. It can also describe someone who is easily annoyed or offended.

words.tr: adj. 多结节的；难以解决的；棘手的
words.ex: The old tree had a knotty trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有一个多结节的树干。
words.en: A knotty problem or issue is very complicated and difficult to solve.

words.ex: The use of tropes in literature can add depth and meaning to a story.
words.ex_cn: 在文学中使用修辞可以增加故事的深度和意义。
words.en: A trope is a word or expression used in a figurative sense; a figure of speech.

words.ex: The magic show riveted the children's attention.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们的注意力。
words.en: A rivet is a short metal pin or bolt for holding together two plates of metal, its headless end being beaten out or pressed down when in place. As a verb, to rivet means to attract and hold the attention of someone completely.

words.ex: He attests that the document is true.
words.ex_cn: 他证明这份文件是真实的。
words.en: To attest something means to declare or affirm that it is true or genuine, often in a formal or legal context.

words.ex: The city showed signs of decadence after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这座城市显示出衰败的迹象。
words.en: Decadence is a situation in which a society or institution is becoming less moral and less satisfactory.

words.ex: The police seized illicit drugs from the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察从嫌疑人那里没收了非法毒品。
words.en: Illicit activities or substances are not allowed by law or by social or religious custom.

words.tr:
n. 记数；
v. 合计；
words.ex: He kept a tally of how many goals he scored.
words.ex_cn: 他记录了自己进了多少球。
words.en: A tally is a record of amounts or numbers which you keep changing and adding to as the activity which affects it progresses.

words.ex: He made a pledge to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了帮助穷人的保证。
words.en: A pledge is a serious promise or agreement, especially one made publicly or officially. It can also refer to something given as security for the fulfillment of a contract or the payment of a debt.

words.tr:
n. 佯攻；虚击；假象
v. 佯攻；佯击；假装
words.ex: He made a feint to the left, then kicked right.
words.ex_cn: 他假装向左，然后右脚踢球。
words.en: A feint is a movement or an action that is intended to deceive someone, for example by making them think that you are going to do one thing when you are really going to do something else.

words.tr:
n. 手铐；脚镣；镣铐；束缚物
v. 给...戴上镣铐；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner wore iron shackle on his ankle.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯脚上戴着铁镣。
words.en: A shackle is a pair of metal rings connected by a chain which are fastened around someone's wrists or ankles in order to prevent them from moving or escaping.

words.ex: The colors intermingle in the painting.
words.ex_cn: 画中的颜色混合在一起。
words.en: If things intermingle, they mix together or are mixed together.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.ex: She is a bluestocking who loves reading books.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个热爱读书的女学者。
words.en: A bluestocking is an intellectual or literary woman.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.tr: adj. 群体的；社区的；公有的；
words.ex: They share a communal kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们共用一个群体厨房。
words.en: Communal means relating to or shared by all the members of a community.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.ex: The king vouchsafed a generous grant to the university.
words.ex_cn: 国王慷慨地赐予了大学一笔赠款。
words.en: If you vouchsafe something to someone, you give or tell it to them, especially in a gracious or condescending manner.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢而弯曲地流动；漫步；闲聊
n. 河流的曲折；漫步；迂回曲折的进程
words.ex: The river meanders through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河蜿蜒穿过森林。
words.en: To meander means to follow a winding and turning course, often used to describe the way a river flows or the way a person walks without a clear direction.

words.tr:
n. （古罗马的）贵族；名门望族；有教养的人；罗马帝国的地方官
adj. 贵族的；贵族似的；上流社会的
words.ex: She was born into a patrician family.
words.ex_cn: 她出生在一个贵族家庭。
words.en: A patrician is a person of high birth or noble status, especially in ancient Rome.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr: adj. 抒情诗般的；充满感情的；热情奔放的
words.ex: He sings a lyrical song about the sea.
words.ex_cn: 他唱了一首关于大海的抒情歌曲。
words.en: Lyrical means expressing the writer's emotions in an imaginative and beautiful way.

words.ex: There is strife between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有争执。
words.en: Strife is angry or violent conflict between two people or groups.

words.ex: The judge will adjudicate the dispute next week.
words.ex_cn: 法官将在下周裁决这场纠纷。
words.en: To adjudicate means to make an official decision about a problem or dispute.

words.ex: The machine is underutilized because few people know how to use it.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器使用不足，因为很少有人知道如何操作它。
words.en: If something is underutilized, it is not being used as much as it could be.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: His puerile jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puerile, you mean that they are silly and childish.

words.ex: He is proactive in solving problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决问题时很积极主动。
words.en: If you are proactive, you take action to make things happen rather than waiting for them to happen to you.

words.ex: He tried to retaliate by spreading rumors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过散布谣言来报复。
words.en: If you retaliate when someone harms or annoys you, you do something which harms or annoys them in return.

words.tr:
adj. 愤愤不平的；委屈的；受害的
v. 令委屈；令苦恼；侵害；“aggrieve”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She felt aggrieved by the unfair treatment she received.
words.ex_cn: 她因受到不公平的对待而感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you feel aggrieved, you feel upset and angry because you think that you have been treated unfairly.

words.ex: He sent a malicious email to hurt his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他发了一封怀恶意的邮件来伤害他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or actions as malicious, you mean that they are intended to harm people or their reputation, or to cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.ex: He expatiated on the importance of education.
words.ex_cn: 他详细阐述了教育的重要性。
words.en: To expatiate means to speak or write about something in great detail or at considerable length.

words.tr: n. 怜悯；悲情；哀婉；凄楚
words.ex: The movie filled us with pathos.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让我们充满感动。
words.en: Pathos is a quality in a work of art or literature that evokes feelings of pity or sadness.

words.tr:
n. 冰雹；
v. 把…誉为；
words.ex: The hail broke many car windows.
words.ex_cn: 冰雹打碎了许多汽车窗户。
words.en: Hail is small balls of ice that fall like rain from the sky. It can also mean to call out to someone in order to attract their attention, or to praise someone enthusiastically.

words.ex: The pastoral man tends his sheep on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧人在山上照看他的羊。
words.en: Relating to the countryside or to the work of a shepherd; idyllically rural.

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: The school's ethos is respect for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的社會精神特质是尊重每一个人。
words.en: The fundamental character or spirit of a culture; the underlying sentiment that informs the beliefs, customs, or practices of a group or society.

words.tr: adj. 玫瑰色的；红润的（皮肤）；美好的；有希望的（前途等）
words.ex: The sky turned rosy at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 日出时，天空变成了玫瑰色。
words.en: If you describe a situation as rosy, you mean that it seems to be full of hope and promise.

words.ex: He writes books under a pseudonym.
words.ex_cn: 他用笔名写书。
words.en: A pseudonym is a name that someone, especially a writer, uses instead of their real name.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr:
adj. 波西米亚人的；不受世俗陈规束缚的
n. 放荡不羁的人
words.ex: She adopted a bohemian lifestyle after quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 她辞职后过上了放荡不羁的生活。
words.en: A bohemian is someone who lives in a very informal and relaxed way and does not accept society's rules of behavior. The term is often used to describe artists, writers, and musicians who live in this manner.

words.tr: adj. 无敌的；无比的；至高无上的
words.ex: Her talent is unrivaled in the music industry.
words.ex_cn: 她的才华在音乐界是无与伦比的。
words.en: Having no rival or equal; incomparable.

words.ex: She invited all her kinfolk to the family reunion.
words.ex_cn: 她邀请了所有的亲属参加家庭团聚。
words.en: Your relatives; your family.

words.ex: The police helped to defuse the situation.
words.ex_cn: 警察帮助减少了危险。
words.en: To remove the fuse from (an explosive device) in order to prevent it from exploding; to reduce the danger or tension in (a situation).

words.ex: The upshot of the meeting was a new plan.
words.ex_cn: 会议的结果是一个新计划。
words.en: The final result or outcome of a situation or event.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使糊涂；胡乱应付
n. 混乱；糊涂
words.ex: He muddled the instructions and got confused.
words.ex_cn: 他把说明搞混了，感到困惑。
words.en: If you muddle things or people, you get them mixed up, so that you do not know which is which.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.tr: n. 庸医的医术；骗子的行为
words.ex: The medical community warns against the dangers of quackery.
words.ex_cn: 医疗界警告人们警惕庸医术的危险。
words.en: The practice of dishonest methods or false claims in order to gain money, especially in medicine.

words.ex: The whisper was barely audible.
words.ex_cn: 那耳语几乎听不见。
words.en: If a sound is audible, it is loud enough for you to hear it.

words.tr: adj. 无限的；不受控制的
words.ex: His generosity was unbounded, always willing to help those in need.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨是无边的，总是愿意帮助那些需要帮助的人。
words.en: If you describe something as unbounded, you mean that it has, or seems to have, no limits.

words.ex: He always follows the maxim 'work hard, play hard'.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵循‘努力工作，尽情玩耍’这一信条。
words.en: A maxim is a short, easily remembered expression of a basic principle, general truth, or rule of conduct.

words.ex: The insurance company agreed to indemnify the victims for their losses.
words.ex_cn: 保险公司同意赔偿受害者的损失。
words.en: To indemnify someone means to compensate them for harm or loss they have suffered.

words.ex: The storm unleashed heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 风暴释放出大雨。
words.en: If you say that someone or something unleashes a powerful force, feeling, activity, or group, you mean that they suddenly start it or send it to move somewhere.

words.tr: adj. 残暴的；恶劣的；糟透的
words.ex: The dictator committed atrocious acts against his people.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者对人民犯下了残暴的罪行。
words.en: If you describe something as atrocious, you are emphasizing that its quality is very bad.

words.tr:
adj. （《圣经》中所说的大洪水前的）古老的；过时的
n.  年迈的人；不合时宜的人
words.ex: He uses an antediluvian typewriter to write letters.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台远古的打字机写信。
words.en: Belonging to the time before the biblical Flood; very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: He gave a stellar performance in the play.
words.ex_cn: 他在剧中表现出色。
words.en: Of or relating to stars; outstanding or excellent.

words.tr:
n. 先锋；前锋；先头部队
v. 做…的先锋；带头做；领先突击
words.ex: She is the spearhead of the new environmental project.
words.ex_cn: 她是这项新环保项目的先锋。
words.en: To spearhead something means to lead it or to be the person who starts it.

words.tr: adj. 氏族的；宗族排外的；团结心很强的
words.ex: The community was very clannish and outsiders found it hard to integrate.
words.ex_cn: 这个社区非常排外，外来者发现很难融入。
words.en: If you describe a group of people or their behavior as clannish, you mean that they often spend time together and seem unfriendly towards people who are not in the group.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.ex: The farmer tried to kill the pest with a spray.
words.ex_cn: 农民试图用喷雾杀死害虫。
words.en: A pest is an animal or insect that damages crops, food, or livestock, or is generally troublesome. It can also refer to a person or thing that causes annoyance or trouble.

words.ex: The entrance to the building is on the left.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的入口在左边。
words.en: An entrance is a way into a place, such as a door or gate. It can also refer to the act of entering a place or the right to enter.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

words.tr: n. 田园风景；田园生活；田园诗
words.ex: The small village was the perfect setting for an idyll.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄是田园诗的完美背景。
words.en: An idyll is a short poem or piece of prose that describes a peaceful or romantic scene, especially of rural life.

words.tr: adj. 庞大的；笨拙的；似象一样的
words.ex: The elephantine statue stood in the park.
words.ex_cn: 那座巨大的雕像矗立在公园里。
words.en: If you describe something as elephantine, you mean that you think it is large and awkward.

words.ex: He added an addendum to the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在合同后加了一个附录。
words.en: An addendum is an additional section at the end of a book or document that provides further information or corrections.

words.ex: He expostulate with his friend about the unfair rule.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友抱怨这条不公平的规则。
words.en: To expostulate means to reason earnestly with someone in an attempt to dissuade or correct them.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

words.ex: He is frugal with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很节俭。
words.en: If you describe someone as frugal, you mean that they are careful about spending money and use things only when they need to.

words.ex: He is an equable man who never gets angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个性情恬静的人，从不生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as equable, you mean that they are calm, cheerful, and fair with other people, even in difficult circumstances.

words.tr:
n. 划分；隔离物；分割
v. 分开；隔开
words.ex: The partition of the room made it more private.
words.ex_cn: 房间的隔断让它更私密了。
words.en: A partition is a wall, screen, or divider that separates one part of a room, vehicle, or other space from another.

words.ex: He read a compendium of math rules.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本数学规则的汇编。
words.en: A compendium is a short but complete collection of information, usually in a book.

words.tr: adj. 虚拟的；几乎的；实际上的；事实上的；
words.ex: He played a virtual game on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他在电脑上玩了一个虚拟游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as virtual, you mean that it is so nearly true that for most purposes it can be regarded as true.

words.tr: v. 使石化；使僵化；吓呆
words.ex: The lightning petrified the tree into stone.
words.ex_cn: 闪电把树变成了石头。
words.en: To petrify means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.

words.tr: v. 笨拙地弄糟；笨手笨脚地走动；语无伦次
words.ex: He bumbled the presentation and forgot his lines.
words.ex_cn: 他笨拙地搞砸了演讲，忘记了台词。
words.en: To bumble is to move or act in an awkward or confused manner, often making mistakes or being inefficient.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.tr: adj. 能笑的；爱笑的；可笑的；滑稽的
words.ex: His funny hat made everyone laugh; it was risible.
words.ex_cn: 他的搞笑帽子让每个人都笑了；这太可笑了。
words.en: If you describe something as risible, you mean that it is so silly that it makes you laugh.

words.tr: v. 使预先有倾向；使易接受；使易于患（病）
words.ex: Genes can predispose a person to diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 基因可能使人更容易患糖尿病。
words.en: If something predisposes you to think or behave in a particular way, it makes it likely that you will think or behave in that way.

words.tr: n. 易被劝服的人；容易做的事情
words.ex: He was a pushover in the negotiations, easily agreeing to all their demands.
words.ex_cn: 他在谈判中是个容易对付的人，轻易同意了他们所有的要求。
words.en: A pushover is someone who is easily defeated or influenced.

words.tr: adj. 宽松的；容积大的；部头大的；卷数多的
words.ex: She wore a voluminous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条宽松的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is voluminous is very large or contains a lot of things.

words.ex: He antedated the contract by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他把合同的日期提前了一周。
words.en: To be of an earlier date than something else; to precede in time.

words.ex: The court will quash the false order.
words.ex_cn: 法院将撤销这个虚假的命令。
words.en: If a court or someone in authority quashes a decision or judgment, they officially reject it and say that it is not valid.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.ex: He took a circuitous route to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他绕了远路以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A circuitous route, journey, or piece of writing is longer than it needs to be because it is not direct.

words.ex: The company decided to outsource its customer service.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司决定将客户服务外购。
words.en: If a company outsources work or things, it pays workers from outside the company to do the work or supply the things.

words.ex: The land is arable and good for growing wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这块地是可耕的，适合种植小麦。
words.en: Arable land is land that is suitable for growing crops.

words.tr: adj. 美丽的；漂亮的；具有美感的
words.ex: The pulchritudinous sunset filled the sky with color.
words.ex_cn: 美丽的日落让天空充满了色彩。

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.ex: His comportment at the meeting was very polite.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的举止非常礼貌。
words.en: The way in which someone behaves or conducts themselves.

words.ex: The loud noise stunned him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他震惊了。
words.en: To stun someone means to shock or surprise them very much.

words.ex: He ate too much and his stomach hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，胃疼。
words.en: The stomach is the organ in your body where food is digested after you have eaten it.

words.ex: He gave a jeremiad about the bad weather.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨了糟糕的天气。
words.en: A jeremiad is a long, mournful complaint or lamentation; a list of woes.

words.tr: adj. 浑浊的；污浊不清的；
words.ex: The river water looks turbid after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后河水看起来浑浊。
words.en: If you describe something as turbid, you mean that it is cloudy, dirty, or muddy.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.tr: v. 从盲区袭击；使措手不及
words.ex: The defender was blindside by a fast pass.
words.ex_cn: 防守球员被一个快速传球从侧面偷袭了。
words.en: To blindside someone means to surprise them by doing something they did not expect, often causing them problems.

words.tr:
n. 枯萎；凋谢；憔悴；
v. 枯萎；凋谢；憔悴；
words.ex: The flowers showed signs of wilt after the long heat.
words.ex_cn: 这些花在长时间高温后出现了枯萎的迹象。
words.en: If a plant wilts, it bends over because it is too dry, too hot, or too weak to stay upright.

words.tr: v. 使安静；安慰；使缓和
words.ex: She sang a song to soothe the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她唱了一首歌来安抚婴儿。
words.en: To soothe someone means to make them feel calmer and less anxious, upset, or angry.

words.tr: n. 重型卡车；不可抗拒的强大力量；无法控制的强大机构；使人盲目牺牲（或崇拜）的事物
words.ex: The juggernaut rolled down the highway, carrying heavy cargo.
words.ex_cn: 这辆重型卡车沿着高速公路行驶，载着沉重的货物。
words.en: A juggernaut is something or someone that is extremely large, powerful, and unstoppable.

words.tr: adj. 内在的；无所不在的
words.ex: The immanent laws of nature govern all living things.
words.ex_cn: 自然界的内在法则支配着所有生物。
words.en: Existing or operating within; inherent.

words.tr:
v. 完成；使完美；圆房
adj. 完美的；至上的；圆满的
words.ex: He consummated the deal with a handshake.
words.ex_cn: 他用握手完成了这笔交易。
words.en: To consummate means to make something complete or perfect, often used in the context of a marriage or an agreement. It can also describe someone who is extremely skilled in a particular area.

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.ex: Bears are omnivorous animals.
words.ex_cn: 熊是杂食动物。
words.en: An omnivorous animal or person eats both plants and meat.

words.tr:
n. 缰绳；驾驭；控制
v. 控制；驾驭
words.ex: He uses a leather rein to control the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他用皮缰绳来控制马。
words.en: A rein is a long, narrow strap attached at one end to a horse's bit, typically used in pairs to guide or check a horse while riding or driving.

words.ex: The gods foreordain his fate.
words.ex_cn: 神早已注定他的命运。
words.en: To decide or determine (something) beforehand; to predestine.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.tr: n. 还击；机敏的回答; vi. 回击；机敏地回答
words.ex: He delivered a clever riposte to her accusation.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的指控给出了机智的回应。
words.en: A riposte is a quick and clever reply to an insult or criticism, or a quick return thrust in fencing.

words.ex: He burst into rage when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他勃然大怒。
words.en: Rage is a feeling of intense anger that is difficult to control.

words.ex: The workers load stones from the quarry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从采石场装载石头。
words.en: A quarry is a place where stone, sand, etc., is dug out of the ground. It can also refer to an animal or person that is being hunted or chased.

words.ex: The lion showed ferocity when it hunted.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在捕猎时表现出凶猛。
words.en: Ferocity refers to the state or quality of being ferocious, which means savagely fierce, cruel, or violent.

words.ex: He is a fiery man who gets angry easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个容易发怒的暴躁男人。
words.en: If you describe something as fiery, you mean that it is burning strongly or contains fire. It can also describe someone's temper or speech as being very passionate or intense.

words.ex: Strong foundations underpin the building.
words.ex_cn: 坚固的地基支撑着这栋建筑。
words.en: To support, strengthen, or provide a foundation for something.

words.tr: adj. 丑恶的；可怕的；丑陋的；
words.ex: The monster had a hideous face.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物有一张丑恶的脸。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is hideous, you mean that they are very ugly or unattractive.

words.tr: v. 狂吃暴饮；大吃大喝；大量消耗
words.ex: He guzzles soda every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都大口喝苏打水。
words.en: If you guzzle something, you drink it quickly and greedily.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；红的；淡红色
words.ex: Her complexion was ruddy from the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的脸色因寒冷的天气而变得红润。
words.en: Having a healthy red color, especially in the face.

words.tr:
n. 艰辛；艰苦劳动；痛苦；分娩的阵痛
v. 辛苦工作；发生或经受阵痛
words.ex: His travail helped him succeed in the end.
words.ex_cn: 他的艰辛最终让他取得了成功。
words.en: Travail refers to painful or laborious effort, especially in the context of work or childbirth.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.tr:
n. 溃败；溃退
v. 彻底击败；使溃败；用鼻子拱土
words.ex: The team rout the opponents last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚这支队伍大胜对手。
words.en: A disorderly retreat or defeat, especially of an army; a chaotic flight from conflict.

words.tr: n. 挥霍无度的人；败家子
words.ex: He was criticized for being a wastrel with his inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他因挥霍继承的财产而受到批评。
words.en: A wastrel is someone who wastes their time, money, or resources in a careless or irresponsible way.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.ex: The duplication of the document cost five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件的复制花了五美元。
words.en: the act or process of making an exact copy of something

words.tr: v. 以甜言蜜语哄骗；勾引
words.ex: He tried to cajole his sister into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗妹妹把钱借给他。
words.en: If you cajole someone into doing something, you persuade them to do it by flattery or by making promises.

words.tr: v. 浸入水中；泼上水；熄灭
words.ex: He doused the burning log in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把燃烧的木头浸入水中。
words.en: To douse something means to quickly throw water over it in order to put out a fire, or to pour a lot of liquid over it.

words.ex: The manager oversees the team's daily work.
words.ex_cn: 经理监督团队的日常工作。
words.en: To oversee means to watch and direct a piece of work, the people doing it, or the way it is done in order to ensure that it is done correctly.

words.tr: adj. 可伸缩的；可扩展的
words.ex: The app is scalable for more users.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用程序可以为更多用户扩展。
words.en: Capable of being expanded or adapted easily to handle growth or increased demand.

words.tr: n. 爱占便宜的人；不劳而获者
words.ex: He's always borrowing money and never pays it back; he's such a freeloader.
words.ex_cn: 他老是借钱从不还；他真是个爱占便宜的人。
words.en: A freeloader is someone who takes advantage of others' generosity without giving anything in return.

words.ex: The hallmark of a good teacher is patience.
words.ex_cn: 好老师的标志是耐心。
words.en: A hallmark is a distinctive characteristic or attribute that is typical of a particular person or thing.

words.ex: The monster made a monstrous sound.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物发出了巨大的声音。
words.en: If you describe something as monstrous, you mean that it is extremely large or that it is extremely unpleasant or wrong.

words.ex: The students roistered through the streets after the football victory.
words.ex_cn: 足球胜利后，学生们在大街上狂欢。
words.en: To engage in noisy, boisterous, or drunken revelry.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.ex: He made a gaffe when he called the boss by the wrong name.
words.ex_cn: 他叫错老板的名字，犯了个错误。
words.en: A gaffe is a mistake that a person makes in public, especially something embarrassing that they say or do.

words.tr: v. 规定价格；稳定物价
words.ex: The government will valorize the price of wheat next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将规定小麦的价格。
words.en: To valorize something means to give or establish its value, especially by government action or intervention.

words.tr: v. 拨弄；玩弄；篡改；收买
words.ex: Don't tamper with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 不要拨弄这台机器。
words.en: If someone tampers with something, they interfere with it or make unauthorized changes to it, often in order to cause damage or make it work differently.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；爱吵架的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: The cantankerous old man yells at his neighbors every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那位脾气暴躁的老人每天早上都对邻居大喊大叫。
words.en: Someone who is cantankerous is bad-tempered and quarrels with people.

words.ex: A small fissure appeared in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上出现了一道小裂缝。
words.en: A fissure is a long, narrow opening or line of breakage made by cracking or splitting, especially in rock or earth.

words.ex: The teacher gave an assessment of the students' work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作品进行了评估。
words.en: An assessment is a judgment about something, especially about how good or bad it is, or an amount that is calculated for something, especially for tax purposes.

words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.ex: The queen was resplendent in her golden crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着金色王冠，光彩夺目。
words.en: Something that is resplendent is very bright and attractive, often because it is richly decorated or very colorful.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；超自然的；难以解释的
words.ex: The psychic claimed to have preternatural abilities.
words.ex_cn: 这位通灵者声称自己拥有超自然的能力。
words.en: Beyond what is normal or natural; supernatural.

words.tr:
adj. 先锋的；前卫的
n. 先锋派；前卫
words.ex: The artist uses avant-garde styles in her paintings.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家在她的画作中使用前卫的风格。
words.en: Avant-garde is used to describe people or works that are experimental or innovative, particularly in the arts.

words.tr: adj. 闪烁的；轻轻摇曳的；柔和的
words.ex: The lambent flames of the candle created a cozy atmosphere in the room.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛闪烁的火焰在房间里营造了一个舒适的氛围。
words.en: Softly bright or radiant; flickering lightly over a surface.

words.ex: He believes in fatalism and does not try to change his fate.
words.ex_cn: 他相信宿命论，不愿改变自己的命运。
words.en: Fatalism is the belief that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.

words.tr:
n. 诡计；花言巧语
v. 欺骗；诱骗；消磨
words.ex: He used a clever wile to deceive his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个巧妙的诡计来欺骗他的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone uses wiles to achieve something, you mean that they use clever methods to persuade people to do what they want.

words.ex: She wore a white veil on her wedding day.
words.ex_cn: 她在婚礼那天戴了一条白色的面纱。
words.en: A veil is a piece of thin soft cloth that women sometimes wear over their heads and which can also cover their face.

words.tr: n. 家谱学；系谱学；宗谱学；家谱（图）
words.ex: He is learning his family genealogy.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习自己的家族家谱。
words.en: Genealogy is the study of the history of families and the line of descent from their ancestors.

words.tr:
v. 回火；适得其反
n. 逆火
words.ex: The engine backfired when he pressed the gas pedal.
words.ex_cn: 当他踩下油门时，发动机回火了。
words.en: If a plan or project backfires, it has the opposite result to the one that was intended.

words.tr: n. 废弃物（树枝、碎石等）；
words.ex: The workers cleared the brash from the construction site.
words.ex_cn: 工人们清除了建筑工地上的废弃物。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as brash, you disapprove of them because you think that they are too confident and aggressive.

words.tr:
n. 试验；化验；定量分析
v. 试验；化验；定量分析
words.ex: The lab will assay the blood sample tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实验室明天将检测这个血液样本。
words.en: An assay is a test to determine the presence, absence, or quantity of one or more components.

words.tr: adj. 过于急切的；过于热心的
words.ex: He was overeager to help and broke the vase.
words.ex_cn: 他太急于帮忙，结果打碎了花瓶。

words.tr:
v. 移居国外；把…逐出国外
n. 侨民；移居国外者
adj. 移居国外的；被逐出国外的
words.ex: He decided to expatriate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他决定移居加拿大以追求更好的生活。
words.en: An expatriate is someone who lives in a country that is not their own, often for work or political reasons.

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.tr:
n. 发酵；酵素；动乱
v. （使）发酵；动乱
words.ex: The ferment of yeast makes bread rise.
words.ex_cn: 酵母的发酵使面包膨胀。
words.en: If a substance ferments or if it is fermented, it changes chemically because of the action of yeast or bacteria, often producing alcohol.

words.ex: The stomach digests food into nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 胃将食物消化成营养物质。
words.en: To digest means to break down food in the stomach and intestines into substances that can be absorbed by the body. It can also mean to understand or assimilate information. As a noun, it refers to a compilation or summary of information.

words.ex: He caught a big carp in the river.
words.ex_cn: 他在河里钓到了一条大鲤鱼。
words.en: To complain or find fault continually, typically about trivial matters.

words.tr: n. 传闻；谣传；道听途说
words.ex: He believed the hearsay without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就相信了这些流言。
words.en: Information received from other people that one cannot adequately substantiate; rumor.

words.tr: v. 求爱；求婚；寻求支持
words.ex: He tried to woo her with flowers and chocolates.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和巧克力追求她。
words.en: If you woo someone, you try to persuade them to marry you or to have a relationship with you, or you try to gain their support or favor.

words.tr: adj. 有狂风暴雨的；狂暴的
words.ex: The tempestuous sea made the voyage dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨的海面使得航行变得危险。
words.en: If you describe a relationship or a situation as tempestuous, you mean that it is full of strong emotions, especially anger or passion.

words.ex: He bought a stake in the new company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了这家新公司的股份。
words.en: A stake is a pointed stick or post that is pushed into the ground, for example to support a young tree. It can also refer to a share or interest in a business, situation, or system.

words.tr: n.  欺骗；作假；使诈；诡计
words.ex: The company was involved in various acts of skullduggery to gain an unfair advantage.
words.ex_cn: 该公司为了获得不公平的优势，参与了各种欺骗行为。
words.en: Underhanded or unscrupulous behavior; trickery.

words.ex: The garden was in a state of plenitude, with flowers blooming everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 花园里繁花似锦，处处充满生机。
words.en: The state of being full or complete; abundance.

words.ex: He tried to counterfeit money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图伪造货币。
words.en: Made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.ex: He gave a spiteful look when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛时投来一个恶毒的眼神。
words.en: If you say that someone is spiteful, you mean that they deliberately want to upset or hurt someone, often in a small way, because they feel angry towards them.

words.ex: The Fed chairman is dovish about raising interest rates.
words.ex_cn: 美联储主席对加息持温和态度。
words.en: If you describe someone in politics as dovish, you mean that they favour the use of diplomacy and negotiation to solve problems rather than the use of force or violence.

words.tr:
n. 栖枝；鲈鱼；
v. 栖息；处于（高处）；
words.ex: The bird sat on a perch near the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟停在树旁的一根栖枝上。
words.en: A perch is a branch or rod where a bird rests or a high position where someone or something is located. As a verb, it means to rest or be located in a high position.

words.ex: He called the speech pure flummery.
words.ex_cn: 他称这番演讲纯粹是空话。
words.en: Flummery refers to meaningless flattery or compliments that are insincere, or something that is superficial and lacks substance.

words.ex: The two lines intersect at point A.
words.ex_cn: 两条线在点A相交。
words.en: If two or more lines or roads intersect, they meet or cross each other.

words.tr:
n. 拙劣的模仿（作品）
v. 拙劣模仿
words.ex: The film is a parody of classic horror movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对经典恐怖电影的滑稽模仿。
words.en: A parody is a humorous or satirical imitation of a serious piece of literature or writing.

words.ex: His genius is indubitable.
words.ex_cn: 他的天才是不容置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something as indubitable, you mean that it is definitely true.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.ex: His comments about her appearance really riled her.
words.ex_cn: 他对她外貌的评论真的激怒了她。
words.en: To make someone annoyed or irritated.

words.tr:
v. 重新洗牌；改组
n. 改组；重新安排
words.ex: The coach will reshuffle the team for the next game.
words.ex_cn: 教练将为下一场比赛重新调整阵容。
words.en: to change the positions of people or things within a group, especially in order to improve the way it works

words.tr:
v. （使）合并；（使）融合；（使）混合
n. 合并；混合
words.ex: He melds the two ideas into one.
words.ex_cn: 他把这两个想法融合成一个。
words.en: To combine or blend to form a single entity.

words.tr: adj. 阈限的；处于过渡状态的
words.ex: He felt liminal between childhood and adulthood.
words.ex_cn: 他感觉自己处于童年和成年之间的过渡状态。
words.en: Relating to a transitional or initial stage of a process; occupying a position at, or on both sides of, a boundary or threshold.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.ex: The painting shows surrealism with floating clocks.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画用漂浮的钟表表现超现实主义。
words.en: A 20th-century avant-garde movement in art and literature which sought to release the creative potential of the unconscious mind, for example by the irrational juxtaposition of images.
